docs.title: Velero Truncated ZFS Backup Objects — Netcat Idle Timeout
Summary
docs.text:
Every scheduled Velero backup since 2026-10-13 is PartiallyFailed with 0 successes. The node-side pipeline zfs send -i <prev> <snap> | nc -w 3 <velero-pod-ip> 9011 uses OpenBSD netcat's -w 3 idle timeout. When the receiver stops draining the socket for >=3s (e.g., during S3 multipart upload backpressure), nc exits 0, zfs send dies with SIGPIPE (exit status 141), and the clouduploader receiver in openebs/velero-plugin:3.6.0 treats the EOF as success and uploads a partial object while logging successfully uploaded object. Truncated objects have DRR_BEGIN=1, DRR_END=0 when inspected with zstream dump.

Last known-good backup: retain-quaterly-20261006023052 (Oct 6, phase Completed). Its whole incremental chain is structurally complete: Oct 6 → Sep 29 → Sep 28, and for 30 of 32 volumes further back through Sep 26 → Aug 25 → Aug 18 → Aug 11. All verified DRR_END=1.

Time-critical: retain-quaterly-20260811023053 is the chain ROOT for at least one volume and expires 2026-11-09. With incrBackupCount: 11 a full arrives every 12 runs; on a weekly schedule that is 84 days against a 2160h (90-day) TTL — about 6 days of margin, and that margin only holds if every scheduled run succeeds. The Oct 13 – Nov 4 failures consumed it: no run succeeded, so no replacement full was ever produced, and the Aug 11 root aged out on schedule. This is a latent design flaw, independent of the nc bug.

docs.title: Symptom and Detection Signature
docs.text:
• Velero backups are PartiallyFailed with errors like: 
    error taking snapshot of volume: rpc error: code = Unknown desc =
  zfs: error in uploading snapshot, status:{Failed}
  • Node agent logs show: 
    zfs: could not backup <vol> snap <snap> bkpname <name>
  cmd [zfs send -i <prevsnap> <cursnap>] | [nc -w 3 <receiver-ip> 9011]
  error: ... pipe source [...]: exit status 141
    (SIGPIPE = 128 + 13)
  • Velero plugin (receiver) logs show, for the same transfer: 
    Transfer done.. closing the server
successfully uploaded object{...}
  • S3 objects are present but structurally incomplete: zstream dump shows DRR_BEGIN=1 but DRR_END=0 (missing end record).

Why this is dangerous: The sender (exit status 141), the receiver (successfully uploaded object) and the backup metadata disagree about the same transfer. The receiver logging success is why the truncation is silent — the object lands in S3 and looks complete unless you inspect its stream structure.

docs.title: Detection Recipe
docs.text:
# List recent backups and their phase
kubectl --context=grigri -n velero get backups --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -20

# Check ZFSBackup CRs for Failed or missing Done status
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get zb \
  -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,VOLUME:.spec.volumeName,STATUS:.status,PREV:.spec.prevSnapName'

# Node agent logs for SIGPIPE
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv logs -l app=openebs-zfs-node --tail=500 | grep -E 'exit status 141|pipe source'

# Velero plugin logs for "successfully uploaded object" on small objects
kubectl --context=grigri -n velero logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=velero --tail=500 | grep 'successfully uploaded object'

Note: kubectl logs only covers the current container lifetime. The node pods restarted ~16h before the last failing run (2026-11-04 03:30), so the commands above may return nothing for older runs. Loki (retention begins ~2026-10-06) is the place to look for older failures:

{job="systemd-journal", node_name=~".+"} |~ "exit status 141|pipe source"

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text: The OpenEBS ZFS driver v2.11.2 runs the backup pipeline as zfs send -i <prev> <snap> | nc -w 3 <velero-pod-ip> 9011. The -w 3 is an idle timeout: if no data flows through the socket for 3 seconds, nc exits 0. The receiver (Velero plugin's clouduploader) closes its object writer when the client disconnects, even if the ZFS stream is incomplete. The plugin polls ZFSBackup.status and treats the uploaded object as success, logging successfully uploaded object.

docs.title: Per-Version Behavior
docs.text:
Version Behavior Exit Code Notes <=2.10.1 Masks truncation 0 Runs pipeline as bash -c "zfs send \| nc" without pipefail, so sender's SIGPIPE is lost and truncated objects are reported as success. Do not downgrade to this version — it hides the bug. 2.11.0–2.11.1 Hangs in Init N/A runPipe waits for zfs send before nc, so if nc exits early, zfs send blocks on its pipe indefinitely. ZFSBackup stays Init. See velero-zfs-stream-pipeline-deadlock.md. 2.11.2 Reports Failed 141 runPipe waits for both children concurrently and joins exit errors. Sender's SIGPIPE is detected and reported. This is the first version that surfaces the bug visibly.

Upstream issue: openebs/zfs-localpv#773 (reopened).

Fix: Branch fix/configurable-netcat-timeout (commit 28f9f96) on pando85/zfs-localpv adds env var ZFS_NETCAT_TIMEOUT, default 300s, applied to both buildVolumeBackupArgs and buildVolumeRestoreArgs. It cherry-picks cleanly onto tag v2.11.2. The fix image is published at ghcr.io/pando85/zfs-driver:2.11.2-nc-timeout (digest sha256:c6a677d4665524408fe8de8e278ead3cb68419853d57200f4485332cc13fb02c, linux/amd64) — see Recovery Procedure step (a).

docs.title: Verification Recipe: zstream dump
docs.text: WARNING: zfs send -nvP size comparison is unreliable below a few MB. We measured a 6.7x overshoot on a complete 624-byte object, and three false-positive "truncations" on sub-2 MB streams. Use zstream dump to count DRR_BEGIN/DRR_END records instead.

docs.title: Structural Verification
docs.text:
# List objects for a specific volume in a backup (the middle component is not trivially
# reconstructable from the volume name alone, so list and grep rather than construct the key).
# Every stream object has a .zfsvol sibling (~1.7 KB metadata), so filter it out or you will
# try to zstream dump the metadata file.
# Retrieve credentials from pass or Vault, not CLI args.
# aws --endpoint-url=https://s3.internal.grigri.cloud --profile velero \
#   s3 ls s3://velero/backups/<backup-name>/ | grep <volume-name> | grep -v '\.zfsvol$'

# Download the stream object
# aws --endpoint-url=https://s3.internal.grigri.cloud --profile velero \
#   s3 cp s3://velero/backups/<backup-name>/<object-key> /tmp/<volume>.zfs

# Count DRR records
zstream dump /tmp/<volume>.zfs | grep -c '^DRR_BEGIN'  # Should be 1
zstream dump /tmp/<volume>.zfs | grep -c '^DRR_END'    # Should be 1 for complete, 0 for truncated

# A complete stream has DRR_BEGIN=1, DRR_END=1.
# A truncated stream has DRR_BEGIN=1, DRR_END=0.

Object key layout: The VSL prefix: zfs does not create a zfs/ directory — it prefixes the object names inside the per-backup directory. The bucket root has only backups/ and restores/. The real key format is:

s3://velero/backups/<backup-name>/zfs-…-<volume-name>-<backup-name>          # ZFS send stream
s3://velero/backups/<backup-name>/zfs-…-<volume-name>-<backup-name>.zfsvol   # ~1.7 KB metadata

Example real key: zfs-retain-quaterly-antdroid-data-retain-quaterly-20261006023052.

docs.title: Size Comparison (Unreliable for Small Streams)
docs.text:
# Estimate the expected size (unreliable < 2 MB)
ssh <node> 'zfs send -nvP -i <prev-snap> <snap>'

# Compare with the object size in S3 (list and grep, do not construct the key)
# aws --endpoint-url=https://s3.internal.grigri.cloud --profile velero \
#   s3 ls s3://velero/backups/<backup-name>/ | grep <volume-name>

For small volumes (< 2 MB), the estimate can overshoot by 6x or more. Do not use size comparison alone to declare truncation; use zstream dump for structural verification.

docs.title: Recovery Procedure
docs.text:
All mutating commands are marked [MUTATING]. The owner should review and execute these steps manually.

The velero CLI is installed at /usr/bin/velero. Every velero invocation below carries --kubecontext grigri -n velero.

docs.title: Step (a): Prerequisite — the Fix Image
docs.text:
The fix image is already built and published. No local build or manual push is required.

  • Image: ghcr.io/pando85/zfs-driver:2.11.2-nc-timeout
  • Digest: sha256:c6a677d4665524408fe8de8e278ead3cb68419853d57200f4485332cc13fb02c
  • Platform: linux/amd64, 5 layers, OCI manifest (application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json). All three cluster nodes are amd64, so single-arch is sufficient.
  • Public and anonymously pullable: an anonymous manifest GET returns HTTP 200. The cluster needs no imagePullSecret — this is why the values.yaml pin works as-is.
  • Patch verified in the published artifact: extracting /usr/local/bin/zfs-driver (76,371,717 bytes) from the pulled image and grepping finds ZFS_NETCAT_TIMEOUT and netCatTimeout. The workflow performs this check as a post-push step and fails the run if the string is absent, so a silently unpatched image cannot be published.
  • Source: upstream tag v2.11.2 (24bbd89) plus commit 7bb8c18 (fix(backup): make the netcat idle timeout configurable), which is a clean cherry-pick of 28f9f96 from branch fix/configurable-netcat-timeout.
  • Compiled default: ZFS_NETCAT_TIMEOUT defaults to 300s when the env var is unset. The chart exposes no env hook for the node plugin container, so the compiled default is what applies.

How it was built: Workflow Fork image build at .github/workflows/fork-build-push.yml in pando85/zfs-localpv, on branch fork/2.11.2-nc-timeout, run 41893612196 (conclusion success).

How to rebuild: Push any fork/** branch to the fork, or trigger the workflow manually via workflow_dispatch with the image_tag input (default 2.11.2-nc-timeout). The tag is derived from the branch name with the fork/ prefix stripped. Do not derive it from deploy/helm/charts/Chart.yaml — at tag v2.11.2 that file reads version: 2.11.2-prerelease, which would produce the wrong tag.

CI credential requirement: GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push to ghcr.io/pando85/* from this repository because it is a fork; the push fails with denied: permission_denied: write_package. This was diagnosed empirically — repo Actions is enabled, repo workflow permissions are write, the workflow declares permissions: packages: write, the package pre-existed, was public and was linked to the repo, and both plain docker push and buildx push failed identically, which ruled out credential plumbing. Adding the org.opencontainers.image.source label did not fix it either. The workflow therefore authenticates with the repository secret GHCR_PAT (a classic PAT with write:packages). GitHub's Container registry docs state that GHCR only supports authentication with a classic PAT — fine-grained PATs do not work.

Leftover bootstrap tag: During package bootstrapping, an alpine:3.23.5 image was pushed as tag _bootstrap purely to create the GHCR package and make it public. It is not a driver image and must not be used. It still exists and should be deleted from the package settings UI; the available token lacks delete:packages, so it cannot be removed via API. Hazard: pulling ghcr.io/pando85/zfs-driver:_bootstrap yields an Alpine shell, not a CSI driver.

docs.title: Step (b): Let ArgoCD Sync the Pinned Image
docs.text:
The chart change in this commit pins zfsPlugin.image to ghcr.io/pando85/zfs-driver:2.11.2-nc-timeout. ArgoCD will sync the new image automatically.

# Verify the sync — confirm the DaemonSet pods are running the fork image
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get pods -o wide

# Check the running container image (the openebs-zfs-plugin container, not the sidecar)
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get pods -l app=openebs-zfs-node \
  -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName}{"\t"}{.spec.containers[?(@.name=="openebs-zfs-plugin")].image}{"\n"}{end}'

docs.title: Step (c): Verify the Running Image and Behaviour
docs.text:
# Confirm the fork image is running (image tag must be 2.11.2-nc-timeout)
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get pods -l app=openebs-zfs-node \
  -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.spec.nodeName}{"\t"}{.spec.containers[?(@.name=="openebs-zfs-plugin")].image}{"\n"}{end}'

# The fork image uses a compiled default of 300s for ZFS_NETCAT_TIMEOUT.
# There is no env var to inspect — the value is baked into the binary.
# The real proof is behavioural: on the next scheduled run, confirm no
# "exit status 141" in node agent logs and all zb CRs reach Done.

If the image tag does not match 2.11.2-nc-timeout, ArgoCD has not synced yet. Do not proceed to step (d) until the fork image is confirmed running on all eligible nodes.

docs.title: Step (d): Delete Post-Oct-6 Backup CRs, Chain-Aware [MUTATING]
docs.text:
Use velero backup delete, not kubectl delete backup. The Velero CLI creates a DeleteBackupRequest, which drives the openebs plugin's DeleteSnapshot so the ZFS snapshots and the S3 objects are actually reclaimed. kubectl delete backup removes only the CR and orphans both.

Note: The two stuck Deleting backups (retain-quaterly-20260728023032, retain-quaterly-20260804023040) are already covered by follow-up #1; deleting them again is not part of this recovery. The irony is that these stuck backups show DeleteBackupRequest can itself stall — confirm each deletion actually completes rather than assuming it.

Verified backup inventory (kubectl --context=grigri -n velero get backups):

Backup name Phase Expiration retain-quaterly-20260728023032 Deleting (stuck ~99d) 2026-10-26 retain-quaterly-20260804023040 Deleting (stuck ~92d) 2026-11-02 retain-quaterly-20260811023053 Completed 2026-11-09 retain-quaterly-20260818023002 Completed 2026-11-16 retain-quaterly-20260825023011 Completed 2026-11-23 retain-quaterly-20260926081711 PartiallyFailed 2026-12-25 retain-quaterly-20260928135503 Completed 2026-12-27 retain-quaterly-20260929023005 Completed 2026-12-28 retain-quaterly-20261006023052 Completed 2027-01-04 retain-quaterly-20261013023021 Failed 2027-01-11 retain-quaterly-20261102042133 PartiallyFailed 2027-01-31 retain-quaterly-20261104033038 PartiallyFailed 2027-02-02 retain-weekly-20261013023021 PartiallyFailed 2026-11-12 retain-weekly-20261020023030 PartiallyFailed 2026-11-12 retain-weekly-20261027023038 PartiallyFailed 2026-11-12 retain-weekly-20261103023034 PartiallyFailed 2026-11-13

PRESERVE (7): - retain-quaterly-20260811023053 — chain root for at least one volume, expires 2026-11-09 - retain-quaterly-20260818023002 - retain-quaterly-20260825023011 - retain-quaterly-20260926081711 — PartiallyFailed but MUST be preserved (see note below) - retain-quaterly-20260928135503 - retain-quaterly-20260929023005 - retain-quaterly-20261006023052 — last known-good

DELETE (7) — all post-Oct-6, both schedules: - retain-quaterly-20261013023021 - retain-quaterly-20261102042133 - retain-quaterly-20261104033038 - retain-weekly-20261013023021 - retain-weekly-20261020023030 - retain-weekly-20261027023038 - retain-weekly-20261103023034

Note on the four weekly targets: Because the weekly schedule is bound to zfspv-full (consequence #4 in step (e)), the four retain-weekly-* entries above are standalone fulls, not chain links — deleting them cannot break any restore path. Furthermore their TTL is only 240h (10 days), so three expire 2026-11-12 and the fourth 2026-11-13; they will self-clean within about a week of writing. Deleting them is optional tidiness. The part that actually matters is deleting the three post-Oct-6 retain-quaterly-* entries, because those are the ones whose truncated objects and stale Done/Failed CRs would otherwise be eligible as incremental parents.

# Delete each post-Oct-6 backup **[MUTATING]**
# velero backup delete --kubecontext grigri -n velero --confirm retain-quaterly-20261013023021
# velero backup delete --kubecontext grigri -n velero --confirm retain-quaterly-20261102042133
# velero backup delete --kubecontext grigri -n velero --confirm retain-quaterly-20261104033038
# velero backup delete --kubecontext grigri -n velero --confirm retain-weekly-20261013023021
# velero backup delete --kubecontext grigri -n velero --confirm retain-weekly-20261020023030
# velero backup delete --kubecontext grigri -n velero --confirm retain-weekly-20261027023038
# velero backup delete --kubecontext grigri -n velero --confirm retain-weekly-20261103023034

# Verify the preserved backups are still present
kubectl --context=grigri -n velero get backups | grep -E '20260811|20260818|20260825|20260926|20260928|20260929|20261006'

Chain topology note: retain-quaterly-20260926081711 is PartiallyFailed but MUST still be preserved. Sep 28 is a FULL for only 2 volumes and an incremental off Sep 26 for the other 30, so Sep 26 is a load-bearing chain link despite its phase. Its one truncated object belongs to a volume that got a fresh full at Sep 28, so the truncated object is orphaned dead weight, not a broken link. Phase alone does not tell you whether a backup is safe to delete.

Sep 28, Sep 29 and Oct 6 are 100% incremental for the remaining volumes. The chain is per-volume, so some volumes have longer chains than others.

docs.title: Step (e): Force a Fresh FULL via incrBackupCount [MUTATING]
docs.text:
Do NOT delete Done ZFSBackup CRs to force a full. That destroys the underlying ZFS snapshots (see "Do Not Do This" below). The source-verified mechanism is to temporarily set incrBackupCount: "0" in the VolumeSnapshotLocation config.

Source: getPrevSnap in pkg/zfs/plugin/backup.go (openebs/velero-plugin v3.6.0, commit cea57783), lines 79–117:

func (p *Plugin) getPrevSnap(volname, schdname string) (string, error) {
    if p.incremental < 1 || len(schdname) == 0 {
        // not an incremental backup, take the full backup
        return "", nil
    }
    listOptions := metav1.ListOptions{
        LabelSelector: VeleroSchdKey + "=" + schdname + "," + VeleroVolKey + "=" + volname,
    }
    bkpList, err := bkpbuilder.NewKubeclient().WithNamespace(p.namespace).List(listOptions)
    ...
    size := len(bkpList.Items)
    count := p.incremental + 1
    if uint64(size)%count == 0 {
        // have to start the next snapshot incremental group, take the full backup
        return "", nil
    }
    // otherwise: pick the lexicographically last SnapName among CRs with Status == Done
}

p.incremental is set in pkg/zfs/plugin/zfs.go lines 68–74 from the VSL config key incrBackupCount (ZfsPvIncr), parsed as uint64.

Consequences:

  1. incrBackupCount: "0" forces a FULL — VERIFIED. 0 < 1 short-circuits getPrevSnap to "" before any modulo arithmetic. No division by zero. If the key is absent entirely, p.incremental keeps Go's zero value 0, so absent also means always-full.
  2. With the production value "11", count = 12, so a full happens when len(CR list) % 12 == 0 — i.e. 11 incrementals between fulls. The count is len(bkpList.Items), which includes CRs from Failed runs, and is filtered only by the labels velero.io/schedule-name=<schedule> and velero.io/volname=<volume> — not by status. Only the prevSnapName selection filters on Status == Done. The post-Oct-6 failed runs therefore shifted the modulo, which is part of why no natural full arrived. Caveat: step (d) deletes those failed backups via velero backup delete, which drives the plugin's DeleteSnapshot path; if that removes the corresponding ZFSBackup CRs (inferred from the plugin's delete path, not verified from source — the openebs/velero-plugin v3.6.0 source is not available locally to confirm), the CR count drops and the modulo position shifts again. Either way, the forced-full route below is the reliable fix.
  3. A manual backup that is not triggered by a Schedule has an empty schdname, so it is ALWAYS a full — the len(schdname) == 0 branch. But because the label selector includes schedule-name, a manual full is not visible to subsequent scheduled runs as a parent, so it creates a standalone restorable anchor without re-basing the scheduled chain. To re-base the scheduled chain, use Route A or Route B below.
  4. zfspv-full is special by design — the two schedules bind to different VSLs. schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml binds to volumeSnapshotLocations: [zfspv-incr] (which carries incrBackupCount: "11"), while schedule-retain-weekly.yaml binds to volumeSnapshotLocations: [zfspv-full] (which has no incrBackupCount key at all — verified by grep -n "incrBackupCount" platform/velero/values.yaml, single hit at line 74 inside the zfspv-incr block). Because getPrevSnap returns "" (full) when p.incremental < 1, and p.incremental defaults to Go's zero value 0 when the key is absent, every retain-weekly-* backup is a standalone FULL by construction, not a link in any incremental chain. Only retain-quaterly-* backups form an incremental chain. The VSL zfspv-full needs no change to produce a full — that is evidently its purpose.

Trade-off: A full backup costs on the order of the Sep 28 backup (~769 GB for all volumes). Continuing the incremental from Oct 6 would be cheaper but risks chain corruption if any intermediate is missing or if the Oct 6 chain root expires (Nov 9 for Aug 11). Forcing a fresh full is safer and simpler.

Both routes below must go through git, not kubectl patch. This repo is GitOps with ArgoCD selfHeal: true; a kubectl patch on the VolumeSnapshotLocation or the Schedule would be reverted almost instantly.

Why either route re-bases the chain: getPrevSnap keys the CR lookup on the labels velero.io/schedule-name=<schdname> and velero.io/volname=<vol>, and createBackup sets those labels whenever schdname is non-empty — the VSL only supplies p.incremental. So a quarterly run performed through zfspv-full still creates a ZFSBackup CR labelled schedule-name=retain-quaterly, and the next quarterly run through zfspv-incr will select it as prevSnapName (it picks the lexicographically last Done SnapName). The chain re-bases onto the new full regardless of which VSL produced it.

docs.title: Route A (recommended) — point the quarterly schedule at zfspv-full for one run [MUTATING]
docs.text:
A one-line change to platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml: volumeSnapshotLocations: [zfspv-incr] → [zfspv-full]. This uses the VSL that already exists for exactly this purpose (consequence #4 above) and changes no numeric value.

Commit 1 — switch VSL [MUTATING]:

# Edit platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml:
# change volumeSnapshotLocations from [zfspv-incr] to [zfspv-full]
sed -i 's/- zfspv-incr/- zfspv-full/' platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml
git add platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml
git commit -m 'velero: Force quarterly full via zfspv-full VSL for one run'
git push
# Wait for ArgoCD to sync, then wait for the next scheduled quarterly run to complete.
# Verify:
velero backup get --kubecontext grigri -n velero
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get zb | grep -v Done

Commit 2 — revert VSL [MUTATING]:

# After the full backup lands (all zb CRs reach Done, backup phase is Completed):
sed -i 's/- zfspv-full/- zfspv-incr/' platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml
git add platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml
git commit -m 'velero: Restore quarterly schedule to zfspv-incr VSL'
git push

Prefer this route because reverting a volumeSnapshotLocations list is harder to get wrong than reverting a counter — there is no numeric value that could silently be left at the wrong setting and turn every future quarterly run into a 769 GB full.

docs.title: Route B — temporarily set incrBackupCount: "0" on zfspv-incr [MUTATING]
docs.text:
Behaviourally identical to Route A (p.incremental = 0 either way), but leaves a live numeric value that must be remembered and restored.

WARNING: Leaving incrBackupCount at "0" makes every scheduled quarterly run a full (~769 GB each). Revert immediately after the full lands. Forgetting to revert is the main risk of this route.

Commit 1 — set incrBackupCount: "0" [MUTATING]:

# Edit platform/velero/values.yaml: under zfspv-incr.config, change incrBackupCount to "0"
sed -i 's/incrBackupCount: "11"/incrBackupCount: "0"/' platform/velero/values.yaml
git add platform/velero/values.yaml
git commit -m 'velero: Force full backup by setting incrBackupCount to 0'
git push
# Wait for ArgoCD to sync, then wait for the next scheduled run to complete.
# Verify:
velero backup get --kubecontext grigri -n velero
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get zb | grep -v Done

Commit 2 — revert to "11" [MUTATING]:

# After the full backup lands (all zb CRs reach Done, backup phase is Completed):
sed -i 's/incrBackupCount: "0"/incrBackupCount: "11"/' platform/velero/values.yaml
git add platform/velero/values.yaml
git commit -m 'velero: Restore incrBackupCount to 11 after forced full'
git push

docs.title: Step (f): Verify the New Backup is Completed and Spot-Check DRR_END
docs.text:
# Wait for the backup to complete
velero backup get --kubecontext grigri -n velero | tail -5

# Check all ZFSBackup CRs reached Done
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get zb | grep -v Done

# Download a few objects and verify DRR_END=1 (list and grep for the key, do not construct it)
# aws --endpoint-url=https://s3.internal.grigri.cloud --profile velero \
#   s3 ls s3://velero/backups/<new-backup-name>/ | grep <volume-name> | grep -v '\.zfsvol$'
# aws --endpoint-url=https://s3.internal.grigri.cloud --profile velero \
#   s3 cp s3://velero/backups/<new-backup-name>/<object-key> /tmp/<volume>.zfs
# zstream dump /tmp/<volume>.zfs | grep -c '^DRR_END'  # Should be 1

docs.title: Step (g): Restore Test into a Scratch Namespace
docs.text:
# Create a scratch namespace
kubectl --context=grigri create namespace restore-test

# Restore a few volumes into the scratch namespace **[MUTATING]**
# velero restore create --kubecontext grigri -n velero \
#   --from-backup <new-backup-name> \
#   --namespace-mappings '<original-ns>:restore-test' \
#   --include-resources persistentvolumes,persistentvolumeclaims

# Verify the restored PVCs are bound and the data is intact
kubectl --context=grigri -n restore-test get pvc
# kubectl --context=grigri -n restore-test exec -it <pod> -- ls -la /data

# Clean up the scratch namespace when done **[MUTATING]**
# kubectl --context=grigri delete namespace restore-test

docs.title: Do Not Do This
docs.text:
• Do NOT downgrade zfs-localpv to 2.10.1. That version runs the pipeline as bash -c "zfs send | nc" without pipefail, so the sender's SIGPIPE is masked and truncation is reported as success. It is the version that hid this bug, not the version that avoids it. See the per-version behavior table above.

  • Do NOT lower multiPartChunkSize below 100Mi. MinIO's MaxUploadParts=10000 caps object size at chunkSize x 10000. The largest full send already consumes most of that budget (~769 GB). Reducing multiPartChunkSize would break large fulls with TotalPartsExceeded (openebs/velero-plugin#185, openebs/velero-plugin#188). Keep it at 100Mi.

  • Do NOT delete Done ZFSBackup CRs to force a full backup. The ZFSBackup resource carries the finalizer zfs.openebs.io/finalizer; on deletion the backup controller's syncBkp sees DeletionTimestamp, calls zfs.DestoryBackup(bkp) (upstream typo is real), which builds a ZFSSnapshot from bkp.Spec.SnapName and runs zfs destroy <pool>/<vol>@<snapname>, then removes the finalizer. Deleting a ZFSBackup CR destroys the underlying ZFS snapshot. Doing that for the Aug 11 → Oct 6 chain makes those backups permanently unrestorable. Use Route A (switch VSL) or Route B (incrBackupCount: "0") in step (e) instead.

docs.title: Follow-Ups (Separate Defects)
docs.text:
These defects were found during the investigation and should be addressed separately:

  1. Two backups stuck in phase Deleting for 92-99 days (retain-quaterly-20260728023032, retain-quaterly-20260804023040) with no deletionTimestamp and no finalizers, despite their DeleteBackupRequest showing Processed. No clear recovery path; may require manual CR deletion and S3 cleanup.

  2. ~43 orphaned backup prefixes in the bucket with no corresponding Backup CR; 1008 objects total, 864 zfs-prefixed, 106 under 1 KB. Requires S3 cleanup with mc rm --recursive --force --versions or equivalent.

  3. ~739 leftover ZFS snapshots on the storage node dating to Aug 11. Requires manual cleanup with zfs destroy after verifying no ZFSBackup CR references them.

  4. Prometheus serves no data at all (even up returns empty) and Grafana has zero alert rules — which is why a 3-week total backup outage was never paged. Requires Prometheus/Grafana investigation and alert rule creation.

  5. 13 stateful zfs-localpv PVCs have no backup/retain label and are silently excluded, including gitaly repo storage and several Spilo postgres volumes. Requires labeling the PVCs and verifying they are included in subsequent backups.

  6. Retention margin is structurally fragile. The 34 PVCs labelled backup/retain: quaterly are the large volumes and they only ever receive incrementals except on every 12th run; the 14 PVCs labelled backup/retain: weekly receive a full every week but with a 10-day TTL, so those fulls expire before they can serve as an archive. The label is single-valued, so no volume is in both sets. The consequence is that the big data depends entirely on one incremental chain whose root expires at 90 days while a replacement full only arrives every 12 weekly runs (84 days) — about 6 days of margin, and that margin only holds if every run succeeds. The Oct 13 – Nov 4 failures consumed it: retain-quaterly-20260811023053 is expiring on 2026-11-09 with no replacement full in place. This is a latent design flaw independent of the netcat bug. Consider shortening the full cycle, lengthening the TTL, or adding a second full anchor.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
A Velero backup stops advancing on one PV while its ZFSBackup stays Init. On the volume's owner node, zfs send remains alive, its nc child has exited (possibly as a zombie), and the receiver's TCP port 9011 no longer has an active connection. zfs destroy of the backup snapshot returns dataset is busy because the sender is still using it. The backup can block subsequent scheduled backups.

An object in S3 is not proof of a complete stream. The receiver closes its object writer when a client disconnects, even if the expected ZFS stream has not arrived. A finished object and a Client{...} operation completed log line do not mean that the ZFSBackup reached Done or that the volume can be restored.

docs.title: Root Cause and Confidence
docs.text:
The confirmed failure mechanism is in the OpenEBS ZFS driver v2.11.x process handling. The node agent runs zfs send ... | nc -w 3 <velero-pod-ip> 9011. Its runPipe implementation waits for zfs send before waiting for nc. If nc exits while the send is still producing data, the copy into nc stops consuming the send's stdout. The pipe fills, zfs send blocks, and the backup controller never updates ZFSBackup.status from Init. The implementation also returns only nc's exit error, ignoring the zfs send error: killing the sender alone risks a false Done status for a truncated stream.

The installed OpenEBS Velero plugin v3.6.0 polls ZFSBackup.status without a timeout in its checkBackupStatus loop. The backup remains blocked even with a 32-hour Velero itemOperationTimeout configured; earlier backups ran longer than 32 hours. On a node-agent restart, snapshot already there is informational: CreateSnapshot returns success and the agent tries to send again. Restarting it alone can reproduce the deadlock.

The investigation does not establish why nc or the receiver stopped on the original sends. Possible triggers include receiver termination, an idle timeout under object-store backpressure, transport failure, or the preceding control-plane outage. A zombie nc proves the process exited; it does not by itself prove an S3 or network outage. Therefore distinguish these conclusions:

  • Confirmed: v2.11.x can turn an early nc exit into an indefinitely blocked zfs send and ZFSBackup in Init.
  • Strong operational evidence: rollback to v2.10.1 prevented that indefinite state on the next retry and allowed the previously stuck Hermes full stream to transfer.
  • Not yet proven: the event that made the original nc processes exit, and whether it was caused by the driver, receiver, object store, network, or control-plane disruption.

docs.title: Version and Failure Timeline
docs.text:
Time (UTC) Event ZFS LocalPV 2026-08-24 03:23 ArgoCD deployed the 2.11.0 chart. 2.11.0 2026-08-25 02:30–02:41 Quarterly incremental backup completed successfully. 2.11.0 2026-09-01 Quarterly backup was created but did not start because the queue was blocked. 2.11.0 2026-09-07 06:07 ArgoCD deployed the 2.11.1 chart. 2.11.1 2026-09-21–23 First retained PartiallyFailed backup completed with 54 errors after starting late. 2.11.1 2026-09-25 02:20 Memory pressure caused the k3s/etcd outage and stale controller state. 2.11.1 2026-09-26 08:17–08:19 First confirmed stream-pipeline deadlock, on the Gitea full send. 2.11.1 2026-09-26 22:39 ArgoCD rolled ZFS LocalPV back. 2.10.1 After rollback The node agent retried the Hermes full send and actively transferred the stream. 2.10.1

This timeline is correlation, not proof that every September backup failure had the same cause. The August 25 success under 2.11.0 was incremental, while the confirmed deadlocks involved large full sends after some volumes lacked usable predecessor metadata. Queue blockage from the September 25 outage and the v2.11.x process-handling defect are separate issues that compounded each other.

Historical Prometheus queries returned no samples for the relevant August–September range. The timeline therefore comes from retained Velero resources, ArgoCD history, Git history, ZFS process inspection, node-agent logs, and S3 object inspection. Prometheus currently exposes Velero backup and Kubernetes container-image metrics, but it cannot retroactively prove the sequence above.

docs.title: How to Diagnose
docs.text:
kubectl --context=grigri -n velero get backups
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv get zb \
  -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,STATUS:.status,NODE:.spec.ownerNodeID,DEST:.spec.backupDest'

# On the owner node, match the specific snapshot and note the sender, nc and their parent PIDs.
ssh <node> 'ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,etime,args' | grep -E 'zfs send|\[nc\]|zfs-driver'
ssh <node> 'ss -tn state established' | grep 9011

# Read-only estimate; compare with the object size, allowing for stream compression/options.
ssh <node> 'zfs send -nP datasets/openebs/<volume>@<backup-name>'
ssh <node> 'zfs holds datasets/openebs/<volume>@<backup-name>'
ssh <node> 'zfs get -H -o property,value clones,userrefs datasets/openebs/<volume>@<backup-name>'

Inspect the Velero backup logs and the historical node-agent logs in Loki if pod logs have rotated. Look for a Velero Uploading snapshot to line without a matching successfully uploaded object, a Client{...} operation completed line, and an agent Got add event for Bkp without a backup ... done line. Inspect zfs holds and zfs get clones,userrefs before attributing a busy snapshot to a send process; a held or cloned snapshot requires a different fix.

The 2026-09-26 Gitea incident is an example: the full send for restored-3eeb806f-98c4-4ff4-a2b7-ef6f676077a1@retain-quaterly-20260926081711 was estimated at 31,893,359,112 bytes, but the object observed in S3 was only about 1.1 GiB. Velero's receiver logged a client completion at 08:19:42 UTC without logging overall upload completion. After an agent restart, a new zfs send remained blocked for over seven hours with a defunct nc process. The matching ZFSBackup remained Init and Velero stayed at 21/234 items. The partial object must not be treated as a usable Gitea backup.

docs.title: Current Status: Verifying PR #777 Fix Image
docs.text:
The chart was upgraded to 2.11.1 with the zfsPlugin.image pinned to ghcr.io/linkvt/zfs-driver:runpipe-773, a pre-merge build of PR #777 that fixes the runPipe deadlock. The fix uses os.Pipe instead of src.StdoutPipe(), waits for both children concurrently, cancels the peer when either side fails, and joins both exit errors so a source failure can no longer be silently dropped. The PR has been reviewed and approved by two upstream maintainers but is not yet merged into a release.

Exit criteria for removing the image pin:

  1. Upstream merges PR #777 and ships it in a release, and the release image passes a disposable large-volume backup test (full send + forced receiver disconnect).
  2. The verification period below confirms the fix works in this cluster.

Verification plan: after deploying, run a normal large full backup and confirm all ZFSBackup CRs reach Done. Then trigger a forced receiver disconnect (e.g. kill the Velero node-agent pod mid-transfer) and confirm the ZFSBackup moves to Failed within seconds — not stuck in Init — with no orphan zfs send or nc processes. Keep the multiPartChunkSize at 100 MiB.

If the fix image fails verification, revert by setting Chart.yaml back to 2.10.1 and removing the zfsPlugin.image override from values.yaml.

Verification status (2026-10-07 audit): the "clean" 2026-10-06 quarterly and weekly backups did not exercise the fix image. They ran 02:30–03:05 UTC under 2.10.1 — confirmed with an instant kube_pod_container_info{namespace="zfs-localpv"} query at the backup start timestamp (docker.io/openebs/zfs-driver:2.10.1) — while the runpipe-773 pods were created at 09:14 UTC, hours after the backups finished. The first scheduled runs on the fix image are 2026-10-13. To attribute any historical backup to a driver version, query kube_pod_container_info at the backup's start time; never infer from the currently deployed image.

docs.title: Further Investigation
docs.text:
For the next natural or controlled failure, collect evidence before restarting either component:

  • Velero and OpenEBS plugin logs covering receiver creation, S3 multipart writes and disconnect.
  • Node-agent logs plus ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,etime,args and repeated ss -tinp samples for port 9011.
  • MinIO request latency, errors and resource pressure during the transfer.
  • Pod restarts, events, node pressure and API availability over the same window.
  • A packet capture scoped to port 9011 where operationally acceptable.
  • zfs send -nP estimate, final object size, ZFSBackup.status, and a scratch zfs recv restore.

A controlled A/B reproducer should use a disposable large PVC under 2.10.1 and the candidate upgrade, then terminate the receiver mid-stream. The upgrade is acceptable only if both versions fail safely and the candidate never leaves the v2.11.x blocked-process signature.

docs.title: Fix / Workaround
docs.text:
Do not kill the sender first. Because the driver ignores the sender's exit code, that could mark a truncated backup Done. Do not destroy the snapshot while the send is running, and never use zfs destroy -R on an in-use volume.

For an active operation that cannot be recovered, perform these steps manually, one at a time:

  1. Record the exact ZFSBackup name, owner node, snapshot, sender PID, and parent Velero backup. Delete the stuck ZFSBackup CR first so the Velero plugin cannot mistake a terminated send for success. This intentionally fails that volume's snapshot; the backup may finish PartiallyFailed. Do not delete a working backup's other Done CRs.
  2. Confirm Velero logged zfsbackups.zfs.openebs.io "<name>" not found for that volume and advanced past the item. If abandoning the entire Velero backup instead, confirm it is no longer active before further cleanup.
  3. Re-check the sender's PID and full command line; only then stop the specific lingering zfs send with TERM. Confirm it and its nc child are gone. Avoid a broad pkill that might interrupt other volumes. A node-agent restart alone does not resolve the stream failure.
  4. Check that no Done ZFSBackup references the snapshot as snapName or prevSnapName, and that ZFS reports no holds or dependent clones. Then destroy only the orphaned snapshot on its owner node. Treat its S3 object as incomplete; clean it up only after checking backup metadata and incremental dependencies.
  5. Run a new backup with a new name and verify every expected ZFSBackup is Done, that Velero reports all snapshots completed, and that a representative restore works. A completed Backup resource alone is not proof that all volumes are restorable.

The operator can use these targeted commands after confirming each preceding condition. Replace placeholders with names and a PID verified immediately before use; never apply them to a live transfer that is still making progress:

# Step 1: intentionally fail only this volume's backup operation.
kubectl --context=grigri -n zfs-localpv delete zb <volume>.<backup-name>

# Step 2: verify Velero recorded the failed volume before continuing.
kubectl --context=grigri -n velero get backup <backup-name> -o yaml

# Step 3: after verifying the PID and full command line, stop only this sender.
ssh <node> 'ps -p <pid> -o pid,ppid,stat,etime,args'
ssh <node> 'sudo kill -TERM <pid>'

# Step 4: after the process exits and the snapshot is confirmed orphaned.
ssh <node> 'sudo zfs destroy datasets/openebs/<volume>@<backup-name>'

For prevention, use a fixed upstream release or patch the driver to cancel/reap both children when either side exits or the receiver disconnects, propagate both exit statuses, and bound the operation with a timeout. The receiver should reject/clean up truncated streams rather than treat socket closure as success. Alert on Init resources and non-advancing backups; investigate node reboots, API outages and receiver/object-store stalls independently.

docs.title: Zalando Patroni Stale DCS Deadlock After PVC Recreate
Symptoms
docs.text:
After deleting a Zalando Postgres PVC and letting the pod recreate with a fresh volume:

  • Pod shows 2/2 Running (Patroni container is running)
  • PostgreSQL is not serving — connections fail with "database does not exist" or "connection refused"
  • patronictl list shows the member as stopped / Replica with no Leader
  • Logs show: "waiting for leader to bootstrap" repeating every 10 seconds
  • The readest-postgres-config ConfigMap has an initialize annotation with an old system identifier
  • The postgres data directory is empty (never initdb'd)

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text:
When you delete the PVC, the Patroni Kubernetes DCS ConfigMaps survive (they're runtime state, not GitOps-managed, no owner references). These ConfigMaps carry the old cluster's initialize marker (system identifier).

Patroni sees the initialize marker in the DCS → believes the cluster already exists → refuses to run initdb on the fresh empty data directory → waits forever for a Leader that will never appear. Deadlock.

The Patroni DCS objects are: - readest-postgres-config (holds initialize marker + dynamic config) - readest-postgres-leader (leader lock + replication slot state)

Both are ConfigMaps in the app namespace, created by Patroni, not managed by the Zalando operator or ArgoCD.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
# Check pod status
kubectl --context=grigri get pods -n readest -o wide

# Check Patroni cluster state
kubectl --context=grigri exec -n readest readest-postgres-0 -c postgres -- patronictl list

# Check Patroni logs
kubectl --context=grigri logs -n readest readest-postgres-0 -c postgres --tail=40 | grep -i "waiting for leader"

# Check if initialize marker exists
kubectl --context=grigri get configmap readest-postgres-config -n readest -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.initialize}'

# Check postgres data directory (should be empty if never initdb'd)
kubectl --context=grigri exec -n readest readest-postgres-0 -c postgres -- ls -la /home/postgres/pgdata/pgroot/data/

If you see: - patronictl list → member "stopped", no Leader - Logs → "waiting for leader to bootstrap" - initialize annotation present with old system ID - Empty data directory

→ You have the stale DCS deadlock.

docs.title: Fix
docs.text:
Delete the stale Patroni DCS ConfigMaps and restart the pod. This is safe: the Zalando operator regenerates the dynamic config from the CR, and Patroni writes a fresh initialize marker after initdb.

# 1. Delete stale Patroni DCS ConfigMaps
kubectl --context=grigri delete configmap readest-postgres-config readest-postgres-leader -n readest

# 2. Restart the pod to trigger fresh bootstrap
kubectl --context=grigri delete pod readest-postgres-0 -n readest

# 3. Wait ~30s, then verify Patroni becomes Leader
kubectl --context=grigri exec -n readest readest-postgres-0 -c postgres -- patronictl list
# Should show: Role=Leader, State=running

After Patroni bootstraps, the Zalando operator will create the database and roles from the CR. If the operator doesn't sync automatically, force it:

# Force operator sync by annotating the CR
kubectl --context=grigri annotate postgresql readest-postgres -n readest zalando.org/sync-at="$(date +%s)" --overwrite

docs.title: Post-Bootstrap Steps
docs.text:
After Patroni bootstraps and the operator creates the database:

  1. Wait for GoTrue + db-migrate to populate the schema (they run as init containers / startup hooks)
  2. Restore non-GitOps data (if applicable):
  3. ALTER DATABASE readest SET search_path TO auth, public;
  4. INSERT INTO auth.custom_oauth_providers ... (custom OIDC provider)
  5. User data, app data, etc.
  6. Restart app pods to ensure they pick up the fresh schema

docs.title: Prevention
docs.text:
To avoid this in the future:

  • Don't delete Zalando Postgres PVCs without also deleting the Patroni DCS ConfigMaps
  • If you must recreate, delete both the PVC and the DCS ConfigMaps in one operation
  • Document the recreate procedure in the deployment docs

docs.title: Why This Happens
docs.text:
Zalando Postgres uses Patroni for HA. Patroni stores cluster state in Kubernetes DCS (ConfigMaps or Endpoints). The initialize marker is written after the first successful initdb and contains the cluster's system identifier. When Patroni starts, it checks:

  1. Is there an initialize marker in the DCS?
  2. Does my local data directory match the system identifier?

If (1) yes and (2) no (empty data dir), Patroni assumes it's a replica waiting for the Leader to bootstrap. But if there's no Leader (the old pod is gone), it waits forever.

The fix removes the stale initialize marker, so Patroni treats this as a fresh cluster and runs initdb.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
• Affected deployment: apps/readest/templates/postgresql.yaml
  • Related: docs/deployment/readest.md (Zalando Postgres + automated migrations)
  • Patroni DCS docs: https://patroni.readthedocs.io/en/latest/kubernetes.html

docs.title: Zalando single-instance cluster stuck UpdateFailed after a resource change
Problem
docs.text:
After changing spec.resources (e.g. lowering a memory request) on a single-replica (numberOfInstances: 1) Zalando postgresql CR, the operator sets status.PostgresClusterStatus: UpdateFailed and ArgoCD reports the application Degraded.

The database is actually fine: the postgres pod is Running, Patroni reports it Leader/running with 0 restarts, the new resource values are applied to the StatefulSet and pod, and clients connect normally. Only the operator's status is stuck. A periodic resync does not reliably clear it.

This is distinct from the stale-DCS deadlock, which happens after a PVC recreate; here the data dir and DCS are untouched.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text:
To apply a pod-spec change such as resources, the operator must recreate the pod. With a single instance there is no replica to fail over to:

cannot perform switch over before re-creating the pod: no replicas
recreating old master pod "<ns>/<cluster>-0"

The operator deletes the sole master and waits for the old pod object to disappear. The StatefulSet controller immediately recreates a pod with the same name, so the operator's deletion-wait cannot confirm the old pod is gone and eventually times out (~10 minutes):

could not sync statefulsets: could not recreate pods: could not recreate old master pod
"<ns>/<cluster>-0": pod deletion wait timeout

The recreate itself succeeded — the new pod carries the updated resources — but the operator's bookkeeping ended in error, leaving UpdateFailed latched on the CR.

docs.title: How to Diagnose
docs.text:
# Operator logs show the no-replica recreate + deletion timeout
kubectl --context=grigri -n postgres-operator logs deploy/postgres-operator --tail=2000 \
  | grep -i '<cluster>' | grep -iE 'no replicas|recreat|deletion wait|updated'

# CR status is latched
kubectl --context=grigri -n <ns> get postgresql <cluster> \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.PostgresClusterStatus}{"\n"}'   # -> UpdateFailed

# But the pod is healthy AND the change is applied
kubectl --context=grigri -n <ns> exec <cluster>-0 -c postgres -- patronictl list
kubectl --context=grigri -n <ns> get pod <cluster>-0 \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources}{"\n"}'

If the pod is Leader/running, restarts are not climbing, and the StatefulSet resources already match the CR, the failure is cosmetic bookkeeping — not a real outage.

docs.title: Fix / Workaround
docs.text:
Restart the postgres-operator to clear the latched state. It resyncs, sees the StatefulSet already matches the desired spec, does nothing destructive, and sets the status back to Running:

kubectl --context=grigri -n postgres-operator rollout restart deploy/postgres-operator
kubectl --context=grigri -n <ns> get postgresql <cluster> \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.PostgresClusterStatus}{"\n"}'   # -> Running

This restarts the control-plane operator only; it does not touch the database pods or data. It does briefly pause reconciliation for all Zalando clusters, so prefer it over deleting/recreating the postgres pod.

docs.title: Prevention
docs.text: Resource/spec changes on a single-instance cluster inherently require recreating the sole master (a brief blip) and can trip this deletion-wait timeout. Where practical, batch resource changes, or expect a transient UpdateFailed that needs an operator restart to clear. Multi-instance clusters can switch over to a replica and avoid the same-name deletion-wait confusion.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text: KubePersistentVolumeFillingUp alert fires for a PVC. df inside the pod shows the volume is nearly full, but the actual data (du) is much smaller than the volume capacity.

docs.title: Root Cause
docs.text:
ZFS Copy-on-Write snapshots hold references to old blocks that have been overwritten. When an application frequently rewrites large files (e.g., media cover images), each snapshot accumulates unique blocks. The cumulative space consumed by all snapshots can far exceed the live data size.

Two independent backup mechanisms create ZFS snapshots on every PVC:

  1. Snapscheduler (snapscheduler.backube/v1 SnapshotSchedule) — daily at 01:00 UTC, configurable maxCount per app (default: 20). Creates snapshot-<uuid> ZFS snapshots.

  2. Velero (Schedule CRD) — weekly on Tuesdays at 02:30 UTC and quarterly on Wednesdays at 03:30 UTC, 90-day TTL. Uses the openebs.io/zfspv-blockstore plugin which creates retain-quaterly-<timestamp> ZFS snapshots and uploads volume data to MinIO.

docs.title: Known High-Churn Applications
docs.text:
App Path Issue Radarr /config/MediaCover/ (2.7 GB) Re-downloads poster/fanart images for ~2000 movies daily (~800-1800 file rewrites/day) Sonarr /config/MediaCover/ Same pattern as Radarr Bazarr /config/MediaCover/ Same pattern as Radarr Lidarr /config/MediaCover/ Same pattern as Radarr Prowlarr /config/MediaCover/ Same pattern as Radarr

Each daily snapshot holds ~50 MB of unique MediaCover blocks. With maxCount: 20, that's ~1 GB minimum in snapshots alone, with burst days reaching 200+ MB per snapshot.

docs.title: Diagnosis
docs.text:
# Check ZFS space breakdown (live data vs snapshots)
zfs list -o name,used,usedbysnapshots,avail,refer <dataset>

# List all snapshots with their unique space usage
zfs list -t snapshot -o name,used,refer,creation <dataset>

# Check what files changed between two snapshots
sudo zfs diff <dataset>@<old-snap> <dataset>@<new-snap> | grep -c MediaCover

# Check inside the pod
kubectl exec -n <namespace> <pod> -- df -h /config
kubectl exec -n <namespace> <pod> -- du -sh /config/* | sort -rh

# Check snapscheduler retention
kubectl get snapshotschedules -A

# Check Velero backup expiration
kubectl get backups -n velero -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PHASE:.status.phase,EXPIRATION:.status.expiration

docs.title: Reduce snapscheduler retention
docs.text:
For high-churn *arr apps, reduce maxCount in apps/<name>/templates/snapshots.yaml:

spec:
  retention:
    maxCount: 5  # was 20, reduced for *arr apps with large MediaCover

Snapscheduler prunes excess VolumeSnapshot CRDs (and their ZFS snapshots) at the next scheduled snapshot time. Changes take effect on the next reconciliation.

docs.title: Clean up orphaned ZFS snapshots
docs.text:
When Velero backup objects expire and are garbage-collected, the corresponding ZFS snapshots should be cleaned up. However, some snapshots may become orphaned (e.g., after a Velero restore or migration). These appear as ZFS snapshots with no matching Velero backup object or VolumeSnapshot CRD.

# Identify orphaned snapshots (ZFS snapshots with no k8s CRD managing them)
zfs list -t snapshot -o name <dataset>

# Destroy orphaned snapshots
sudo zfs destroy <dataset>@<snapshot-name>

docs.title: Increase ZFS quota (temporary band-aid)
docs.text: sudo zfs set quota=20G <dataset>

docs.title: Prevention
docs.text:
• Use maxCount: 5 for *arr apps (MediaCover is regenerable — Radarr re-downloads images automatically). The real config is only ~50-80 MB (DB + settings).
  • Use maxCount: 1 for database PVCs (Postgres, MariaDB) since they use WAL-based recovery.
  • Use maxCount: 20 only for PVCs with low churn and critical data.
  • MediaCover data is not worth snapshotting extensively — Velero weekly backups provide sufficient disaster recovery coverage.

docs.title: Key Files
docs.text: File Purpose apps/<name>/templates/snapshots.yaml Snapscheduler SnapshotSchedule CRD per app platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-quaterly.yaml Velero quarterly-chain backup schedule (Wed 03:30 UTC) platform/velero/templates/schedule-retain-weekly.yaml Velero weekly full backup schedule system/zfs-localpv/ ZFS-LocalPV driver and VolumeSnapshotClass (zfspv-snapclass)

docs.title: Add or remove nodes
docs.text: Or how to scale vertically. To replace the same node with a clean OS, remove it and add it again.

docs.title: Add new nodes
docs.text:
Tip

You can add multiple nodes at the same time

docs.title: Inventory groups
docs.text:
Add the node to metal/inventory/hosts.ini. A worker joins [amd64_node] (which flows kube_node → k3s_cluster) and [amd64]. It must not join kube_control_plane, nvidia or ipmi:

diff --git a/metal/inventory/hosts.ini b/metal/inventory/hosts.ini
--- a/metal/inventory/hosts.ini
+++ b/metal/inventory/hosts.ini
@@ -7,6 +7,7 @@
 [amd64_node]
 grigri
+k8s-amd64-1

 [amd64]
 prusik
 grigri
+k8s-amd64-1

The hardcoded play host lists in prepare.yml and cluster.yml must not be edited:

play hosts purpose prepare.yml:11 Setup amd64 grigri, prusik media user, postfix/telegram notifications, smartd prepare.yml:18 Setup swap prusik swap file prepare.yml:23 Setup NVIDIA drivers nvidia group GPU runtime prepare.yml:30 Setup pikvm prusik-ipmi IPMI console cluster.yml:28 Install zfs-exporter grigri, prusik ZFS metrics

A new node gets no setup role, so no media user, no postfix/telegram notifications and no smartd config. These are exactly the ZFS/GPU/backup paths a new node must stay out of.

docs.title: Host variables
docs.text:
Create metal/inventory/host_vars/<node>.yml. Contents depend on whether the node has a ZFS pool.

No-ZFS node (e.g. k8s-amd64-1):

# Ubuntu 26.04: sudo-rs rejects -H; classic sudo is at /usr/bin/sudo.ws
ansible_become_exe: /usr/bin/sudo.ws

# chrony is the default time daemon on 26.04; the `ntp` package does not exist
ntp_daemon_select: chrony
ntp_package: chrony
ntp_config_file: /etc/chrony/chrony.conf

# Required when DHCP does not push the search domain. roles/k3s/templates/config.yaml.j2
# builds `server: https://prusik:6443` from ansible_hostname, so a node that cannot resolve
# short names cannot join. grigri and prusik get `search grigri` from DHCP.
prepare_dns_search_domains:
  - grigri

# All three of kube-reserved / system-reserved / eviction-hard must be set because
# host_vars overrides group_vars/kube_node.yml wholesale. eviction-hard also replaces
# kubelet's whole threshold map (k3s defaults are nodefs/imagefs 5%), so list every
# signal you care about. A CI-only node may want nodefs.available<5%: see
# docs/troubleshooting/ci-runner-amd64-disk-full.md.
k3s_kubelet_extra_args:
  - kube-reserved=cpu=0.5,memory=512Mi,ephemeral-storage=1Gi
  - system-reserved=cpu=0.5,memory=1Gi,ephemeral-storage=1Gi
  - eviction-hard=memory.available<500Mi,nodefs.available<10%

Omit every zfs_*/l2arc_*/swap_file_size_mb key — roles/setup/tasks/zfs.yml:2-8 asserts on them and hard-fails. Also never set prepare_additional_disks (the disk-format loop at roles/prepare/tasks/main.yml:64-70 no-ops only while that list is empty, and prepare_additional_disks_force_format is data-destroying).

ZFS node (e.g. prusik, grigri): same k3s_kubelet_extra_args (all three keys, because group_vars/kube_node.yml:6 is overridden wholesale), plus zfs_arc_min_gb, zfs_arc_max_gb, l2arc_write_max_mb, l2arc_write_boost_mb, l2arc_noprefetch, and on prusik only swap_file_size_mb.

docs.title: Ubuntu 26.04 specifics
docs.text:
key value why ansible_become_exe /usr/bin/sudo.ws sudo-rs removed -H; do NOT apt remove sudo-rs, it takes ubuntu-minimal with it ntp_daemon_select chrony the ntp package no longer exists in resolute; must go through ntp_daemon_select / the metal/roles/ntp wrapper — setting ntp_daemon in host_vars does nothing (include_vars outranks inventory host_vars) ntp_package chrony ntp_config_file /etc/chrony/chrony.conf prepare_dns_search_domains [grigri] when DHCP does not push the search domain

24.04 uses ntpsec, 22.04 uses the ntp default. See docs/troubleshooting/ansible-ubuntu-2604-compat.md for full details.

docs.title: Prerequisites: pfSense BGP neighbour
docs.text: system/kube-system/resources/cilium/bgp-cluster-config.yaml selects kubernetes.io/os: linux with localASN: 64513 peering to peerAddress: 192.168.192.1 at peerASN: 64512. The cluster side is automatic for any new node, but FRR on pfSense must have a neighbour entry for the node's IP with remote-as 64513, matching grigri and prusik. Without it, BGP never establishes and no pod CIDR or LoadBalancer IP is announced from the node.

docs.title: Pre-flight: bootstrap the new node
docs.text:
make first-boot is not usable for a modern Ubuntu node: it forces -e ansible_user=root --ask-pass and Ubuntu images are PermitRootLogin prohibit-password. It is also not scopeable because it appends its own --limit after ANSIBLE_EXTRA_ARGS (the last --limit wins in metal/Makefile:10,43-82).

Before the first make prepare, create the user and ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the new node. Passwordless sudo is needed because roles/prepare/tasks/user.yml:26-30 is what writes the %sudo ... NOPASSWD:ALL rule (chicken-and-egg). Either:

  • add /etc/sudoers.d/90-ansible (mode 440) by hand once, or
  • run the first prepare with -K (ask-become-pass), which works because ansible_become_exe points at classic sudo

docs.title: Prepare and join
docs.text:
All commands must be scoped with --limit. ANSIBLE_EXTRA_ARGS is interpolated verbatim BEFORE the playbook path (metal/Makefile:10,43-82), so the last --limit wins.

# 1. OS preparation (scoped to the new node)
cd metal && ANSIBLE_EXTRA_ARGS="--limit <node>" make prepare

# 2. Join the cluster (HUMAN ONLY — an untagged make cluster is on the AGENTS.md never-run list;
#    agents may run only a committed, config-only "-t k3s --limit <node>" apply)
cd metal && ANSIBLE_EXTRA_ARGS="--limit <node>" make cluster

With --limit, the k3s role's run_once + delegate_to: prusik tasks are read-only (slurp) and the kubeconfig write is delegate_to: localhost.

docs.title: Node labels
docs.text:
The node-labels play needs metal/kubeconfig.yaml, which only exists after the k3s role writes it (roles/k3s/tasks/main.yml:167) during make cluster. So labels come after the join.

# Label ZFS nodes only (HUMAN ONLY)
cd metal && ANSIBLE_EXTRA_ARGS="--limit grigri,prusik -t node-labels" make cluster

docs.title: Post-join verification
docs.text:
# Node is Ready
kubectl --context=grigri get nodes -o wide

# Allocatable memory and kubelet args
kubectl describe node <node>

# DaemonSets scheduled: cilium, cilium-envoy, node-exporter, smartctl-exporter,
# vector-agent, nodelocaldns
kubectl get ds -A

# Cilium BGP peer to 192.168.192.1 established (bgp-cluster-config.yaml peers on
# kubernetes.io/os: linux, so it is automatic — but the router must accept the new peer)
kubectl --context=grigri get pods -n kube-system -l k8s-app=cilium -o wide
kubectl --context=grigri exec -n kube-system <cilium-pod-on-that-node> -c cilium-agent -- cilium bgp peers

# chrony synced to pfsense.grigri (192.168.192.1)
chronyc -n sources
# On 22.04/24.04 (ntpsec): ntpq -pn

# Nothing new stuck Pending
kubectl get pods -A --field-selector=status.phase=Pending

docs.title: BGP peer must show established
docs.text:
cilium bgp peers prints Session active when the TCP session is still trying — this is not established. A healthy peer shows established with a non-zero uptime. Meanwhile Cilium itself looks completely healthy (Cilium: Ok, NetworkUnavailable=False, KubeProxyReplacement: True), so a missing BGP session is easy to miss.

If the session stays active, the pfSense FRR neighbour entry for the node's IP is missing or wrong (see Prerequisites).

Do not judge the session by the advertised-route count. CiliumBGPAdvertisement (default-advertisement) advertises only Service / LoadBalancerIP — podCIDRs are never advertised on any node. A freshly joined node therefore correctly shows Advertised 0, and only starts announcing a /32 when a LoadBalancer service places a backend on it (externalTrafficPolicy: Local). grigri advertises two (192.168.193.3/32 transcoder-rabbit, 192.168.193.8/32 kanidm-ldaps) because it hosts those backends. So the consequence of a down session is narrow but real: any LoadBalancer VIP that lands on the node would be unreachable from the network.

Two things that look like failures and are not:

  • Pinging a pod IP from the LAN fails on every node — pod IPs are not advertised by design. Use cilium bgp peers, not a pod ping, as the test.
  • Received can differ between nodes (0 on a new peer vs 9 on grigri). Neither node installs the received prefixes into its kernel routing table — both have 7 routes and reach the router via DHCP — so the difference is cosmetic. To make it match, give the new pfSense neighbour the same peer-group and address-family settings as the existing ones.

Note: cilium bgp peers prints a deprecation notice suggesting cilium shell bgp/peers; both work. cilium bgp routes accepts only available / advertised — there is no received subcommand.

docs.title: The node is briefly Ready,SchedulingDisabled — this is normal
docs.text:
The k3s-agent system-upgrade Plan (namespace system-upgrade) has cordon: true and selects every worker (node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane DoesNotExist). Immediately after joining, the node shows Ready,SchedulingDisabled with taint node.kubernetes.io/unschedulable:NoSchedule. An apply-k3s-agent-on-<node>-... job runs; because the node already has the target k3s version, the job compares sha256 of /opt/k3s against /host/usr/local/bin/k3s, logs [INFO] Binary already been replaced, exits 0, and the controller uncordons. This clears in under a minute. The node ends up labelled plan.upgrade.cattle.io/k3s-agent, so it is not re-upgraded.

Do NOT uncordon by hand. The Ansible-managed /etc/rancher/k3s/config.yaml and /etc/systemd/system/k3s.service are untouched during this process.

docs.title: Time sync must point at pfsense.grigri
docs.text:
Verify with chronyc sources (26.04/chrony) or ntpq -pn (22.04/24.04 ntpsec) — the output should show 192.168.192.1, matching prusik and grigri.

If make cluster fails partway through the play, handlers run at the end are discarded, so the chrony/ntp daemon keeps its distro config in memory even though the config file on disk is correct. This is sticky: a re-run sees the file unchanged, notifies no handler, and never reloads. Recovery: force a handler run or restart the daemon manually. See docs/troubleshooting/ansible-limit-cross-host-facts.md for the full explanation of the handler-discard mechanism.

Warning

On a no-ZFS node, zfs-localpv-node is 2/2 Running with zero restarts even though the node has no pool and the zpool binary is not installed — it only fails when actually asked to provision or mount a volume. A green DaemonSet is not evidence the node can serve PVCs. The allowedTopologies exclusion in system/zfs-localpv/templates/storage-class-openebs-zfspv.yaml is the only thing preventing durable PVCs from binding to a no-ZFS node.

Warning

A PVC with no storageClassName silently inherits the cluster default openebs-zfspv, whose allowedTopologies list only grigri and prusik — on a no-ZFS node such a PVC stays Pending forever instead of failing loudly. This is deliberate: no local StorageClass exists by decision (a system/local-path/ chart was considered and dropped — a StorageClass is an advertisement for unbacked, unquoted storage on a weak node). The silent Pending footgun is guarded by a PersistentVolumeClaimPending PrometheusRule at system/monitoring/resources/storage-prometheus-rules.yaml (warning after 10m) and PersistentVolumeClaimLost (critical after 5m). Node-local storage exceptions should use hostPath with type: Directory and directories created from metal/ via Ansible, not a StorageClass. k3s' bundled local-storage is disabled (metal/roles/k3s/defaults/main.yml:8-12).

docs.title: Scoped Ansible runs and cross-host facts
docs.text: All make prepare / make cluster runs must be scoped with --limit. Scoped runs break on templates that read another host's gathered facts (hostvars[x].ansible_hostname), because --limit removes the control plane from every play and delegate_to does not gather delegate facts. This was fixed in commit 1c3f5a48. See docs/troubleshooting/ansible-limit-cross-host-facts.md for the full explanation and the second symptom (handler discard on a discarded play).

docs.title: Remove a node
docs.text:
Danger

It is recommended to remove nodes one at a time

Warning

Removing a host from metal/inventory/hosts.ini only stops Ansible from targeting it — it does not stop k3s on the box itself. If the machine is still running with /etc/rancher/node/password on disk, it will silently rejoin the cluster on the next boot. Always drain, uninstall k3s on the node, and delete the Node object before touching the inventory.

  1. Drain the node:
kubectl drain ${NODE_NAME} --delete-emptydir-data --ignore-daemonsets --force
  1. Uninstall k3s on the node itself (still in the inventory at this point):
cd metal
ANSIBLE_EXTRA_ARGS="--limit ${NODE_NAME}" make uninstall-k3s

metal/playbooks/uninstall/k3s.yml stops/disables the k3s service, kills leftover container/kubelet processes, unmounts /run/k3s and /var/lib/rancher/k3s, and removes /usr/local/bin/k3s, /etc/rancher/k3s, /etc/rancher/node (the cluster join token) and the systemd unit. This repo installs k3s from a downloaded binary, so upstream's k3s-agent-uninstall.sh/k3s-killall.sh do not exist on the node — this playbook is the equivalent.

  1. Remove the node from the cluster (this also garbage-collects its <node>.node-password.k3s secret in kube-system):
kubectl delete node ${NODE_NAME}
  1. Now remove it from the inventory, and delete its host_vars/ file if it has one:
diff --git a/metal/inventory/hosts.ini b/metal/inventory/hosts.ini
--- a/metal/inventory/hosts.ini
+++ b/metal/inventory/hosts.ini
@@ -7,7 +7,6 @@
 [amd64_node]
 grigri
-k8s-amd64-1

Commit and let ArgoCD/Ansible converge.

  1. Shutdown the node:
ssh ${NODE_NAME} poweroff

docs.title: PostgreSQL Configuration
docs.text:
Optimizing Full-text search in PostgreSQL for FreshRSS involves adding indexes. This can significantly improve search performance without modifying FreshRSS' code (which uses ILIKE).

First, ensure you have the pg_trgm extension installed:

CREATE EXTENSION pg_trgm;

Then, create the necessary indexes for title and content:

CREATE INDEX gin_trgm_index_title ON "freshrss_entry" USING gin(title gin_trgm_ops);
CREATE INDEX gin_trgm_index_content ON "freshrss_entry" USING gin(content gin_trgm_ops);

Replace "freshrss_entry" with the appropriate entry name (e.g., freshrss_alice_entry).

For faster searches on authors (e.g., author:Alice), add another index:

CREATE INDEX gin_trgm_index_author ON freshrss_entry USING gin(author gin_trgm_ops);

Repeat this process for other text fields as needed. Refer to the CREATE TABLE _entry section for the list of fields.
