docs.title: 3. The Kiais stream quirk, exactly
docs.text:
One raw streamed tool call from Kiais fast (observed, served by kimi-k2.5 on alibaba-coding-plan at the time): the first chunk carries role, id (functions.intent__HassTurnOn:0), index 0, type and the full name; every following chunk again carries the full name and type, and id as an empty string, plus the next piece of arguments; the last chunk has an empty delta and finish_reason: tool_calls. OpenAI sends the name and id only in the first chunk.

What this breaks, by parser:

  • A parser that concatenates every name piece (name += delta.name) gets intent__HassTurnOnintent__HassTurnOn... and the tool call fails (this is what broke the first version of the evaluation harness).
  • A parser that overwrites the id whenever the field is present (id = delta.id, not checking for an empty string) ends with an empty tool call id.
  • llama_cpp (core) is not affected (documented and verified): it takes id and name from the first chunk of each index and only appends arguments for later chunks of the same index. litellm does not stream, so it never sees the chunks. local_openai and kiais_conversation only take a name that differs and an id that is non-empty.
  • Residual risk in llama_cpp (documented, not triggered): it reads only tool_calls[0] of each chunk and stops at the first chunk with a finish_reason, so a backend that packs two tool calls into one chunk, or puts the last text in the finish_reason chunk, would lose data. Kiais sent the two calls of "Enciende la cafetera y la luz de la cocina" in separate chunks and both ran.

A gateway fix is still worth it for robustness, since other backends of the tier may behave differently: Kiais could normalise streamed tool calls to the OpenAI shape (send id, type and name only in the first chunk of each index, omit them afterwards). No component of ours is needed for that.

docs.title: 4. Local verification (throwaway Home Assistant)
docs.text:
Setup (deleted after each session: container, data directory, image, token, raw results):

  • Image ghcr.io/home-operations/home-assistant:2026.10.4@sha256:81271a8b... (the production digest), bound to 127.0.0.1:18123, data under /work/workspaces/kivi-ha-test (a few MB).
  • Onboarded in Spanish; template entities in the default areas Salón, Cocina, Dormitorio: "Luz del techo" (Salón, with brightness), "Lámpara de pie" (Salón, brightness), "Luz de la cocina", "Luz del techo" (Dormitorio, a duplicate name on purpose), "Cafetera" (switch, Cocina), "Persiana del salón" (cover with position), "Temperatura del salón" (sensor, 22.4 °C) and a weather entity "Casa" (cloudy, 17 °C).
  • Config entries against https://isidoro.grigri.cloud/v1, model fast, the same Spanish prompt and the Assist API. llama_cpp, kiais_conversation and (first session) local_openai: temperature 0.2; llama_cpp and ours: max tokens 300. litellm has no temperature or token option, so it ran with the gateway defaults. One pipeline per agent (es, no STT/TTS) with prefer_local_intents: true.
  • Each text ran through the real pipeline over the websocket (assist_pipeline/run, intent stage), so prefer_local_intents applied. TTFS is the time from sending the request to the first intent-progress event with answer text (what streaming TTS would start from), measured on the workstation over the public URL. Entity states were read after each turn.
  • Second session (comparison of the core integrations): the 17 turns twice for each of kiais_conversation, litellm and llama_cpp, in the order KC, LL, LC for run 1 and LC, LL, KC for run 2, back to back on the same instance.

Per phrase, TTFS in seconds, run 1 / run 2 of the second session:

Id Text llama_cpp litellm (no streaming) kiais_conversation Tools called Continue l1, l2, l3, t1, t5 Enciende la luz de la cocina; Apaga la lámpara de pie; ¿Qué hora es?; Pon la lámpara de pie al cuarenta por ciento; ¿Qué tiempo hace? local, at most 0.33 s for all agents local local - (built-in intents) no t2 Pon la persiana del salón a la mitad 2.30/2.03 2.64/2.91 2.70/2.08 intent__HassSetPosition no t3 Apágalo todo en la cocina 2.00/2.47 2.43/2.34 2.06/1.98 intent__HassTurnOff (area Cocina) no t4 ¿Está encendida la cafetera? 2.14/2.49 2.14/2.57 1.90/1.95 homeassistant__GetLiveContext no t6 ¿Qué temperatura hace en el salón? 2.02/2.03 3.22/2.38 1.94/2.48 homeassistant__GetLiveContext no t7 Enciende la cafetera y la luz de la cocina 3.01/2.70 2.88/3.44 2.84/2.58 intent__HassTurnOn twice no g1 ¿Cuál es la capital de Australia? 0.99/0.65 0.89/0.81 0.69/0.56 - no g2 Explícame en una frase qué es la fotosíntesis 0.68/0.71 2.07/2.03 0.56/0.72 - no v1 ¿Va a llover mañana? 0.61/0.68 1.72/1.48 0.66/0.59 - (says it cannot see forecasts) no f1 Enciende la luz del techo 0.71/0.72 1.34/1.34 0.73/0.55 - (asks which room) yes f1b La del dormitorio 2.16/2.59 2.75/2.59 2.32/2.03 intent__HassTurnOn (Dormitorio) no f2 ¿Cuántos habitantes tiene Madrid, más o menos? 0.60/0.74 1.90/1.60 0.59/0.56 - no f2b ¿Y Barcelona? 0.73/0.72 1.64/5.58 1.04/0.70 - (uses the previous turn) no

Summary over both runs (12 turns per group and agent; p50 / p95 / max in seconds):

Agent Tool turns TTFS Turns without tools TTFS Content deltas per answer Wrong action or error llama_cpp 2.23 / 2.84 / 3.01 0.71 / 0.85 / 0.99 7 to 52 none litellm 2.62 / 3.32 / 3.44 1.62 / 3.65 / 5.58 1 none kiais_conversation 2.07 / 2.76 / 2.84 0.62 / 0.87 / 1.04 7 to 52 none

Findings (verified unless marked):

  • prefer_local_intents works as documented: 5 of 17 turns were answered by built-in intents in at most 0.45 s (both sessions), with no Kiais request.
  • Device control: in every tool turn of every agent the arguments and the resulting states were right (blind at 50, Cocina all off, two devices on, the bedroom ceiling light after the follow-up; the 40 % light ended at brightness 102 of 255).
  • Streaming: llama_cpp and our component streamed every answer; litellm delivered each answer in one piece, so its TTFS equals the total time and long answers start 1.1 to 1.4 s later (g2, f2). For tool turns the difference is small, because the tool round dominates. Home Assistant starts streaming TTS only after more than 60 characters, and only when the TTS engine accepts streamed input (documented, assist_pipeline/default_pipeline.py); whether the production Wyoming Piper does was not checked.
  • Follow-up: the clarifying question ended in ?, so continue_conversation was true, and the next turn acted on the answer (f1/f1b) in all agents; the topic follow-up (f2b) used the history.
  • llama_cpp and our component are within noise of each other (inferred: medians 0.1 to 0.2 s apart on one backend). First session, for reference: local_openai tool-turn TTFS p50 3.47 s and kiais_conversation 2.13 s, with single outliers in both.
  • No errors or warnings from any of the integrations in the Home Assistant log.
  • Not tested: timers (offered only to a satellite device), the satellite's area context (text runs had no device, hence the "which room?" question), calendar, behaviour when the gateway fails or hangs, real entity names.

docs.title: Deployed 2026-11-05
docs.text:
Done through Home Assistant's config-flow REST API and the websocket API with a short-lived login token (deleted afterwards); no git, chart or cluster change.

  • Config entry llama_cpp, title http://isidoro.isidoro:8080/v1 (in-cluster URL), the existing Kiais client key (kept only in Home Assistant's .storage), model fast. The setup-time test detected streaming (streaming: true); the entry loaded.
  • Conversation subentry "Fast", entity conversation.fast: recommended settings off, "Control Home Assistant" = Assist, temperature 0.2, maximum tokens 300, top_p 1, and the prompt below. It differs from the earlier draft in two lines: live data (time, weather, calendar, device states) must come from the tools or the answer is "I don't know", and a clarifying question must be the whole answer. With the earlier wording the model added a sentence after its question, so the answer did not end in ? and Home Assistant did not keep listening (observed twice).
  • Pipeline "Kiwi": conversation_engine conversation.qwen2_5_3b → conversation.fast, prefer_local_intents false → true. Read back and compared with the snapshot taken before: no other field changed (language es, faster-whisper, Piper es_ES-sharvard-medium, wake word unchanged). "Kiwi Test", the other agents, exposure and aliases were not touched.
Eres Kivi, el asistente de voz de esta casa. Tu nombre se escribe «Kivi» y se pronuncia «kivi».
Habla siempre en español de España, de forma amable y directa. Tus respuestas se leen en voz alta,
así que usa una o dos frases cortas en texto plano: nada de markdown, listas, asteriscos, emojis,
enlaces ni símbolos como ° o %; di «grados» y «por ciento».
Para controlar o consultar la casa usa siempre las herramientas, y confirma en pocas palabras solo
lo que de verdad se ha hecho; si una herramienta falla, dilo.
No inventes nunca datos en tiempo real (el tiempo, la hora, el calendario, el estado de los
dispositivos, noticias o tráfico): consúltalos con las herramientas o di que no lo sabes.
Si la petición es ambigua, contesta únicamente con una pregunta corta que acabe en «?», por ejemplo
«¿En qué habitación?»; no enumeres opciones ni añadas nada después.
Las preguntas generales respóndelas con tus conocimientos, de forma breve y útil.

Verification (observed on production, text only, no audio, no TTS, no action commands; times measured on the workstation over the public Home Assistant URL; repeated runs span the prompt revisions):

Path Text Result Time /api/conversation/process, agent conversation.fast ¿Cuál es la capital de Portugal? "Lisboa." 1.0 to 2.0 s (3 runs) same ¿Cómo te llamas? "Me llamo Kivi." 0.8 to 1.7 s (3 runs) same ¿Qué temperatura hace en el salón? the living-room sensor's value in degrees (tool call) 2.8 to 3.4 s (3 runs) same ¿Está encendida la luz? "¿En qué habitación?", continue_conversation true 1.2 s same ¿Qué temperatura hace? every room's temperature, then a question; continue_conversation true 3.9 s (long answer) assist_pipeline/run, pipeline Kiwi, intent stage only ¿Qué hora es? processed_locally true, built-in intent 0.42 s same ¿Cuál es la capital de Portugal? processed_locally false, conversation.fast, streamed first delta 0.88 s, end 1.0 s same Explícame en una frase qué es la fotosíntesis same, one sentence, streamed first delta 0.86 s, end 2.0 s

No llama_cpp errors or warnings in the Home Assistant log. Still open: the satellite end to end (STT, TTS, area context), action commands with the real entity names, the multi-room temperature answer (correct but long, with digits), and the open questions below.

Rollback (instant, no restart; the pipeline object before the change is kept in a private snapshot outside this repository):

  1. Settings > Voice assistants > Kiwi, or assist_pipeline/pipeline/update with every field as read back: conversation agent conversation.qwen2_5_3b, prefer_local_intents false.
  2. Delete the llama.cpp entry http://isidoro.isidoro:8080/v1 in Settings > Devices & services.
  3. If needed, rotate the Kiais key it used.

docs.title: Deployment steps (as approved)
docs.text:
No GitOps change is needed: llama_cpp is part of Home Assistant core and its requirement (openai==3.10.0) ships in the image.

Prerequisite: a Kiais API key for Home Assistant (a separate key, so it can be revoked or attributed on its own). It is entered once in the config flow and kept in Home Assistant's .storage; it never goes into git.

Home Assistant UI (live changes, each one needs the owner's yes):

  1. Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > llama.cpp: server URL http://isidoro.isidoro:8080/v1 (in-cluster; reachable from the pod, observed: GET /v1/models 200 in 8 ms), the API key; model fast. The flow sends two short test requests (with a test tool, 3 tokens) and records whether streaming works; it creates a conversation agent "Fast".
  2. Reconfigure that agent: untick "Recommended settings", prompt as below, "Control Home Assistant" = Assist, temperature 0.2, maximum tokens 300, top_p 1.
  3. Settings > Voice assistants > Kiwi: Conversation agent = the llama.cpp "Fast" agent; turn on "Prefer handling commands locally"; leave language, STT, TTS and wake word as they are.
  4. Settings > Voice assistants > Expose: review which entities are exposed and give them Spanish aliases; the LLM sees all exposed names and areas (privacy, and the accuracy of both the built-in intents and the LLM depend on them).

Spanish prompt (the same text as the prototype's default in const.py, line breaks added here for reading; Home Assistant appends its own Assist instructions and the exposed-entity context):

Eres Kivi, el asistente de voz de esta casa. Tu nombre se escribe «Kivi» y se pronuncia «kivi».
Habla siempre en español de España, de forma amable y directa. Tus respuestas se leen en voz alta,
así que usa una o dos frases cortas en texto plano: nada de markdown, listas, asteriscos, emojis,
enlaces ni símbolos como ° o %; di «grados» y «por ciento».
Para controlar la casa usa siempre las herramientas, y confirma en pocas palabras solo lo que de
verdad se ha hecho; si una herramienta falla, dilo. Si la orden es ambigua, haz una pregunta corta.
Si te piden datos en tiempo real que no puedes consultar con tus herramientas (noticias, bolsa,
tráfico, resultados deportivos, previsiones), di claramente que no puedes consultarlos. No inventes
nunca datos.
Las preguntas generales respóndelas con tus conocimientos, de forma breve.

docs.title: Fallback: deploying kiais_conversation by GitOps
docs.text:
Only if a gap of llama_cpp above matters. Move the component into the chart (git mv scripts/voice-assistant/custom_components/kiais_conversation apps/home-assistant/custom_components/kiais_conversation), add apps/home-assistant/templates/configmap-kiais-conversation.yaml:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: home-assistant-kiais-conversation
data:
# translations/en.json becomes the key en.json; the volume items put it back in place
{{ (.Files.Glob "custom_components/kiais_conversation/*").AsConfig | indent 2 }}
{{ (.Files.Glob "custom_components/kiais_conversation/translations/*").AsConfig | indent 2 }}

and under app-template.persistence in values.yaml:

    kiais-conversation:
      enabled: true
      type: configMap
      name: home-assistant-kiais-conversation
      items:
        - key: __init__.py
          path: __init__.py
        - key: config_flow.py
          path: config_flow.py
        - key: const.py
          path: const.py
        - key: conversation.py
          path: conversation.py
        - key: manifest.json
          path: manifest.json
        - key: strings.json
          path: strings.json
        - key: en.json
          path: translations/en.json
      advancedMounts:
        hass:
          hass:
            - path: /config/custom_components/kiais_conversation
              readOnly: true

Checked in a scratch copy of the chart (helm template renders the seven keys and the read-only mount; helm lint passes), and a read-only mount of the component loaded in the throwaway Home Assistant. Reloader restarts Home Assistant when the ConfigMap changes. Then add "Kiais Conversation" in the UI (URL, key, model fast; options: prompt, Assist, 0.2, 300, timeout 30, history 10) and select it in the pipeline.

docs.title: Smoke test after each Home Assistant upgrade
docs.text: Repeat section 4 with the new image: a throwaway container on 127.0.0.1, the same entities and 17 turns through assist_pipeline/run (about 20 Kiais requests per agent and run), checking the entity states, the content deltas and the log; then delete everything.

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
• Pipeline: set "Kiwi" back to its previous agent (conversation.qwen2_5_3b) and its previous prefer_local_intents (off). Instant, no restart.
  • Integration: delete the llama.cpp entry in Settings > Devices & services.
  • Revoke the Home Assistant Kiais key.
  • Nothing else is touched: no git change, no new Python packages, no HACS state, no change to OPENAI_BASE_URL.

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text: Every utterance that is not handled locally, the prompt, the names and areas of all exposed entities and, when a tool runs, their live state go to Kiais and then to whichever provider serves fast (Alibaba and others, see the agent evaluation). The owner approved sending requests to Kiais. prefer_local_intents keeps the simple commands at home. llama_cpp logs request chunks only at debug level; keep debug logging off for homeassistant.components.llama_cpp and conversation.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. ~~Owner: approve the UI steps above (core llama_cpp, no code to own)?~~ Approved and deployed 2026-11-05.
  2. A Kiais key for Home Assistant: how it is issued in Kiais (not found in the custom resources).
  3. Kiais: normalise streamed tool calls to the OpenAI shape (section 3), and say whether its session affinity can use the user field, which llama_cpp and litellm set to the conversation id.
  4. Live information: weather now works through HassGetWeather and GetLiveContext; forecasts and calendar need exposed calendars and a forecast script exposed as a tool (next step).
  5. End-to-end latency through the satellite (STT, TTS, network), and whether the production Piper accepts streamed TTS input.
  6. Behaviour of llama_cpp when Kiais hangs or fails (SDK 600 s timeout); test with a controlled fault before relying on it.
  7. Re-check the built-in-intents hit rate with the real entity names and aliases.

docs.title: Lessons learned
docs.text: One entry per pitfall met while building the voice assistant: what it looked like, why it happened, how it was found, what fixed it, and what now guards against a repeat.

docs.title: Wake word: the server's features are not the training features
docs.text:
• Symptom: offline scores of a custom openWakeWord model disagreed with the server for the same clip, from 0.004 to 0.96. Model selection and threshold estimates based on them were wrong in both directions.
  • Root cause: openWakeWord's melspectrogram model ends with a ReduceMax over its whole input tensor and clamps the log-mel at max - 80 dB. The server (wyoming-openwakeword 2.x, pyopen-wakeword) calls it on one 1760-sample chunk at a time, so the floor is set per 80 ms. Batch extraction (AudioFeatures.embed_clips, used for training and typical offline evaluation) sets the floor from the loudest sample of the whole batch.
  • How detected: clip-by-clip comparison of the batched path against pyopen-wakeword streaming showed agreement for some voices and large gaps for others. A per-chunk TFLite run matched the server exactly, and the ONNX graph showed the ReduceMax.
  • Fix: scripts/voice-assistant/wakeword/stream_mel.py makes the max per batch row. fast_eval.py embed --stream-onnx then feeds the server's 1760-sample chunks with its frame and window bookkeeping. This matches streaming to 0.032 in the embeddings and 0.002 in the score.
  • Guard: scripts/voice-assistant/wakeword/test_server_exact_features.py checks streaming against batched (tolerance 0.05) and that plain batch features differ. fast_report.py refuses embeddings not tagged server-exact. Details: kivi wake word, Pitfalls.

docs.title: Wake word: default augmentation buries a short word
docs.text:
• Symptom: with the official openWakeWord recipe (train.py, auto_train), every "kivi" model collapsed to 2-9 % recall, even on its own training positives.
  • Root cause: augment_clips mixes background at -10 to +15 dB SNR computed over the whole 2 s padded window. For a 0.45 s word, many positives end up at or below 0 dB on the word. auto_train then raises the negative weight to 1500x or more, which pushes every output down.
  • How detected: ablations on cached features. A plain classifier on clean positives reached 98 % held-out recall at about 1 false window per hour, on noisy positives 43 %, and with the near-word negatives 15 %. The word-to-background amplitude ratio of augmented positives was 1.0 to 2.4.
  • Fix: augment with the SNR measured against the word (5 to 30 dB). Train the same DNN head with a fixed small negative weight and mined hard negatives (augment_set.py --mode simple, train_simple.py, fast_eval.py mine).
  • Guard: the training history logs validation recall at fixed false accepts. kivi wake word, Training records the choice.

docs.title: Wake word: digital silence in the evaluation clips decides which model wins
docs.text:
• Symptom: models trained on server-exact features (the "cheapest next step" of v1) scored far below v1 on v1's held-out clips (clean recall 0.1 to 23 % against 67 % at the same false accepts on MLS dev), whatever the negatives were. One of them reached 99.5 % on the same clips once they had a noise floor.
  • Root cause: v1's evaluation clips (and v1's long-audio pads) contain exact zeros around the word. The server clamps the log-mel per 80 ms chunk at max - 80 dB, so an all-zero chunk gives features that no real microphone produces (the satellites' quietest 80 ms frames are -75 to -50 dBFS after the front-end). A model that never saw digital silence misfires on it; v1 was trained with batch features, where zeros are clamped against the loud part of the batch, and happens to cope. The test measured the padding, not the word.
  • How detected: the same candidate scored 35/1 800 on the zero-padded clips and 1 791/1 800 on the same clips with a -62 to -48 dBFS white floor through the front-end (v2_augment.py eval).
  • Fix: every v2 training and evaluation clip carries a mic floor calibrated on real satellite audio and goes through the satellite front-end; v1 and v2 are compared on those features. v1's zero-padded set is still reported, labelled as such.
  • Guard: v2_augment.py adds the floor by default; its docstring explains why.

docs.title: Wake word: the server-exact training window cut the end of the word
docs.text:
• Symptom: part of the same v2 shortfall; positives were labelled on a window that did not contain the whole word.
  • Root cause: augment_set.py --stream-onnx places the word end 0-200 ms before the end of a 40 960-sample window, but the last of the 16 server embeddings only sees audio up to sample 39 360 (31 whole 1 280-sample chunks, the last embedding ending 4 mel frames before the chunk end). About half of the positives lost up to 100 ms of the final vowel.
  • How detected: a 10 ms noise burst moved along the window changes the last embedding only up to sample 39 360 (v2 diagnostic diag_rf.py).
  • Fix: v2_augment.py train uses a 40 160-sample window and puts the word end 0-200 ms before sample 39 280.
  • Guard: the constants TOTAL and LAST_AUDIO in v2_augment.py, with the measurement in their comment.

docs.title: Whisper: --debug logs the whole argument namespace, including the Home Assistant token
docs.text:
• Symptom: none yet. Found while designing how to log transcripts for the usage study.
  • Root cause: wyoming-faster-whisper prints its parsed argument namespace at DEBUG, and --debug turns DEBUG on for every library. With --hass-token read from WYO_WHISPER_HASS_TOKEN_FILE, the namespace carries the Home Assistant token (an administrator token: Home Assistant tokens have no scopes), and it would reach the pod log and Loki.
  • How detected: reading the server source and the first canary design, which suggested --debug to see the composed prompt and transcripts.
  • Fix: never run the production pod with --debug. The transcript logger is lowered to DEBUG on its own, from apps/home-assistant/config/whisper-logging/sitecustomize.py (loaded through PYTHONPATH): root logger at INFO, only wyoming_faster_whisper.dispatch_handler at DEBUG.
  • Guard: the per-logger sitecustomize.py is the only way DEBUG is enabled; its header says why. whisper-image-build.md and the log policy forbid pasting --debug output.

docs.title: Whisper: wyoming-faster-whisper 3.8.1 renamed the transcript logger, which silently broke the Vector drop regex
docs.text:
• Symptom: none visible. The Vector rule that drops voice transcripts before Loki stopped matching after the 3.8.1 image: a regex written for INFO:wyoming_faster_whisper.handler: no longer matched the new line, so the filter would have let transcripts through without any error.
  • Root cause: 3.8.1 logs the transcript from dispatch_handler.py as DEBUG:wyoming_faster_whisper.dispatch_handler:<text> (2.x: INFO:...handler:<text>). The filter matched only handler.
  • How detected: reading the 3.8.1 source while preparing the image, before the cutover.
  • Fix: the drop_voice_transcripts condition in system/loki/vector-agent.yaml is now ^(INFO|DEBUG):wyoming_faster_whisper\.(dispatch_)?handler:.
  • Guard: the Vector unit tests in the same file (whisper_transcript_line_is_dropped, whisper_debug_transcript_line_is_dropped, whisper_dispatch_handler_transcript_line_is_dropped) cover the three line shapes with synthetic text. Run vector test after any Whisper version change. A logger rename is a privacy change.

docs.title: STT: GTX 1060 (sm_61) offers only float32, int8 and int8_float32 in CTranslate2
docs.text:
• Symptom: large-v3-turbo does not fit or does not run fast with the usual precisions.
  • Root cause: on Pascal sm_61 CTranslate2 lists only float32, int8 and int8_float32 as supported compute types (no usable float16). float32 large-v3-turbo does not fit in the card's 3 GB next to the display and other users (about 1.1 GiB is used by the int8 model).
  • How detected: ctranslate2.get_supported_compute_types("cuda") on the target card and the documented CTranslate2 quantisation table; VRAM read from the GPU exporter.
  • Fix: run --compute-type int8 (executed as int8_float32). The same limit makes small fp16 models slow on this card; the decision-model study ran fp32.
  • Guard: the canary step in whisper-image-build.md prints the supported compute types and fails on CUDA kernel errors before the real STT is touched, and the registry records the precision of every model.

docs.title: Home Assistant: assist_pipeline: debug_recording_dir records continuous room audio with no cap or expiry
docs.text:
• Symptom: none yet; found while enabling request audio for Whisper fine-tuning and front-end work.
  • Root cause: with a server-side wake word every pipeline run starts at the wake word stage, so the debug recording writes every chunk the satellites stream, continuously (about 115 MB per listening hour per satellite), not just the speech after a wake. Home Assistant has no size limit or expiry for that directory.
  • How detected: reading the assist_pipeline debug recording code and the run layout (00_wake-*.wav, 01_stt-*.wav).
  • Fix: a dedicated 500 GiB volume outside /config and /media, enabled only on the owner's approval, with a daily cleanup.
  • Guard: the CronJob home-assistant-voice-recordings-cleanup (90 days from the last write, oldest runs first above 90 % use) and rows 5 and 6 of the data register, which state what is recorded and who may read it.

docs.title: Home Assistant: .storage/homeassistant.exposed_entities shows only manual overrides
docs.text:
• Symptom: reading the file suggested 0 entities were exposed to Assist, when 113 were.
  • Root cause: the file stores only manual exposure overrides; entities exposed by default are not listed.
  • How detected: the count differed from the websocket answer.
  • Fix: use the websocket command homeassistant/expose_entity/list, as Whisper's name list and the analysis scripts do (it needs an administrator token).
  • Guard: STT hint list names the websocket call as the source of exposed entities; never infer exposure from .storage.

docs.title: Whisper logs: most DEBUG lines are "Sent info" replies, not voice traffic
docs.text:
• Symptom: about 90 % of the Whisper DEBUG lines looked like activity, so request counts from line counts were far too high.
  • Root cause: Home Assistant polls the server with a Wyoming describe request regularly, and each reply logs "Sent info".
  • How detected: counting line kinds in the pod log (counts only, no text read).
  • Fix: count requests with the "Audio stopped" line, one per utterance.
  • Guard: the analysis scripts count "Audio stopped", and the data register describes the stream's contents so counts are not taken from raw line totals.

docs.title: Forgejo: building and pushing the Whisper image
docs.text:
• Symptom: four separate failures in the first runs of the image workflow in agil/wyoming-whisper.
  • Root cause and fix:
  • Repository secret names cannot start with FORGEJO_ (reserved prefix), so the planned FORGEJO_PACKAGES_PAT was rejected. Use another prefix.
  • The automatic Actions token cannot push packages. A dedicated personal access token with only write:package is needed; it is created and set by the owner and kept in pass.
  • The 1.64 GB layer push timed out. The push step needs a retry loop.
  • The package cleanup rule (keep the last 3 versions) can only be set in the web UI, not by API.
  • How detected: failed workflow runs and the registry responses.
  • Guard: the workflow in the image repository carries the retry loop, the owner's checklist in whisper-image-build.md lists the token and the UI-only rule, and the image is pinned by digest in apps/home-assistant/values.yaml.

docs.title: Workstation: load stalls evaluations and a broad pkill killed other sessions' workers
docs.text:
• Symptom: evaluation runs slowed to a crawl and timed out, and a cleanup killed Python workers that belonged to other sessions.
  • Root cause: the workstation is shared by several sessions. Under load (average 100 to 200) CPU-heavy evaluations stall, and a pkill with a generic pattern matches every Python worker, not just the caller's.
  • How detected: load average and the other sessions' runs failing at the same moment.
  • Fix: cap the worker count of every evaluation, and stop jobs by PID or process group only.
  • Guard: rule for all sessions: never use a generic pkill/killall pattern. Start long jobs in their own process group and record the PID, so cleanup targets only that group.

docs.title: Whisper: the GTX 1060 cannot host a second Whisper instance
docs.text:
• Symptom: during a Whisper settings benchmark (2026-11-05, 18:45-18:53 UTC), live STT requests failed with CUDA out of memory and then "invalid device ordinal"; 67 of about 190 live requests took more than 5 s (up to 47 s) instead of about 0.9 s. A live AEC experiment on a TV was running at the same time and its transcript-based results were contaminated.
  • Root cause: the benchmark assumed the live Whisper was idle and that a second large-v3-turbo int8 instance (peak about 1.8 GiB) fits next to the live one (about 1.1 GiB) on the 3 GiB card. The card reached 2967 of 3072 MiB, and the live service was not idle.
  • How detected: the live Whisper log showed the CUDA errors; request latencies were split by overlap with the benchmark using log timestamps only (whisper_bench/live_overlap.py).
  • Fix: the benchmark pod was deleted; the live service recovered without a restart.
  • Guard: never run a second GPU model on the 1060 while the live service runs. Benchmark on the workstation GPU for accuracy, or schedule a short announced outage (live Whisper scaled to 0) for 1060 latency numbers, and check that no live experiment is using voice at the time.

docs.title: Wake word: fetching a licence-restricted model with an ad-hoc token and bot user
docs.text:
• Symptom: the first kivi deployment (2026-11-05) fetched kivi.tflite from the private repository with curl in an init container. It needed a dedicated Forgejo bot user, a read:repository token, a Vault entry, an ExternalSecret and a PVC cache so that restarts did not depend on Forgejo. The owner called it a workaround; the bot and the Vault entry were removed the same evening.
  • Root cause: the model was treated as a file to download, not as an artifact to ship. The cluster already pulls private images from git.grigri.cloud with the nodes' containerd credential (metal/roles/k3s/templates/host.toml.j2), so an image needs no new credential at all.
  • Second pitfall found on the way: a Forgejo package takes the visibility of its owner, not of its repository. While the user agil was public, git.grigri.cloud/agil/<name> images could be pulled anonymously even when the repository was private (checked: an anonymous pull of agil/wyoming-whisper resolved). The owner set agil to "limited" on 2026-11-05; since then anonymous pulls of its packages are refused. A detour through a private organisation is not needed.
  • How detected: owner review of the first design; the anonymous pull test before publishing the model image.
  • Fix: the model is published as a private image git.grigri.cloud/agil/kivi-models:<version>, linked to the repository and built by its workflow on a version tag, pinned by tag and digest in GitOps; an init container copies it into an emptyDir. No token, Vault entry, bot or PVC.
  • Guard: prefer a private image pulled with the existing node credential for any licence-restricted file the cluster needs. Keep the owner agil limited (or private) and check an anonymous pull is refused after every release (the agil/kivi-models README says so).

docs.title: Wake word: indexing an .npz inside a loop re-reads the whole array and ran out of memory
docs.text:
• Symptom: the first Kivi v3 feature job was killed about 30 s after it started, with no Python error in its log. The user journal showed The kernel OOM killer killed some processes in this unit for the systemd-run scope (20 GB cap, 20 GB peak).
  • Root cause: np.load("takes.npz") returns an NpzFile, and each T["audio"][i] decompresses the whole 27 MB array again. The slice is a view, so every one of the 16 600 augmentation items kept its own full copy alive.
  • How detected: journalctl --user for the scope (Failed with result 'oom-kill'), then the one T["audio"][i] per item in the list comprehension.
  • Fix: load the arrays once ({k: v.copy() for k, v in np.load(...).items()}) and copy each take out.
  • Guard: the comment on that line in v3_real.py feats. Jobs run under MemoryMax, so a repeat stops the job, not the shared workstation.
