docs.title: How to register a model
docs.text:
A model is deployed only after its registry row exists with its sha256 and server-exact scores.

  1. Measure it with the features and runtime the cluster uses (for wake words, the server-exact pyopen-wakeword path; see lessons learned) and write the experiment document first.
  2. Store the file: a publishable file by version in the image or package registry; a licence-restricted file in the private repository agil/kivi-models with a model card, licence notes and SHA256SUMS (the repository README explains the layout).
  3. Add the row here: role, model, version, short sha256 of the served file, precision, where it runs, deployed (leave "No" until the owner approves), threshold and key settings, scores with a link to the experiment, licence, storage location.
  4. Only then open the GitOps change. After the rollout, update "Deployed? (since)" and keep the previous row's rollback version.

docs.title: Kivi plan
docs.text: Last updated 2026-11-05.

docs.title: 1. Goal
docs.text: A Spanish voice assistant, "Kivi" (Home Assistant pipeline "Kiwi"), with low latency and high accuracy on home commands. General questions, live information and follow-ups are routed to Kiais. The MVP is home control; everything else is a later improvement.

docs.title: 2. Current architecture (live 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
satellite (LG webOS TV, ESPHome API)
  -> HA openWakeWord (wake word still `alexa`)
  -> Whisper large-v3-turbo int8 on the GTX 1060
       custom image agil/wyoming-whisper 3.8.1.1, verbs prompt + live HA names
  -> HA built-in intents first (prefer_local_intents)
  -> miss: Kiais fast, through the core llama_cpp integration
  -> Piper TTS
Measure Value Whisper latency, p50 0.91 s Local (built-in intent) commands, end to end about 1 s Kiais commands about 4.1 s Kiais general questions about 2.3 s (first words about 0.9 s) Verbs prompt, clean synthetic audio 82 to 88% correct Verbs prompt, synthetic audio at 0 dB SNR 46 to 57% correct

The accuracy rows come from synthetic Spanish audio, not real household use; see Small local models and STT hint list. Detail on each part: Conversation agent evaluation, Kiais as the conversation agent, Conversation agent design, Whisper image build.

docs.title: 3. Decisions log (2026-11-05)
docs.text: Decision Why Core llama_cpp integration to reach Kiais, not litellm or an own component Least to maintain; verified with prefer_local_intents (Kiais integration). The verbs prompt ships with the custom Whisper image; the verbs-only fallback on 2.4.0 is not needed The canary passed and 3.8.1.1 is live (image build). No local fallback LLM Kiais availability is treated as Home Assistant's own (Decisions 2026-11-05). No small LLM on the GTX 1060 (router, STT corrector or home agent) Rejected by measurement (Small local models). Transcripts re-enabled in Loki for the Whisper stream, 180-day retention Needed to validate against real usage; see section 5. No audio collection for now Superseded the same day by the next row. Audio collection on (owner approval 2026-11-05): Home Assistant keeps the audio of every pipeline run for 90 days, including the continuous wake-stage room audio while the satellites listen Real household audio for wake word, AEC / front-end and speech-to-text work. Cluster storage only, no backup, agents see counts and sizes only; section 5 and the data register (datasets 5 and 6). Local models only for any decision model; no cloud API Privacy; no household text leaves the cluster or the workstation.

docs.title: 4. Workstreams
docs.text: Workstream Status Next step Gate / decision owner a Wake word "Kivi" Training Retrain with word-level SNR augmentation, evaluate against alexa Owner approves deploy b Whisper Done (3.8.1.1 live) Confirm the hint-list effect on real commands Owner provides real commands c Real-usage validation Collecting Offline replay of the collected transcripts Owner reviews samples d Decision model ("Kivi decider") Validating value P0 zero-shot baselines and headroom analysis Headroom meaningful, then owner e Whisper fine-tuning Collecting audio (from 2026-11-05) Fine-tune only after the AEC work, on the collected request audio Owner (approved the collection 2026-11-05) f Later / backlog Not started See below Owner

docs.title: a. Wake word "Kivi"
docs.text:
• Custom model in openWakeWord format, trained on the workstation. Doc: Kivi wake word (in progress).
  • First runs collapsed: the default augmentation sets the SNR against the whole window, so the positives end up too noisy and the training pushes a huge weight on the negatives. Retraining with word-level SNR augmentation.
  • Baseline to beat, alexa on synthetic audio: recall 63% / 38% / 21% at clean / 10 dB / 0 dB; false accepts 0.2 to 0.4 per hour of Spanish speech.
  • Deploy needs the owner's approval. Rollback: set the satellite's wake_word_id back to alexa.

docs.title: b. Whisper
docs.text:
• Done: 3.8.1.1 live with the verbs prompt and live Home Assistant names.
  • Next: confirm the hint-list effect with the owner's real commands; investigate the "Pon" heard as "Con" error; Renovate on the private image repository; manual image bumps in this repository until then.

docs.title: c. Real-usage validation (data)
docs.text:
Transcripts stay in Loki for 180 days (section 5). Replay on the workstation uses derived datasets that are deleted at the end of the experiment, at most 30 days. Plan:

  1. Offline replay of the transcripts against Home Assistant's built-in sentences and the real entities.
  2. Measure the miss rate and classify each miss: misheard (STT), phrasing gap, other.
  3. Turn the classes into fixes: aliases, custom sentences, hint-list changes.

Log policy and the data register: Log policy, data register.

docs.title: d. Decision model ("Kivi decider")
docs.text:
Validate the value first; build nothing before there is headroom over the built-in intents.

utterance (STT text)
  -> HA built-in intents
       match: execute (about 1 s)
       miss:  Kivi decider (small local model)
                -> home command: execute the intent through HA
                -> everything else: Kiais (general questions, live info, follow-ups)
Phase What Detail P0 Zero-shot baselines: Laya, Quyet-1.0-Tiny, embedding + fuzzy matching Decision models (in progress) P0 Broader synthetic dataset kivi-fake-v1: fake homes, phrasing styles, negatives including TV dialogue; headroom analysis Decider PoC (in progress) P0 Real-usage replay after a few days of data (workstream c) P1 Data, only if headroom is meaningful P2 Fine-tune Quyet-1.0-Tiny; optional local teacher: pplx-decider-v1.1-27b (open weights) or Laya P3 Gates: wrong actions at most 0.5%; at least 50% of built-in misses rescued; p95 below 150 ms; at most 800 MB on the GTX 1060 (fp32, Pascal) Any miss of a gate stops the line P4 Integration: decider HTTP service plus a small Home Assistant custom conversation agent that delegates to Kiais; shadow mode first; structure borrowed from home-assistant-laya, not installed Owner approves each live step

docs.title: Related project: home-assistant-laya
docs.text:
allenporter/home-assistant-laya (Apache-2.0, read 2026-11-05 at 8803550, laya==0.4.24; source reading only, nothing installed or run) is a Home Assistant custom component (HACS) with a conversation agent entity around the same Laya model. It is the closest existing match for P4, but it is a prototype, not a base to run as is.

What it does (documented, from the source):

  • Pipeline. Selected as the pipeline's conversation agent. It builds a shortlist (at most 5 intents, 10 areas, 20 entities, lexical matching on names), asks one Laya forward pass five typed questions (intent, compound, target entity, target area, entity or area), and on a confident answer executes the HA intent (intent.async_handle, slots name, area, domain, brightness, temperature). On low confidence or a "compound" request it calls conversation.async_converse on a configured fallback agent, so a chain Laya, then Kiais is a config option. With prefer_local_intents the pipeline tries the built-in intents first (HA behaviour as in Kiais integration; not yet tried with this non-LLM agent, hypothesis until the shadow run).
  • Entities. Only those exposed to Assist (async_should_expose), but if none are exposed it silently uses all states. Controllable domains only.
  • Gate. Per-question probability of the chosen option against confidence_threshold 0.40 (the README describes a normalised formula, the code uses the raw probability) and compound_threshold 0.70. Our zero-shot study needed 0.6 to 0.85 and the threshold did not transfer between phrase sets (Decision models).
  • Hardware. In-process PyTorch in the HA executor via the laya package; the README quotes about 1.2 GB of RAM, 100 to 250 ms on a CUDA GPU and 1.5 to 3.0 s on CPU for a full home context (author estimates, not measured by us). idle_timeout defaults to 0, so the weights are unloaded after every request and reloaded on the next.

Why it does not fit as is:

  • No Spanish. The component calls laya.load() with no checkpoint, which is the English-only root checkpoint (ModernBERT-large); the multilingual one is never selected. Instructions, stopwords, the domain words and the number regexes (%, "degrees") are English; "grados" or "por ciento" are not parsed. Tests and the evaluation home are English only.
  • No evidence for our gates. No accuracy, wrong-action or rescue numbers; the benchmarks are the model card's latency. The slot set excludes volume and media actions, which we planned to cover.
  • Wrong-action risk by design. An area target with no domain word in the utterance is sent as area only (hypothesis: what HA does with it is unchecked).
  • Hard to deploy in our cluster. requirements makes HA pip-install laya (torch, transformers, and a new vegaml dependency) into the HA container; issue 6 reports the install failing on HA OS. Issue 7 (remote Laya service) is open without a reply.
  • Maturity. Created 2026-09-20, one release (0.1.0). The author's 45 commits are from 2026-09-20 and 21; since then only Renovate bumps (53 commits). 9 stars, 1 fork, 3 open issues. CI runs pytest, ruff, hassfest and HACS validation; about 900 lines of integration tests, speculative-engine unit tests and slow live tests on an English fake home. hacs.json says HA 2024.04 but the code uses the newer conversation entity API; unproven against our HA 2026.10.4.
  • Privacy and supply chain. Inference is local and the integration code makes no network calls of its own. HA installs laya from PyPI at runtime and the package downloads weights from Hugging Face on first load (revision pinned inside laya, safetensors and JSON only, no trust_remote_code). The integration passes no hash. Not reviewed: laya 0.4.24 beyond a read of load and serve; vegaml not reviewed at all.

What is reusable:

  • laya[serve] already ships an HTTP server (FastAPI, POST /v1/systemone and /batch, bearer key, idle unload, LAYA_THREADS, LAYA_MODELS to pick multilingual, LAYA_CUDA_AMP=fp32 to avoid fp16 autocast on Pascal). That covers the "decider HTTP service" half of P4 without code of ours, for Laya only (Quyet needs its own service).
  • DecisionEngine (speculative/scoring/engine.py) is a small abstract class (async_predict(state, questions)), so a RemoteEngine that calls the server over HTTP is roughly 60 lines. This is the change issue 7 asks for.
  • The 5-stage DecisionFlow (request, retrieval, hydration, scoring, resolution) and its fixtures are a useful reference for the HA side: exposure handling, intent introspection, originating-area prior, fallback via async_converse.

How it changes P4 (proposal, owner decides):

  1. Build our own thin HA agent for P4, borrowing the structure; do not install this component. Reasons: Spanish, our gates, shadow mode, our own question design and parsing (already measured in decision_models/) and the model choice are all ours, so the reusable part is the ~190-line conversation.py pattern and the DecisionEngine seam, both Apache-2.0 (keep the licence header and attribution if code is copied).
  2. Serve over HTTP outside HA: laya[serve] for Laya, a minimal service for Quyet; HA never imports torch.
  3. Add what is missing, in this order: Spanish number and domain parsing; the multilingual or fine-tuned checkpoint; a per-question threshold fitted on kivi-fake-v1 and real replay and checked on held-out phrases; a shadow mode (log the decision, always fall through to Kiais, no device action); no "all states" fallback; area-only targets rejected unless the domain is known; unload disabled (idle_timeout > 0 equivalent) so p95 can be measured.
  4. Contribute only small, upstreamable pieces if useful (remote engine for issue 7, a model option), after P3 says the line continues. There is no sign of maintainer activity beyond the first two days, so do not depend on upstream merges.
  5. Reference result, not a reason to skip P3. This project does not change the P0 finding: zero-shot Laya multilingual was near chance on action and area in Spanish; the component adds no fine-tuning or Spanish data. The P3 gates stay as they are.

docs.title: e. Whisper fine-tuning (audio collection started, fine-tuning later)
docs.text: Audio collection started on 2026-11-05 on the owner's approval: Home Assistant's assist_pipeline debug recording keeps the request audio and the continuous wake-stage room audio of every run for 90 days, on the cluster volume home-assistant-voice-recordings (data register, datasets 5 and 6). Fine-tuning itself still waits: only if real data shows ASR errors dominate, and after the AEC / front-end work. Then LoRA on large-v3-turbo, evaluated on a held-out real set against the base model. The wake-stage audio also serves the wake word (workstream a) and AEC work.

docs.title: Related project: paulglavin/VoicePipeline (reviewed 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
Not adopted. A server-side Wyoming STT wrapper: offline DTLN noise suppression, Silero VAD, WeSpeaker speaker ID and English STT; no AEC and no wake word. MIT, a single-author hobby project with no tests. Ideas borrowed into this plan:

  1. Review and labelling loop for the recorded audio, needed before the recordings can train the wake word, AEC or STT: the stored WAV with its transcript and scores, a Pending queue of low-confidence items, owner confirm or reject, and an append-only labels table.
  2. Experiment: a blind noise suppressor arm (DTLN or RNNoise; off, on and a 50 % blend) in the synthetic noise benchmark and the live A/B runner. Expected gain is modest; AEC remains the main fix.
  3. Parked: speaker ID, for per-person replies or for rejecting TV voices.

docs.title: f. Later / backlog
docs.text:
• Phase-2 learning collector: alias proposals from misses, within the transcript retention window (STT hint list and learning).
  • Kiais stream tool-call chunk fix (optional; Kiais integration).
  • AEC / front-end and false-wake work, in the satellite repository.
  • Cleanup of old Home Assistant entries.

docs.title: 5. Data handling
docs.text: Purpose-limited: transcripts are collected only to validate the assistant on real usage, in Loki (global 180-day retention, no separate stream rule), and analysed locally; derived replay datasets on the workstation are deleted at the end of the experiment, at most 30 days. Agents see aggregates only (counts, miss rates, categories); no transcript text goes to any AI service or cloud. Samples are shown only to the owner. Nothing private is committed to git. Transcripts expire with the 180-day retention; stopping means reverting the exception commit. Audio of every pipeline run (request audio and the continuous wake-stage room audio) is kept for 90 days on a cluster volume from 2026-11-05, on the owner's approval; agents never open or listen to it and report counts and sizes only. Policy and checked locations: Log policy; data register.

docs.title: 6. Open decisions for the owner
docs.text:
1. Approve the deploy of the custom "Kivi" wake word once it beats alexa (rollback is one setting).
  2. Provide real commands (or a review session of samples) to confirm the hint-list effect and the "Pon" / "Con" error.
  3. Decide, after the P0 headroom analysis, whether the decider goes on to P1 and P2.
  4. Choose the optional local teacher for P2 (pplx-decider-v1.1-27b or Laya), if the project reaches it. Related: for P4, confirm "own thin agent, borrowing the home-assistant-laya structure" instead of installing or forking that component (workstream d).
  5. Approve any live Home Assistant change: shadow-mode conversation agent, entity cleanup.
  6. Decided 2026-11-05: audio collection is on (90 days, including wake-stage room audio). Household consent is the owner's responsibility.
  7. Confirm whether the 180-day transcript retention stays or is shortened once the validation is done.

docs.title: Kivi speech-to-text: a home vocabulary hint list and learning from usage
docs.text:
Status: design (no live change). Nothing in Home Assistant, the cluster or GitOps state was changed. Date: 2026-11-05 Scope: the Spanish STT step of the Assist pipeline "Kiwi" (assistant "Kivi"): Wyoming faster-whisper in namespace home-assistant, Home Assistant 2026.10.4, pipeline language es. Related: conversation agent evaluation (built-in intents coverage, prefer_local_intents); small local models study, section 5 (prompt and hotwords measurements, summarised in section 1.6); Kiais integration (current conversation agent).

Evidence labels: documented (read in source code, a changelog or a manifest, with the version named), observed (read from the cluster, Loki or the repository on the date above), inferred (derived from documented material, not run), hypothesis (to be tested).

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
1. Upstream already does phase 1. wyoming-faster-whisper 3.6.0 (2026-08) added --hass-token: the server reads the conversation-exposed entity names, their aliases, and the area and floor names from Home Assistant over the websocket API, ranks them in four tiers and passes them to Whisper as initial_prompt within a 200-token budget, refreshed in the background at the start of each utterance. 3.7.0 fixed alias ranking and added environment and _FILE configuration. The deployed image is 2.4.0 (2024-12), which has only a static --initial-prompt. The cheapest phase 1 is to rebuild the owner's image on 3.8.1 and set --hass-token plus a fixed, generic Spanish command-verb --initial-prompt prefix. No home names need to be committed, because they are fetched in the cluster.
  2. Measured: names plus command verbs help, names alone barely do. On 145 clips per condition with TV sound mixed in, built-in intent success went from 82/71/65/46 % (clean, +10, +5, 0 dB) without a prompt to 85/79/75/57 % with area and device names plus a generic verb list (48 clips fixed against 7 broken over the noisy conditions, p ≤ 0.007 each). Names alone gave 81/74/70/52 %. hotwords gave byte-identical output to initial_prompt. "Kivi" in the prompt leaked into 3 of 1400 transcripts, so the wake name stays out (section 1.6).
  3. hotwords is not a separate mechanism. In faster-whisper it is the same "previous text" slot as initial_prompt (no logit bias). For commands of a single 30 s window the two behave alike (confirmed by measurement), so initial_prompt is enough.
  4. Home Assistant sends nothing usable per request. The Wyoming integration in 2026.10.4 sends Transcribe(language=...) only. The protocol has transcript_names and transcript_terms since Wyoming 1.10.0, but neither Home Assistant 2026.10.4 nor the server uses them.
  5. Transcripts are already stored. The deployed server logs every transcript at INFO level and Vector ships it to Loki, which keeps 180 days. Any learning loop should start by deciding this.
  6. Learning loop: capture each run from Home Assistant's pipeline debug API (STT text, intent result, processed_locally, timings) into a small in-cluster store with 30-day retention for text, derive misrecognition signals, and turn them each week into ranked proposals (hint words, entity aliases, a text correction map) that the owner approves. Measure with intent success rate and repeat rate before and after.

docs.title: 1.1 What is deployed (observed)
docs.text:
• apps/home-assistant/values.yaml, controller whisper: image pando85/wyoming-whisper:2.4.0 (built from pando85/wyoming-addons, whisper/Dockerfile: CTranslate2 4.5.0 on Ubuntu 20.04 with CUDA 12.2, wyoming-faster-whisper v2.4.0), args --model large-v3-turbo --language es --device cuda --compute-type int8, runtime class nvidia, on prusik. No --initial-prompt, no --beam-size (2.4.0 default 0 = auto). Service home-assistant-whisper:10300.
  • wyoming-faster-whisper 2.4.0 pins faster-whisper==1.1.0 and wyoming==1.5.3 (documented, requirements.txt at tag v2.4.0).
  • The handler logs each transcript with _LOGGER.info(text) (documented, handler.py at v2.4.0; also dispatch_handler.py in 3.8.1). Observed: 157 INFO:wyoming_faster_whisper.handler lines in the last 48 h of pod logs, and 707 Loki entries for {namespace="home-assistant", container="whisper"} in the last 7 days (counts only, no text read). Loki retention_period: 180d (system/loki/values.yaml).
  • Measured by the owner: STT p50 0.86 s for about 3 s of audio (given, not re-measured here).

docs.title: 1.2 What the server supports
docs.text:
Feature 2.4.0 (deployed) 3.8.1 (latest tag, 2026-09-14) Label --initial-prompt (static, startup only) yes yes, also WYO_WHISPER_INITIAL_PROMPT[_FILE] documented Home Assistant names as prompt (--hass-token, --hass-api, --hass-refresh-seconds, --hass-prompt-max-tokens default 200, --hass-prompt-timeout default 1.0 s) no yes (3.6.0, alias tiering 3.7.0) documented hotwords no no (not passed to faster-whisper) documented Per-request prompt from the transcribe event no no (only language is read) documented Segment confidence (avg_logprob, no_speech_prob) returned or logged no no (segments joined to text, info discarded) documented Server-side VAD (--vad-filter, --vad-clip, --vad-endpointing) no yes documented Text post-processing / correction map no no documented

Source: rhasspy/wyoming-faster-whisper (now OHF-Voice), CHANGELOG.md, __main__.py, dispatch_handler.py, faster_whisper_handler.py, hass_api.py, name_cache.py, vocabulary.py at v3.8.1/HEAD. CHANGELOG.md at HEAD lists an unreleased 3.9.0 (language reporting only).

How the 3.6+ name biasing works (documented, hass_api.py, vocabulary.py, name_cache.py):

  • Websocket calls: homeassistant/expose_entity/list (keeps entities exposed to conversation), get_states (friendly names), config/entity_registry/get_entries (aliases, area, device), config/device_registry/list (only when an entity's area comes from its device), config/area_registry/list, config/floor_registry/list. Nothing is written.
  • Tiers, filled in order until the budget is used: (1) areas and floors that contain an exposed entity, (2) entity names in light, switch, fan, media_player, climate, scene, todo, (3) other areas and floors, (4) other entity names. Each alias sits behind its entity. Names are de-duplicated case-insensitively and joined with ,, ending in .. The budget is counted with the model's own tokenizer. --initial-prompt is always kept at the front.
  • Refresh starts at AudioStart in the background; at AudioStop the server waits at most --hass-prompt-timeout for an unfinished refresh, then uses the previous names. A failed fetch never fails a transcript. Default --hass-refresh-seconds 0 refreshes on every utterance.
  • --debug logs the exact prompt and how many names were dropped. Note that --debug also logs each transcript (models.py), so it should only be enabled briefly.
  • The token must belong to an administrator: homeassistant/expose_entity/list is decorated @websocket_api.require_admin in Home Assistant 2026.10.4 (documented, homeassistant/components/homeassistant/exposed_entities.py). Home Assistant tokens have no scopes, so this token can do anything an admin can.

docs.title: 1.3 What Home Assistant sends per request (documented, 2026.10.4)
docs.text:
• homeassistant/components/wyoming/stt.py writes Transcribe(language=metadata.language) and then the audio. Manifest pins wyoming==1.10.2.
  • Wyoming 1.10.0 added vad_sensitivity, transcript_names and transcript_terms to transcribe (documented, rhasspy/wyoming CHANGELOG.md, wyoming/asr.py). Home Assistant 2026.10.4 does not fill them, and the 3.8.1 server does not read them. So a per-request hint list from Home Assistant is not available today; it must be configured on the server.
  • The Transcript event can carry a context dict, but the Home Assistant integration reads only text (documented). Confidence cannot travel back to Home Assistant this way.

docs.title: 1.4 initial_prompt versus hotwords in faster-whisper (documented, faster-whisper 1.1.0)
docs.text:
• initial_prompt is tokenised and placed in the decoder's previous-text slot (<|startofprev|>) for the first window; with condition_on_previous_text later windows see the previous output instead. It is reset when the decoding temperature rises above prompt_reset_on_temperature (0.5).
  • hotwords (added in faster-whisper 1.0.2) goes into the same previous-text slot, before any previous tokens, for every window, and is ignored when prefix is set. It is not a keyword boost or logit bias. For voice commands, which fit in one 30 s window, the two are equivalent; using both would only duplicate tokens.
  • Length: the previous-text part is cut to max_length // 2 - 1 = 223 tokens (Whisper's decoder context is 448). Anything longer is silently truncated from the front.

Known pitfalls:

  • Echo and hallucination (documented in the upstream vocabulary.py comment and changelog; widely reported for Whisper prompting): long prompts make the model output prompt words that were not spoken, especially on silence or non-speech. In this home the risky audio is not silence (Home Assistant's VAD ends the stream) but TV sound and room noise captured after the wake word. Hypothesis: a prompt that is a list of nouns is low risk, because an echoed noun list does not match an intent; a prompt with full imperative sentences ("enciende la luz del salón") could produce an actionable hallucination. Keep the prefix free of complete commands.
  • Style leakage: the model imitates the prompt's casing, punctuation and spelling. This helps (names come back spelled, accented and capitalised as Home Assistant stores them) and can hurt (a comma list prompt tends to add commas; an English prompt can pull Spanish output towards English). The prefix should be Spanish and use the same punctuation as normal speech.
  • Model dependence: Distil-Whisper models degrade with prompts (documented, upstream 3.8.0 changelog: distil-small.en breaks from about 52 prompt tokens). large-v3-turbo is a pruned, fine-tuned model, not a distilled one; in Spanish it benefits from a prompt of about 120 tokens (observed, 1.6). Whisper small and medium were significantly worse than turbo without a prompt (clean 70 % and 76 % against 82 %), so the model stays.
  • Latency: prompt tokens add decoder prefill work per beam. Hypothesis: tens of milliseconds on the GTX 1060 for about 200 tokens; being measured in section 9 of the small local models study, against the 0.86 s p50.
  • Wake word in the prompt: observed: with "Kivi" at the start of the prompt, "Kivi" appeared in 3 of 1400 transcripts whose audio did not contain it. A leading "Kivi" can break strict intent matching, so the wake name stays out of the prompt.

docs.title: 1.5 Home Assistant matching that the hint list feeds (documented, 2026.10.4)
docs.text:
• The default agent matches in stages: exposed entities only, then unexposed entities, then unknown names (IntentMatchingStage in conversation/default_agent.py), with hassil==3.12.1 and home-assistant-intents==2026.10.6. Names and aliases must match the text.
  • 2026.10.4 adds a gazetteer fallback (conversation/gazetteer.py, gazetteer-matcher==1.1.0) that reaches intents through near-miss names and unseen wordings, but LANGUAGE = "en": it is English only and does not run on the "prefer local intents" fast path. For Spanish there is no fuzzy matching, so a single misheard letter or accent in a name means no match.
  • Hypothesis (not checked in hassil source here): accent and case differences between the transcript and the stored name can break a match. The hint list helps here because Whisper copies the stored spelling. Test with scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/builtin_intents.py.

docs.title: 1.6 Measured effect on this setup
docs.text:
Source: small local models study, section 5 (observed by that study, 2026-11-05). Setup: faster-whisper large-v3-turbo int8, beam 5, as deployed, run on z800; 5 Piper voices × 29 control phrases that built-in intents can handle = 145 clips per condition; TV content mixed in at +10, +5 and 0 dB SNR. Metric: Home Assistant built-in intent success (hassil 3.12.1, home-assistant-intents 2026.10.6). The names are those of the study's test home, not the owner's.

Prompt (initial_prompt) Clean +10 dB +5 dB 0 dB None 82 % 71 % 65 % 46 % Area and device names (about 80 tokens) 81 % 74 % 70 % 52 % Names plus generic Spanish command verbs (about 40 tokens more) 85 % 79 % 75 % 57 % Same text as hotwords byte-identical output to initial_prompt
  • Names only against no prompt: 31 clips fixed and 9 broken over the noisy conditions; no gain on clean audio.
  • Names plus verbs against no prompt: 48 fixed and 7 broken over the noisy conditions (p ≤ 0.007 in each noisy condition); against names only: 29 fixed and 4 broken.
  • The verb list used: Enciende, apaga, sube, baja, abre, cierra, para, pausa, reanuda, silencia, quita el silencio, pon, temporizador, minutos, volumen, brillo, por ciento, grados. Without it the remaining errors were mostly the first verb of short commands (for example "Apaga la tele" heard as "Hasta acá la tele", "Reanuda" as "Renuda").
  • "Kivi" at the start of the prompt: 3 of 1400 transcripts contained "Kivi" not present in the audio.
  • STT latency with the prompt: being measured (section 9 of that study); 0.86 s p50 without a prompt in real use.

Conclusion (inferred from the above): the command verbs carry most of the gain, and they are generic, so they belong in the static --initial-prompt prefix; the names add a smaller gain on noisy audio and come from Home Assistant through --hass-token.

How 3.8.1 composes the two (documented, vocabulary.py _build_prompt at v3.8.1, unchanged at HEAD): the --initial-prompt text comes first (a . is added if it does not end in punctuation), then the Home Assistant names joined by , and ending in .. The --hass-prompt-max-tokens budget (default 200) counts the whole prompt, prefix included, using the model's tokenizer, and the prefix is always kept. With the ~40-token verb prefix about 160 tokens are left for names, in tier order. Two differences from the study's prompt are untested: the order (the study put names before verbs; upstream puts the prefix first) and the real home's name list, which may be longer than the study's ~80 tokens. Hypothesis: neither changes the result much; check with the study's harness by swapping the order once.

docs.title: 1.7 Making the hint list reloadable without a restart
docs.text:
Three ways, smallest first:

  1. Upstream 3.8.1 as is (recommended). Names from Home Assistant reload by themselves (per utterance or every --hass-refresh-seconds). The static part (--initial-prompt) is startup-only; put it in a ConfigMap read through WYO_WHISPER_INITIAL_PROMPT_FILE and let Reloader restart the pod when it changes (the chart already uses reloader.stakater.com/auto). A restart reloads the model; with a weekly cadence at most this is acceptable. Inferred: the prefix is generic Spanish text, so it can live in git.
  2. Small patch, file watched. Extend the image with a file /config/stt-hints.txt (extra names) and /config/stt-corrections.yaml (see 3.4), checked by modification time at each AudioStart like the name refresh, and appended as tier 0 after the prefix. About 60 lines in name_cache.py/dispatch_handler.py plus a ConfigMap or Secret volume (a mounted ConfigMap updates in place within about a minute; no restart). Needed for home-specific extra words and for the correction map.
  3. Small patch, fetched. Same, but the server fetches hints and corrections from the phase 2 service over HTTP. Avoids keeping home-specific words in a Kubernetes object that GitOps does not manage. More moving parts; only worth it once phase 2 exists.

Image work for option 1 (inferred, to verify in a build): in pando85/wyoming-addons whisper/Dockerfile, set WYOMING_WHISPER_VERSION to 3.8.1 and install wyoming-faster-whisper[hass] (extra hass = aiohttp). 3.x needs faster-whisper>=1.2.1, av<19 and pysilero-vad; it does not need torch, so the CTranslate2 CUDA base still fits. The Ubuntu 20.04 base ships Python 3.8, the minimum 3.x supports; a newer CTranslate2 base is worth taking at the same time. run.sh in the image passes --uri, --data-dir, --download-dir; 3.x reads environment variables too. Upstream's own Dockerfile.gpu is not published and is about 10.7 GB because of CUDA torch. 3.0.0 changed --model and --language defaults to auto; the deployment passes both explicitly, so that change is harmless.

docs.title: 2.1 Sources
docs.text:
Source API (read-only) Admin needed Notes Exposed entities ws homeassistant/expose_entity/list yes only conversation exposure Friendly names ws get_states no what the user sees and says Aliases, entity area ws config/entity_registry/get_entries no Device area ws config/device_registry/list no Areas and floors, with their aliases ws config/area_registry/list, config/floor_registry/list no upstream 3.8.1 includes area and floor aliases next to their names (_place_names) Assistant name, Spanish command words static prefix in git n/a generic, not home-specific Media sources (playlists, radio names, artists) Music Assistant or media_player/browse_media no only if music commands are common; long names cost many tokens

Admin requirement documented for 2026.10.4 as above. All APIs are documented websocket commands of the frontend.

docs.title: 2.2 Ranking and trimming
docs.text:
Upstream's deterministic tiers (1.2) are a good default. Changes worth making only after phase 2 data exists:

  • Usage-weighted ranking: within a tier, order names by how often they appear in successful commands over the last 30 days, and promote names that appear in misrecognitions (3.3). This needs the patch in 1.7 option 2 or 3.
  • Budget: keep --hass-prompt-max-tokens at the default 200. The measured prompt was about 120 tokens; a real home that fills the budget gives a longer prompt than was tested, so lower the budget to about 130 if the phase 1 check shows echoed names. Spanish names with accents cost more tokens per character than English ones (inferred from BPE behaviour; check with --debug).
  • Prefix (generic, in git): the measured verb list from 1.6, unchanged: Enciende, apaga, sube, baja, abre, cierra, para, pausa, reanuda, silencia, quita el silencio, pon, temporizador, minutos, volumen, brillo, por ciento, grados. (about 40 tokens, counted inside the 200-token budget). Single words and short phrases only, no full commands (1.4), and never "Kivi" (observed leak, 1.6). Changing the list means re-running the study's comparison.

docs.title: 2.3 Refresh
docs.text: Set --hass-refresh-seconds 300. Every utterance otherwise opens a websocket and runs get_states for the whole house; with 300 s a rename takes at most five minutes to show and the at-most-1 s wait at AudioStop happens at most once per five minutes (inferred from name_cache.py).

docs.title: 2.4 Where it runs and the GitOps shape
docs.text:
Option Effort Notes A. Inside the STT service (upstream --hass-token) lowest no generator to maintain; names never leave the cluster or reach git B. CronJob generator writing a ConfigMap or Secret medium needs write RBAC in the namespace; fights ArgoCD if the object is in git; home names in a Kubernetes object C. Sidecar generator writing a shared file medium no RBAC; still needs the 1.7 option 2 patch

Recommended A. GitOps changes (proposal, not applied): in apps/home-assistant/values.yaml under controllers.whisper: new image tag, args --hass-api http://home-assistant-hass:8123/api --hass-refresh-seconds 300, environment WYO_WHISPER_HASS_TOKEN_FILE pointing at a mounted Secret, and an ExternalSecret reading secret/home-assistant/<path> from Vault. Keep the Renovate hint above the image. The token is created by the owner in Home Assistant (a dedicated user is cleaner to revoke) and written to Vault by the owner.

docs.title: 3.1 Capture points (documented, 2026.10.4, unless stated)
docs.text:
Point What it has Limits Pipeline debug runs: ws assist_pipeline/pipeline_debug/list and /get every event of a run: run-start, stt-end with stt_output.text, intent-end with processed_locally and intent_output (response type, error code, targets, conversation_id), TTS, timestamps admin only; in memory, STORED_PIPELINE_RUNS = 10 per pipeline; lost on restart (the hass pod restarted 45 min before this check, observed) Whisper logs (Loki) transcript text and time no intent result, no agent, no confidence; currently 180 days in Loki Satellite logs (webos-voice-satellite) STT_END text, INTENT_END speech and conversation_id, its own stage latencies only that satellite; no intent result code assist_pipeline debug_recording_dir option audio files per run audio: off by default, opt-in only A custom Home Assistant integration hooking the pipeline everything, no loss couples to internal APIs that change between releases

Most reliable without touching Home Assistant internals (inferred): poll the pipeline debug API every 10 to 15 s and store new runs. Ten runs per pipeline is far more than a household produces in 15 s. Cross-check completeness weekly against the whisper transcription count; a gap only happens across Home Assistant restarts.

docs.title: 3.2 What to record and what not
docs.text:
Per run (in the store, not in logs):

  • time, pipeline, satellite device, language, conversation id;
  • STT text (normalised: lower case, whitespace collapsed), STT duration, audio duration if known;
  • confidence from a whisper patch that logs avg_logprob, no_speech_prob and prompt hash per utterance without text, joined on time (the Transcript event cannot carry it, 1.3);
  • intent stage result: processed_locally, response type (action_done, query_answer, error), error code (no_intent_match, no_valid_targets, failed_to_handle), intent name and target entity ids;
  • which agent answered (local built-in or the LLM agent), stage latencies (STT, intent, TTS).

Not recorded: audio (off; opt-in short sessions only, with consent of everyone recorded), TTS text of LLM answers (not needed for STT learning), anything from runs of other pipelines.

Retention and access:

  • raw run rows with text: 30 days, then deleted; derived counts and n-gram statistics without free text kept 1 year; approved corrections (pairs of short command texts) kept until removed.
  • store: a new database and user in the existing Zalando cluster home-assistant-postgres, declared in apps/home-assistant/templates/postgresql.yaml; credentials from the operator Secret. Velero backups then hold up to 30 days of text too, which should be accepted explicitly. A small SQLite file on its own PVC is the lighter alternative.
  • access: only the collector and the owner; no ingress; the review page (3.5) behind the existing oauth2-proxy. Prometheus metrics expose counts only.
  • the whisper INFO transcript lines: either drop them in Vector for container="whisper" or patch the server to log them at DEBUG; otherwise they stay in Loki for 180 days alongside the store. Owner decision.

docs.title: 3.3 Signals of a misrecognition
docs.text: Signal Definition (initial; calibrate on data) Strength No local match intent-end error no_intent_match or no_valid_targets from the built-in agent strong for home commands, but general questions also fail locally by design when they go to the LLM Quick repeat a second run from the same satellite within 20 s whose text is similar (normalised edit ratio at least 0.6) strong; the second text is often the correction Repeat that succeeds quick repeat where the first failed and the second gave action_done strongest; gives a (wrong, right) pair LLM did a home action prefer_local_intents is on and the agent is Kiais through core llama_cpp (conversation.fast) since 2026-11-05 (Kiais integration); so processed_locally false and the LLM run changed a device state (state change with the run's context id, from the recorder) medium; needs the context join, hypothesis that the context id carries through Low confidence avg_logprob below about -0.8 or no_speech_prob above 0.5 weak alone; thresholds are hypotheses User correction next run within 10 s is "no", "para", "cancela", "eso no" medium Empty or one-word transcript empty text or a lone area or entity name medium; also detects prompt echo

docs.title: 3.4 From signals to proposals
docs.text:
A weekly job (CronJob in the same app) groups the week's flagged runs and produces ranked proposals, each with its count, examples (at most three, shown only in the review page, never in notifications) and the expected effect:

  1. Hint words: words in the right side of (wrong, right) pairs that are names or domain words and are not in the current prompt, or were dropped by the budget. Action: raise them (needs the 1.7 option 2 or 3 patch) or rename or alias the entity so upstream picks it up.
  2. Entity and area aliases: a wrong form that recurs (at least 3 times, from at least 2 days) for the same target. Action: add it as an alias in Home Assistant. Guard: reject an alias that equals or is close to another entity's name or alias in the same area. Aliases are registry changes outside git, so each one needs the owner's explicit yes (~/homelab/AGENTS.md, "Owner approval for live changes").
  3. Correction map: word or phrase rewrites applied to the transcript before intent matching (for example a systematic mis-spelling of an area). Home Assistant has no hook between STT and the intent stage, so the place is the whisper server (1.7 option 2 or 3, about 30 more lines: apply whole-word, case-insensitive rules after transcription). Each rule records its count and the date approved, and is dropped if its hit count is zero for 90 days.
  4. Evaluation and fine-tuning dataset: approved pairs become the text regression set; audio only from opt-in sessions where the owner reads the approved phrases (or Piper-synthesised clips as in the small local models study).

Review and approval:

  • weekly: a Home Assistant persistent notification with counts only ("12 proposals, local success rate 81 % (+3)"), linking to the review page;
  • review page: a small internal page (the collector's own, behind oauth2-proxy) listing proposals with approve or reject; approving an alias writes nothing to Home Assistant by itself, it produces the exact change for the owner to make or confirm;
  • generic changes (code, manifests, generic prefix words, metric and dashboard definitions) go through a PR to ~/homelab; home-specific words, aliases and correction rules never enter the public repository (~/homelab/AGENTS.md, personal information).

docs.title: 3.5 Measuring improvement
docs.text:
• Primary: weekly local success rate = runs with processed_locally and action_done or query_answer, divided by runs classified as home commands (local success, plus local failures whose quick repeat succeeded or whose LLM run acted on a device).
  • Secondary: no-match rate, quick-repeat rate, LLM fallbacks for home actions, STT p50 and p95, prompt echo rate (empty or name-only transcripts).
  • Regression set: approved (wrong, right) pairs. Text level, offline: the right side must match locally and the wrong side, after the correction map, must too (run with builtin_intents.py against an exported inventory, not against live Home Assistant, because conversation/process executes actions). Audio level: WER and intent success on the opt-in or synthetic clips, with and without the prompt and corrections.
  • Before and after: compare 2 weeks before a change with 2 weeks after; at household volumes (about 80 runs a day observed from whisper logs) a few percentage points is noise, so report counts with a confidence interval and treat small changes as unproven.

docs.title: 4. Options compared
docs.text: Option Effort Risk Latency cost Privacy Static --initial-prompt with home names on 2.4.0 very low names in git (public repo), stale prompt prefill (hypothesis: tens of ms) names exposed publicly: not acceptable Static verb-only --initial-prompt on 2.4.0 (interim) very low verbs alone not measured about 40 prompt tokens generic text only Upstream 3.8.1 --hass-token low (image rebuild, Secret) admin token in the STT pod; image jump 2.4 → 3.8 same prefill; refresh hidden in the utterance; at most 1 s once per refresh interval if Home Assistant is slow names stay in the cluster Generator CronJob plus ConfigMap medium write RBAC, drift with ArgoCD same names in a Kubernetes object Usage logging and weekly proposals medium (collector, store, review page) another admin token; text at rest 30 days none (off the request path) transcripts at rest; bounded retention Correction map in the STT server low on top of phase 2 a bad rule rewrites good text; mitigated by approval and counts negligible rules hold home words, kept out of git Small local model as STT corrector or router medium to high added latency and new failure modes hundreds of ms (hypothesis; see the small local models study) stays local Fine-tuning Whisper on home data high overfitting, maintenance per model update none at inference needs consented audio

docs.title: 5. Recommended phased plan
docs.text:
Phase 1: fixed verb prefix plus live Home Assistant names. Justified by 1.6: names plus verbs raised built-in intent success by 3 to 11 points (more in noise), with few regressions; the wake name stays out. Open gate: the prompt's latency cost (study section 9) must stay small against the 0.86 s p50. 1. Rebuild pando85/wyoming-whisper on wyoming-faster-whisper[hass]==3.8.1 (owner's repo). 2. In GitOps: new tag, --hass-api, --hass-refresh-seconds 300, token via ExternalSecret and WYO_WHISPER_HASS_TOKEN_FILE, and the measured verb list (2.2) as --initial-prompt, in a ConfigMap read through WYO_WHISPER_INITIAL_PROMPT_FILE. No "Kivi". 3. Verify: --debug for a few minutes to read the composed prompt (verbs first, then names) and the dropped-name count (then off); STT p50 within 0.1 s of 0.86 s; owner's spot check on 20 home commands, including short ones that start with a verb ("Apaga la tele", "Reanuda"). Optional interim step before the image rebuild: the verb list alone as --initial-prompt on the deployed 2.4.0 (one arg, generic text). Verbs alone were not measured (hypothesis: most of the gain, because the remaining no-verb errors were leading verbs); check with the study's harness first. 4. Owner-side cleanups that help immediately: add Spanish aliases for entities whose names are English or technical, and keep exposure to what is actually said.

Phase 2: usage logging and weekly proposals. Collector (polls pipeline debug), store (30-day text), signals (3.3), weekly proposals and review page (3.4), metrics and a Grafana dashboard with counts only, decision on whisper transcript lines in Loki. Patch the whisper server to log confidence without text and to read an extra-hints file and a correction map (1.7 option 2). Start the regression set.

Phase 3: correction model or fine-tune, only if justified. Trigger: after 8 weeks of phase 2, local success on home commands still below the target (owner to set, for example 95 %) and the residual errors are not fixable by aliases or rules. Candidates: a small local model as corrector or router (see the small local models study), or a LoRA or full fine-tune of the Whisper model on consented audio.

docs.title: 6. Needs from the owner
docs.text:
• Approval to rebuild and push the whisper image in pando85/wyoming-addons.
  • Done (2026-11-05): a Home Assistant long-lived token from an administrator account (required by expose_entity/list), now in Vault (see "The Home Assistant token" below).
  • Decision on the transcripts already in Loki (180 days): drop or keep.
  • Phase 2: approval to keep transcripts for 30 days in the cluster, the store choice, and the review flow; each proposed alias is approved one by one.

docs.title: The Home Assistant token
docs.text:
Created on 2026-11-05 for --hass-token (not yet wired into the whisper deployment).

  • Belongs to the owner's admin user. Home Assistant tokens have no scopes, so it can do anything that admin can; treat it as a full-access secret.
  • Name: wyoming-whisper Kivi STT hint list; lifespan 3650 days (to about 2036-11).
  • Vault: secret/home-assistant/wyoming-whisper, key hass_token (KV v2 version 1). ExternalSecret form: remoteRef.key: /home-assistant/wyoming-whisper, property: hass_token.
  • Verified: the Vault value authenticates against GET /api/ (HTTP 200) and matches the value created, by hash.
  • Revoke: Home Assistant profile, Security, Long-lived access tokens, delete the entry by name. Anything using it then gets 401 and the hint list falls back to the static prefix.
  • Rotate: create a new token with the same name pattern over the websocket (auth/long_lived_access_token) or in the profile, vault kv put it from a 0600 file to the same path (new KV version), let the ExternalSecret and Reloader roll the pod, then delete the old token. See Home Assistant API access for agents for the headless login.

docs.title: 7. Open questions
docs.text:
• Latency cost of the ~120 to 200-token prompt on the GTX 1060 (small local models study, section 9).
  • Verbs-only prompt and prefix-first order, not measured (1.6).
  • Does part of the wake word reach the STT audio, and does Home Assistant strip "Kivi" from the transcript before matching? (Keeping "Kivi" out of the prompt is settled, 1.6.)
  • Answered: prefer_local_intents is on and the agent is Kiais via core llama_cpp (conversation.fast) since 2026-11-05 (Kiais integration).
  • Does hassil 3.12.1 fold accents when matching Spanish names?
  • Does the context id of an LLM tool call reach the recorder's state changes, so they can be joined to the run?

docs.title: 8. Log policy: voice transcripts in Loki (temporary exception)
docs.text:
Two owner decisions on 2026-11-05, in this order:

  1. Morning: what people say to the assistant must not be kept in logs or Loki. A Vector filter and a Whisper image that logs transcripts only at DEBUG implemented it.
  2. Later the same day: a time-limited exception. To collect real usage for offline replay against Home Assistant's built-in sentences (the decision-model idea in the plan), transcripts are kept in Loki for 180 days, on the owner's explicit request ("we can get all the data that we need"). What is collected, why, and how to stop is in the data register.

Current state (from 2026-11-05, effective once the change is synced).

  • Source. The Whisper container (git.grigri.cloud/agil/wyoming-whisper:3.8.1.1, namespace home-assistant, container whisper) logs each transcript as DEBUG:wyoming_faster_whisper.dispatch_handler:<text> (the 2.x image used INFO:wyoming_faster_whisper.handler:<text>). The image patch moved that line from INFO to DEBUG.
  • How DEBUG is enabled for that one logger. Not with --debug: at DEBUG the server prints its whole argument namespace, which includes the Home Assistant token read from WYO_WHISPER_HASS_TOKEN_FILE, and it enables DEBUG for every library. Instead apps/home-assistant/config/whisper-logging/sitecustomize.py (a ConfigMap mounted at /opt/whisper-logging, loaded through PYTHONPATH) sets the root logger to INFO and only wyoming_faster_whisper.dispatch_handler to DEBUG. Besides the transcript, that logger's other DEBUG lines are now logged too: audio stopped, VAD end of voice command, completed request time, and the initial prompt with the Home Assistant names. The names are accepted in logs; the token is not logged.
  • Vector. The drop_voice_transcripts filter in system/loki/vector-agent.yaml is kept but not wired in: the truncate transform reads kubernetes_logs directly. vector validate warns "has no consumers", which is expected. Its regex now also matches dispatch_handler (the old one matched only handler, which no longer matches the 3.8.1 logger name), and the tests cover both.
  • Loki. No per-stream rule. The global retention_period: 180d applies (the compactor has retention_enabled: true and delete_request_store: filesystem), so the whisper stream is kept 180 days like everything else. If the global value is ever lowered, the transcript retention changes with it. The stream labels are namespace="home-assistant", container="whisper".
  • False wakes are captured too. Wake word detection runs on the server (openWakeWord), so a false wake streams whatever was being said to Whisper and its transcript lands in Loki like any command. People in the room are recorded in text without having said the wake word.
  • How to turn it off. Revert the commit that made this exception (restores the Vector wiring and removes the sitecustomize ConfigMap, PYTHONPATH and the mount). Whisper then logs no transcript (DEBUG is off for that logger again). Transcripts already in Loki stay until they age out at 180 days; to remove them earlier, use Loki's delete API (see the data register).

Original policy, still valid outside the exception. The other places checked on 2026-11-05 (counts and shapes only, no text read):

  • Home Assistant (hass): default log level (no logger: config), so only warnings and errors reach Loki. None of the 2,212 voice-related lines in 7 days carries input text (the common one is an ollama "model not found" traceback). Do not enable debug for conversation, assist_pipeline or homeassistant.components.llama_cpp: that would log request text.
  • Home Assistant recorder (PostgreSQL): the assist_satellite, conversation, stt, tts and wake_word entities only keep a state (idle, listening, processing, responding) and friendly_name; no events carry speech text.
  • Piper (rhasspy/wyoming-piper:2.5.2): only startup lines at INFO. It logs the synthesized text only with --debug; never add that flag.
  • openWakeWord: startup line only.
  • Kiais gateway (namespace isidoro, RUST_LOG=kiais=debug): logs events and timings, no request or response bodies seen. The chat_messages table in its database is empty. Re-check after Kiais upgrades because it runs at debug level.
  • Old transcripts already in Loki. Not purged: the morning decision was to stop collecting them, not to delete the history, and the exception now keeps new ones as well. They age out with the 180-day retention. Loki's deletion mode is the default (filter-and-delete), so a purge by log selector and line filter through the delete API remains possible.

docs.title: Building the Kivi Whisper STT image on Forgejo
docs.text:
Status: image 3.8.1.1 published (digest sha256:938daef7b6e3fd76bb8601171a34b375df13b8bd37fc61a27b5b6a696f61680d); the cutover (Phase C) is rolled out 2026-11-05 with the owner's approval, see Rollout 2026-11-05 for the differences from this plan and the verification result. Date: 2026-11-05 Goal: replace pando85/wyoming-whisper:2.4.0 with an image built on wyoming-faster-whisper[hass]==3.8.1, so the STT step gets the live Home Assistant name list (--hass-token) and the static Spanish verb prefix (--initial-prompt), as designed in STT hint list and learning from usage (phase 1).

Evidence labels: documented, observed, inferred, hypothesis (as in the design doc).

docs.title: Where the build lives
docs.text:
Everything about building the image is in the repository agil/wyoming-whisper (https://git.grigri.cloud/agil/wyoming-whisper, private, created 2026-11-05): the Dockerfile and the hashed lock, the Forgejo Actions workflow (build and push only on a tag), the transcript-log patch (transcripts at DEBUG, not INFO), the Renovate configuration, and the docs on the build pipeline, the sm_61 check, the runner disk, the risks and the image rollback. This page keeps only what belongs to the cluster.

Summary of the decisions (details and evidence in that repository):

  • Base ghcr.io/opennmt/ctranslate2:4.8.5-ubuntu22.04-cuda12.8 pinned by digest, Python 3.10, wyoming-faster-whisper[hass]==3.8.1, faster-whisper 1.2.1, ctranslate2 4.8.5.
  • GTX 1060 (sm_61): the driver 580 is the last Pascal branch, so the image stays on CUDA 12.x. cuobjdump on the local build shows sm_61 SASS in the CTranslate2 library (static evidence, 2026-11-05; the canary below is the gate). The local build is about 3.2 GB uncompressed, about 2 GB compressed.
  • Tags are <upstream version>.<revision> (first planned: 3.8.1.1), created by a human after the canary; no latest.
  • Pull access: the nodes' containerd already has a read-only credential for git.grigri.cloud (metal/roles/k3s/templates/host.toml.j2, the owner's own account, pull/resolve only), so a package owned by that account needs no imagePullSecret here (verified: the cluster runs this image).
  • Visibility: a package takes the visibility of its owner, not of the repository. Until 2026-11-05 the user agil was public and this image could be pulled anonymously although the repository is private; since agil became "limited" that day, anonymous pulls are refused.
  • Fallback if the runners' disks are at risk: build on GitHub and publish to ghcr.io/pando85/wyoming-whisper (only the image name changes here).

docs.title: What the owner must do before the first tag
docs.text:
1. Create a Forgejo token with only write:package, keep it in pass (0600 file) and set it as the repository secret PACKAGES_PAT (the FORGEJO_ prefix is reserved) of agil/wyoming-whisper.
  2. Optional: the Renovate secrets RENOVATE_PAT and RENOVATE_GITHUB_COM_TOKEN for that repository, then enable the schedule in its renovate.yml.
  3. Approve the first tag (v3.8.1.1); afterwards set the package cleanup rule (keep the last 3 versions).

docs.title: Cluster plan
docs.text: Steps marked [owner] need the owner; [approval] can be done by an agent after an explicit yes.

docs.title: Phase B: GPU canary on prusik (before touching the real STT)
docs.text:
The card has 3 GB with about 1.1 GB in use, so do not run two large-v3-turbo instances. A tiny model needs well under 300 MiB. The check itself is described in the image repository (docs/sm61-verification.md); here is the cluster part.

  1. [approval, GitOps] Commit a temporary controller whisper-canary in apps/home-assistant/values.yaml: the new image (tag@sha256 from the job summary), args --model tiny-int8 --language es --device cuda --compute-type int8 --debug, nvidia.com/gpu: "1", runtimeClassName: nvidia, no Service and no Ingress, emptyDir for /data (it downloads the tiny model; needs egress to Hugging Face).
  2. [owner or approved exec] Read-only checks in the pod: python3 -c "import ctranslate2 as c; print(c.get_cuda_device_count(), c.get_supported_compute_types('cuda'))" (expect 1 and int8 in the list) and the pod log. A Wyoming transcribe of a short Spanish clip of the owner's own voice through kubectl port-forward is the end-to-end test; delete the clip afterwards. --debug also logs transcripts: use it briefly and do not paste the output.
  3. Pass: no CUDA error such as no kernel image is available for execution on the device, int8 supported, one transcript returned. Record the result in the image repository's docs/sm61-verification.md.
  4. Remove the canary controller (revert that commit).

docs.title: Phase C: cutover (homelab GitOps)
docs.text:
All three changes in one commit home-assistant: Run whisper 3.8.1 with live Home Assistant names (or split into an inert ExternalSecret and ConfigMap commit first), pushed only with the owner's yes.

C1. Token Secret (Vault path already exists, see the Home Assistant token: secret/home-assistant/wyoming-whisper, key hass_token):

apps/home-assistant/templates/external-secret-whisper.yaml 

apiVersion: external-secrets.io/v1
kind: ExternalSecret
metadata:
  name: whisper-hass-token
spec:
  secretStoreRef:
    kind: ClusterSecretStore
    name: vault
  target:
    name: whisper-hass-token
  data:
    - secretKey: hass_token
      remoteRef:
        key: /home-assistant/wyoming-whisper
        property: hass_token

C2. Prompt ConfigMap apps/home-assistant/templates/configmap-whisper-prompt.yaml (generic Spanish verbs only, no home names, no "Kivi"; text from section 2.2 of the design doc, changing it needs the study's comparison): 

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: whisper-prompt
data:
  initial-prompt.txt: >-
    Enciende, apaga, sube, baja, abre, cierra, para, pausa, reanuda, silencia, quita el silencio,
    pon, temporizador, minutos, volumen, brillo, por ciento, grados.

C3. apps/home-assistant/values.yaml, controller whisper 

    whisper:
      type: deployment
      replicas: 1
      annotations:
        reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"      # roll on ConfigMap/Secret change (Recreate: a short STT gap)
      ...
      containers:
        whisper:
          image:
            repository: git.grigri.cloud/agil/wyoming-whisper
            tag: 3.8.1.1@sha256:<digest from the A5 job summary>
          args:
            - --model
            - large-v3-turbo
            - --language
            - es
            - --device
            - cuda
            - --compute-type
            - int8
            - --hass-api
            - http://home-assistant-hass.home-assistant.svc:8123/api
            - --hass-refresh-seconds
            - "300"
          env:
            WYO_WHISPER_HASS_TOKEN_FILE: /secrets/hass_token
            WYO_WHISPER_INITIAL_PROMPT_FILE: /prompt/initial-prompt.txt
and under persistence: 
    whisper-hass-token:
      enabled: true
      type: secret
      name: whisper-hass-token
      advancedMounts:
        whisper:
          whisper:
            - path: /secrets
              readOnly: true
    whisper-prompt:
      enabled: true
      type: configMap
      name: whisper-prompt
      advancedMounts:
        whisper:
          whisper:
            - path: /prompt
              readOnly: true
The image repository is private, so the homelab Renovate cannot read its tags: drop the # renovate: hint above (or add a host rule with a read:package token) and bump the tag by hand after each canary.

Notes: the token file is the Vault value as stored; the server may not strip a trailing newline (hypothesis, check in the first --debug log). Keep --model and --language explicit (3.x defaults them to auto). The existing probes (TCP 10300) still work.

C4. Verify (the design doc's phase 1 gate): the pod starts without re-downloading the model (hypothesis: 3.x reuses /data/models--mobiuslabsgmbh--faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo; if it starts downloading, the startup probe's 150 s will kill it, so first run with --local-files-only or raise failureThreshold for the first start); --debug for a few minutes to read the composed prompt (verbs first, then names, dropped-name count), then remove --debug; STT p50 within 0.1 s of 0.86 s; the owner's spot check on 20 home commands.

C5. When to do it: off-hours. Recreate plus the model load makes the STT unavailable for the duration of the start (about the probe's 150 s worst case).

docs.title: Phase D: rollback to 2.4.0
docs.text:
1. git revert the cutover commit (one revert restores image, args, env, the mounts; do not revert only the image, because 2.4.0 rejects --hass-api and --hass-refresh-seconds). Push with the owner's yes and let ArgoCD sync; Recreate brings 2.4.0 back.
  2. pando85/wyoming-whisper:2.4.0 stays pullable from Docker Hub (tag dated 2025-02-28) and is still in prusik's containerd cache. Do not delete the Docker Hub tag until the new image has run for a few weeks.
  3. The model volume needs no repair: 3.x only adds files under /data (Xet cache), 2.4.0 ignores them.
  4. If only the hint list misbehaves (echoed names, odd transcripts), do not roll back the image: drop --hass-token handling by deleting WYO_WHISPER_HASS_TOKEN_FILE, or revoke the token in Home Assistant (the server falls back to the static prefix on 401, per the design doc).
  5. Remove the whisper-hass-token ExternalSecret and the token itself only when abandoning the feature.
  6. Image-level rollback (previous tag, older CT2 base if sm_61 fails) is in the image repository's docs/rollback.md.

docs.title: Who does what
docs.text: Step Owner Agent, with approval Create the packages token (write:package), store it in pass, set the repository secret yes no (an agent must not mint or see it) Vault token for --hass-token done 2026-11-05 read-only check of the path only First tag v3.8.1.1 and the package cleanup rule approve, UI for the rule tag push with approval Canary controller commit, cutover commit, ArgoCD sync approve each push yes (commit, push, sync) kubectl exec/port-forward in the canary pod, voice clip for the test yes, or approve only with approval Spot check of 20 commands, go or no-go yes no Docs and compatibility record of results no yes

docs.title: Cluster-side risks
docs.text:
• GPU, driver, sm_61 and the runner disk: see the image repository's docs/risks.md. A driver or GPU operator bump past 580 breaks this card for every GPU pod.
  • Circularity. Forgejo and the STT pod both run on prusik. A cold start after a node reboot with an empty containerd cache waits for Forgejo; the digest pin and IfNotPresent keep this a retry, not an outage.
  • Model cache reuse and token newline (C3, C4) are untested hypotheses with a cheap check in the first start.
  • Version jump 2.4.0 to 3.8.1 (also faster-whisper, ctranslate2, wyoming, Python, CUDA): compare p50 and the 20-command check against the 2.4.0 baseline.
  • Admin token in the STT pod (accepted in the design doc): Home Assistant tokens have no scopes; never put the token or entity names in the image repository, its Actions logs or pasted --debug output.
  • Transcripts are no longer written to the whisper log at INFO (patched to DEBUG in the image); the Vector rule that drops voice transcripts before Loki still applies to the old image until the cutover.

docs.title: Rollout 2026-11-05
docs.text:
Rolled out 2026-11-05 as one commit (home-assistant: Run whisper 3.8.1 with live Home Assistant names). Differences from the plan above, checked against the image's own --help and source (the image wins):

  • No ConfigMap and no WYO_WHISPER_INITIAL_PROMPT_FILE: the static verbs prompt is the single --initial-prompt argument (the verified single-argument form from the conversation-agent decisions). The server puts it first and appends the names (vocabulary.py, _build_prompt).
  • Token via WYO_WHISPER_HASS_TOKEN_FILE=/secrets/hass_token as planned; the server reads the file and strip()s it, so the trailing-newline hypothesis is closed (static check in the image, 2026-11-05).
  • The controller carries reloader.stakater.com/auto so a changed token Secret rolls the pod.
  • Model cache: the entrypoint passes --data-dir /data --download-dir /data as in 2.4.0, HF_HOME and XDG_CACHE_HOME are /data, large-v3-turbo maps to mobiuslabsgmbh/faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo, and the existing volume holds exactly /data/models--mobiuslabsgmbh--faster-whisper-large-v3-turbo (1.6 GB, read-only ls/du on the 2.4.0 pod): the cache is reused (static evidence; the first start log is the check).
  • The startup probe allows 60 failures x 5 s (was 30) as insurance against a re-download.
  • Log level is the default (INFO, no --debug); transcripts are logged only at DEBUG in this image.

docs.title: Verification result 2026-11-05
docs.text: Synced at 15:50Z (ArgoCD about 3 minutes after the push), pod Running after 42 s with 0 restarts, the ExternalSecret SecretSynced, no model download, no CUDA error. The log at INFO shows only Biasing toward names from <HA API> and Ready, then Processing audio lines, no transcript lines (Loki: none; Vector drop_voice_transcripts stopped increasing). Direct Wyoming round trip with 10 synthetic Spanish commands twice: stop-to-transcript p50 0.91 s (max 0.95 s) against 0.86 s on 2.4.0 measured with the same clips the same day; the three differing transcripts (digits for number words, one "Con" for "Pon") were identical on 2.4.0. GPU memory 1141 MiB before, 1101 MiB after. Not verified: the number of names in the hint list (logged at DEBUG only) and the 20-command spot check by the owner.

docs.title: Conversation agent evaluation for "Kivi": Kiais gateway metrics, a reusable dry-run harness, and what Home Assistant's built-in intents already cover
docs.text:
Status: TARGET_VERIFIED for Kiais fast (full run) and PARTIAL for balanced (lean run); advanced not run (not needed: its latency is already out of range); local models are a separate study Date: 2026-11-05 Device alias / model / firmware / webOS / architecture: none (no TV, no audio, no voice pipeline run). Read-only on the owner's homelab: Kiais custom resources in namespace isidoro and the Prometheus datasource via the Grafana MCP. Power and playback state: not applicable Related research / requirements / issue: satellite-side backlog section 12 (formerly EXP-020 of that repository); the small local models study (formerly EXP-019 there) reuses this harness Risk: read-only on the cluster and Home Assistant. Nothing was changed in Home Assistant, the cluster or on any TV. Only synthetic Spanish test text was sent to Kiais (309 chat requests in total, no real user data). Approval needed / obtained: the owner authorized synthetic text to Kiais and the use of the Kiais key that already exists in his local coding-agent client configuration on the workstation (no hard limit, no needless requests). The key was loaded into the environment of the run only and never printed or stored in any repository, log or result.

Evidence labels used here: documented (read in a source file or custom resource), observed (read from the homelab metrics or API on the date above), inferred (computed from documented material, not run on the real system), hypothesis.

docs.title: Question and falsifiable hypothesis
docs.text:
Which "brain" should answer the Kiwi pipeline's free-form requests (the pipeline is named "Kiwi", the assistant is spelled and called "Kivi"): the Kiais gateway (fast, balanced, advanced) or a local model? This run covers Kiais only and builds the harness the local run will reuse.

Hypotheses to falsify, per tier:

  • H1: tool-call correctness on Spanish home-control phrases is at least 95 % and the answers are fit for TTS (plain Spanish, one or two sentences).
  • H2: the time to the first spoken word (TTFS: tool round plus the first token of the final answer) is under about 3 s at the median for a control phrase.
  • H3: for live-information questions the model uses a tool or says it cannot know, and never invents.
  • H4: failover inside the gateway (including a try of the unreliable z800 backend) does not add visible latency.

Outcome (details in the chat measurements section): H1 borderline (93 % overall, 94 % on action phrases, against 95 %), H2 borderline (TTFS p50 3.06 s against 3 s), H3 holds, H4 not testable (no failover or z800 try happened in the run).

docs.title: Prerequisites and safe baseline
docs.text:
• Read-only cluster access (kubectl --context=grigri -n isidoro get ...) and the Grafana MCP grafana-grigri (datasource prometheus, 45 days of Kiais series).
  • Public listing works without a key: GET https://isidoro.grigri.cloud/v1/models returns balanced, fast, advanced (observed).
  • POST /v1/chat/completions without a key returns 401 invalid_api_key (observed, one request).
  • The key used for the runs is the one already present in the owner's local client configuration for the gateway on the workstation; it was read by a wrapper into one environment variable for the duration of one command. No key was taken from cluster secrets or volumes.

docs.title: A. Offline checks (done)
docs.text:
python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval -p 'test_agent_eval.py'   # 33 tests, local scripted server, no network
python3 scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/run.py plan                             # 120 jobs, about 237 requests per full run

docs.title: B. Kiais chat runs (done 2026-11-05 from the workstation over the public URL)
docs.text:
export AGENT_EVAL_API_KEY=...        # loaded for the command only; never commit, print or paste it
python3 scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/run.py run --base-url https://isidoro.grigri.cloud/v1 --model fast --label kiais-fast
python3 scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/run.py run --base-url https://isidoro.grigri.cloud/v1 --model balanced --label kiais-balanced \
    --categories general,live,followup
python3 scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/run.py run --base-url https://isidoro.grigri.cloud/v1 --model balanced --label kiais-balanced \
    --categories control --ids c01,c05,c10,c15,c18,c19,c27,c35,c38,c39,c41,c44 --repeat-control 1
python3 scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/run.py summarize ~/webos-voice-satellite/devices/private/kivi/kiais-fast/*

Requests sent: 11 in two smoke tests (the first one exposed the tool-name streaming issue described below), 221 for fast and 77 for balanced: 309 in total, plus one unauthenticated request. The harness counts requests in request_ledger.jsonl next to the results and refuses to exceed --total-budget (default 600) or --max-requests per run. After a grading rule or the fake resolver changes, run.py regrade DIR re-executes the stored calls and re-grades offline, with no requests (used here after a resolver fix, see below).

docs.text:
python3 -m venv /tmp/v && /tmp/v/bin/pip install hassil==3.12.1 home-assistant-intents==2026.10.6 pyyaml
