docs.title: Method
docs.text:
Harness (scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/, Python, standard library plus PyYAML):

  • Any OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint, streaming. For a local model use Ollama's OpenAI-compatible mode (--base-url http://HOST:11434/v1, --warmup to load the model first, --extra-body '{"options": {...}}' for Ollama options). No Kiais-specific code. The API key comes only from an environment variable and is never written to results.
  • Per request: TTFT (first content or tool-call token), time to any first token (reasoning counts), total, finish reason, model field and response headers that look like a backend or request id (kept to find out which backend served, when the gateway exposes it).
  • Per phrase: the user text, the model's tool calls, a fake result fed back (dry run: nothing is executed), up to four rounds, then the final spoken text. TTFS (time to first speech) is the time of all tool rounds plus the TTFT of the final answer; that is what a user waits through.
  • Grading (scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/grade.py) is automatic and deterministic: the fake Home Assistant resolves each call's name, area, floor and domain slots to entity ids, and the expectation names the tool and the entity ids (exact, include, within), value slots (brightness, position, temperature, volume_level, derived volume_dir and total_seconds) and answer regexes. Alternatives (any_of) cover legitimate variants (HassTurnOff or HassSetPosition 0 to lower a blind; a clarifying question for an ambiguous request). Extra state-changing calls fail a phrase. "First-call ok" counts only the first round; "pass" allows a retry after a tool error (as Home Assistant's model loop does). Spoken-format checks (no markdown, no emoji, Spanish, "Kivi" not "Kiwi", length) are reported separately.
  • Phrases (scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/phrases_es.yaml): 44 home control (action 31, state questions 4, ambiguous 3, colloquial 5, unknown target 1, plus lights, blinds, awning, air conditioning, TV volume/mute/pause on "la tele", timers, fan, area words salón/cocina/dormitorio/baño/terraza), 15 general, 11 live-information (weather now, rain tomorrow, time, date, calendar today and week, bitcoin, football result, traffic, news, weekend forecast) and 6 two-turn follow-ups. 76 phrases, 120 jobs with control repeated twice.
  • Fake home (scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/inventory_es.yaml): written for this test, with duplicate names across areas (a "Luz del techo" in three rooms) so ambiguity is real; the satellite sits in "Salón". No real names or identifiers.
  • Tool schemas and system prompt (scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/ha_fake.py): 26 tools modelled on Home Assistant 2026.10.4. Documented (read from the 2026.10.4 tag): in 2026.10.4 the Assist LLM API is assembled from per-integration llm.py platforms, and tools are namespaced <domain>__<Name>: intent__HassTurnOn, intent__HassTurnOff, intent__HassSetPosition, intent__HassStopMoving, intent__HassCancelAllTimers, intent__HassStartTimer and the other timer tools (only offered to a device that supports timers), light__HassLightSet (brightness 0 to 100, color, temperature), climate__HassClimateSetTemperature, media_player__HassMediaPause/Unpause/Next/Previous/PlayerMute/PlayerUnmute/SetVolume (volume_level 0 to 100)/SetVolumeRelative (volume_step up, down or -100 to 100), fan__HassFanSetSpeed, calendar__get_events (calendar, range today or week), homeassistant__GetLiveContext (name, domain, area) and llm__GetDateTime. There is no weather tool and no tool for the current climate temperature: those go through GetLiveContext. The Home Assistant prompt fragments (device-control instruction, area sentence, dynamic-context text, static context list) are copied from the source; the Spanish persona is ours. Unconfirmed: the exact device-class enums for the on/off tools (written from memory), the argument-name mapping in IntentTool beyond what the source shows, and the shape of real tool results (modelled on the source: action_done with success targets, errors as {"error": type, "error_text": ...} as in chat_log.py).
  • Resolver approximation: strip().casefold() name matching without accent folding, area/floor/domain/device-class filtering, the satellite area preferred for duplicate names, required states for pause/next. It is not Home Assistant's matcher.

Metrics: Prometheus on the homelab, metric family kiais_*: kiais_requests_total{model,backend,status,stream}, kiais_backend_attempts_total{...,outcome}, kiais_failover_events_total{...,reason}, kiais_requests_with_failover_total, kiais_candidate_skips_total{...,reason}, kiais_ttft_seconds_bucket, kiais_request_duration_seconds_bucket, kiais_dispatch_attempts, kiais_circuit_breaker_state. Windows of 30 days (ending 2026-11-05) and 7 days; percentiles are histogram_quantile over bucket increases, so they are interpolated and coarse. In these series model is the tier (fast, balanced, advanced) and backend is the upstream; the model behind a backend comes from the Model custom resources.

docs.title: Expected evidence and failure interpretation
docs.text:
• If the key is issued, H1 fails for a tier when the tool-call pass rate on action phrases is below 95 %; the per-phrase JSON shows whether the cause is wrong arguments (a name instead of area plus domain), extra calls, or no call.
  • H2 fails when the TTFS p50 for control phrases is above about 3 s; the split between the tool round and the final answer shows where the time goes.
  • H3 fails on any invented number or fact in the live-information phrases (must_not_regex and the limitation regex).
  • Do not treat the fake-home pass rate as the owner's real home pass rate: names, areas and entity counts differ.

docs.title: Tier definitions (documented, Kiais custom resources, read 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
Tier Backends in order (model on upstream) fast kimi-k2.5 on alibaba-coding-plan; mimo-v2.6-flash-free on opencode; qwen3.6-35b-a3b on z800 (the owner's PC, excluded from conclusions: the owner says it is not reliable); qwen3.8-flash-next on millaguie (llm.millaguie.net); qwen3.8-flash on alibaba-token-plan balanced qwen3.6-35b-a3b on z800; qwen3.7-plus on alibaba-coding-plan; deepseek-v4.1-flash-free on opencode; qwen3.8-flash-next on millaguie; qwen3.8-flash on alibaba-token-plan advanced deepseek-v4.1-flash on millaguie-advanced; qwen3.8-max on alibaba-token-plan; gpt-6.1-sol on chatgpt-oauth

Routing policy default (documented): 3 retries with a 0.5 s base and 10 s cap, circuit breaker opening after 5 failures for 30 s, quota demotion at 80 %, cache-aware routing and session affinity. Gateway environment (documented): upstream connect timeout 5 s, stream idle timeout 300 s, slow-first-content degradation threshold 30 s. The Upstream list currently shows z800 as Unreachable with the circuit Open and not eligible (observed; kiais_circuit_breaker_state is 2 on both gateway pods).

docs.title: Traffic and which backend served (observed, 30 days to 2026-11-05)
docs.text:
Tier Served (HTTP 200) per 30 d Per day Served last 7 d Backends that served (30 d) fast 2 347 about 78 97 alibaba-token-plan 1 708 (73 %), alibaba-coding-plan 521 (22 %), millaguie 105, opencode 13 balanced 133 303 about 4 440 31 659 alibaba-coding-plan 69 125 (52 %), alibaba-token-plan 58 801 (44 %), millaguie 3 088, z800 1 605, opencode 630 advanced 13 384 about 450 5 286 alibaba-token-plan 6 887, chatgpt-oauth 5 447, millaguie-advanced 1 050

In the last 7 days all 97 fast requests were served by alibaba-coding-plan (kimi-k2.5): the serving backend shifts over time (cache-aware routing and quota demotion), so a single tier name does not mean a single model. The fast tier carries very little traffic, in bursts (for example 279 requests on one day, 0 to 10 on most), so its caches and connections are often cold. The traffic on balanced is dominated by large coding-agent requests: the latency figures below describe that workload, not short voice turns.

docs.title: Errors and failover (observed, 30 days)
docs.text:
Tier 5xx without a backend Requests with at least one failover Failover share of served Backend attempt outcomes other than success fast 502: 39, 503: 744 (about 24 % of all fast requests, 783 of 783 within 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-15; none from 2026-10-16 to 2026-11-05) 206 8.8 % alibaba-coding-plan client_error 76; opencode client_error 34; z800 network_error 14 balanced 502: 576, 503: 4 765 (3.4 %), 504: 1 18 164 13.6 % z800 network_error 2 241 and timeout 76; opencode client_error 782; rate_limited several hundred advanced 503: 237 (1.7 %) 1 956 14.6 % chatgpt-oauth rate_limited 801

Correction found during the chat run: kiais_requests_with_failover_total also counts requests where a candidate was only skipped (for example z800 through its open circuit). During the fast run of 2026-11-05 about 50 of 235 requests were counted "with failover" while the only attempt outcome was a first-try success on one backend and the only event was z800 circuit_open skipping. So the failover shares in the table above overstate real retries; the real failover events (below) are about 49 in 30 days for fast.

Failover reasons for fast: alibaba-coding-plan client_error 31 (rejected requests), opencode client_error 4, z800 network 14; skip reasons: cooldown 845 (coding-plan), 777 (token-plan), 862 (opencode), circuit_open 986 (z800) and 55 (opencode), slow_first_content_degraded 7 (token-plan). So z800 is, for fast, almost always skipped through its open circuit rather than tried first: 14 network failures in 30 days against 986 skips. The cost of one try of z800: not measured. The gateway configuration gives a ceiling of the 5 s connect timeout plus the retry delay of at least 0.5 s for a refused or unreachable host; the metrics have no per-attempt duration for failed attempts. Hypothesis: a try while the circuit is closed adds up to about 5.5 s once, then the circuit opens after 5 failures and later requests skip it.

docs.title: Latency of the gateway (observed, 30 days; 7 days in brackets)
docs.text:
Tier TTFT p50 / p95 (s) Total p50 / p95 (s) fast 1.89 / 4.52 (2.93 / 5.06) 6.25 / 28.9 (4.17 / 11.5) balanced 2.54 / 8.06 (2.38 / 5.91) 7.60 / 35.5 (7.35 / 31.4) advanced 4.57 / 16.2 (4.55 / 15.98) 12.9 / 89.7 (11.3 / 76.5)

Per backend in fast, 30 days:

Backend (model) Served TTFT p50 / p95 (s) Total p50 / p95 (s) alibaba-coding-plan (kimi-k2.5) 521 2.15 / 4.70 3.44 / 13.5 alibaba-token-plan (qwen3.8-flash) 1 708 1.87 / 4.46 7.40 / 31.5 millaguie (qwen3.8-flash-next) 105 0.99 / 1.45 6.17 / 29.6 opencode (mimo-v2.6-flash-free) 13 2.92 / 9.31 9.38 / 39.4

The backlog's earlier figure ("TTFT p50 about 1.5 s on only 2 requests") is superseded by this: on about 2 350 requests the fast TTFT p50 is 1.9 s over 30 days and 2.9 s over the last 7. Caveats: the series mix client workloads and prompt sizes; it is not known whether the gateway's TTFT counts reasoning tokens (a thinking model can show a long TTFT before any spoken text); totals depend on output length, which is short for voice.

Implication for H2 (inferred, before the chat run): a control phrase through an LLM costs two round trips (tool call, then the answer), so with a gateway TTFT of about 2 to 3 s the time to first speech would be roughly 4 to 6 s, before TTS and the satellite. Home Assistant can start TTS while the answer streams, but the tool round cannot be streamed away. The chat run below measured it: TTFS p50 is 3.06 s on fast, in line with this estimate at the low end. This is a latency argument for keeping simple control off the LLM (below).

docs.title: Which phrases Home Assistant's built-in intents would handle (inferred, prefer_local_intents)
docs.text:
Documented (source 2026.10.4, assist_pipeline and conversation/default_agent.py): with prefer_local_intents on, the pipeline first tries a strict match of the text against the Spanish sentences using exposed entity names, areas and floors, with the satellite's area as context. When the pipeline's agent is an LLM with control, matches of HassGetState and HassMediaSearchAndPlay are ignored so they do not interfere with the LLM; a "no match" kind of handler error (unknown name or area, nothing in the required state) is ignored too and the text goes to the agent; only successes (and failed-to-handle errors) answer locally. Home Assistant 2026.10.4 pins hassil==3.12.1 and home-assistant-intents==2026.10.6; the analysis used exactly those versions with the same recognize_best call and slot lists (names with domain and device-class context, areas, floors, satellite area), and mapped each recognised intent to the fake tool resolver (scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/builtin_intents.py).

Result for the 44 control phrases Count Phrases handled locally with the expected targets 29 c01-c04, c06-c12, c17-c25, c27-c34, c42; for example "Enciende la luz del salón", "Sube el brillo de la lámpara de pie al 80", "Baja la persiana del salón", "Pon el volumen de la tele al 30", "Silencia la tele", "Pausa la tele", "Pon un temporizador de una hora y media", "Enciende la cafetera", "Baja el volumen" handled locally, no LLM-tool twin 1 c35 "¿Qué temperatura hace en el salón?" (HassClimateGetTemperature, answers from the climate entity) recognised but ignored (goes to the LLM) 5 c05, c13, c15, c16, c26: "Pon la luz del salón al cuarenta por ciento", "Pon la persiana del salón a la mitad", "Pon el aire del salón a 22 grados" and similar "pon ..." forms match the media-search sentence first no match (goes to the LLM) 9 c14 "Para el toldo", c36 and c37 (state questions), c38-c41 (colloquial: "Está muy oscuro aquí", "Quita la tele", "Ponme la tele más bajita", "Apágalo todo en la cocina"), c43, c44 (a room that does not exist)

Also locally: "¿Qué hora es?" and "¿Qué día es hoy?" (HassGetCurrentTime, HassGetCurrentDate); nothing for the weather, the calendar, general questions or the open-world live questions. About two thirds of the control phrases (30 of 44) would never reach the agent; the ones left are the colloquial, ambiguous, numeric "pon ..." and state phrases, which is where the agent matters.

Limits of this inference: the names in the fake home were chosen to be natural Spanish names; the owner's real entity names, aliases and exposure decide the real hit rate. Strict matching needs exact wording; no fuzzy matching. The "ignored" group depends on the LLM agent having the control feature (true for an LLM with the Assist API). The result must be rechecked with the owner's real names before it becomes a decision.

docs.title: Chat measurements (observed, 2026-11-05, workstation to https://isidoro.grigri.cloud/v1, streaming, temperature 0.2)
docs.text:
fast (model name fast; control phrases twice, every other category once; 126 graded turns, 221 requests). Grading is automatic; "review" phrases (a joke, a free explanation, "hace mucho calor") are excluded from the percentages.

Group Turns Pass Pass % (without review) First-call ok % TTFS p50 / p95 (s) Total p50 / p95 (s) control, all 88 80 93 92 3.06 / 3.69 3.47 / 4.36 control, action 62 58 94 94 3.06 / 3.69 3.47 / 4.23 control, ambiguous (clarify or sensible default) 6 6 100 100 3.06 / 3.72 3.42 / 4.21 control, colloquial 10 6 75 (2 review) 75 2.65 / 3.51 3.34 / 4.77 control, state questions 8 8 100 100 3.18 / 3.58 3.51 / 4.36 control, missing target ("luz del garaje") 2 2 100 n/a 1.39 / 1.47 2.65 / 2.67 follow-ups (two turns each) 12 12 100 100 2.59 / 4.24 2.99 / 4.60 general questions 15 13 100 (2 review) n/a 1.20 / 1.65 1.71 / 4.22 live information 11 11 100 n/a 0.87 / 2.95 1.78 / 4.57 all 126 116 95 93 2.78 / 3.67 3.23 / 4.36
  • Request TTFT (all requests): p50 1.30 s, p95 1.77 s. In a control phrase the tool-call round has a median TTFT of 1.5 s and the final-answer round 1.25 s (82 two-round phrases), so the time to first speech is about 3 s: H2 is borderline (3.06 s against 3 s), not met with margin. This includes the network from the workstation to the public URL.
  • Failures of fast were the same in both repetitions (no phrase differed between the two runs): "Para el toldo" and "Cancela el temporizador" (it asks what to do or which timer instead of acting, 4 of the 4 failed action turns) and "Quita la tele" (it pauses instead of turning off; colloquial). Everything else passed, including the arguments (brightness, position, temperature, volume, timer seconds), the area-plus-domain use for areas and the satellite-area preference for the three "Luz del techo".
  • Live information: it called GetLiveContext for the weather now, calendar__get_events with today or week, answered the date and time from the prompt, and for the bitcoin price, a football result, traffic, news, tomorrow's rain and the weekend forecast it said it cannot check them ("Solo tengo acceso al tiempo actual"). No invented figures: H3 holds on these 11 phrases.
  • Spoken format: 100 % of the answers were plain Spanish without markdown or emoji, and the name was never written "Kiwi". Answers were one or two short sentences.
  • H1 (at least 95 %): 93 % overall and 94 % on action phrases, just under the threshold, and the misses are underspecified requests where asking back is defensible. On the clearly specified phrases it is 100 %.
  • Which backend served: the response gives only model: fast and no backend header. The gateway metrics for the run window show all 235 fast requests served by alibaba-coding-plan (kimi-k2.5), all first-try 200, zero real failovers; z800 appeared only as 50 skips through its open circuit. So H4 could not be tested (no retry or z800 try happened) and the run carries no cost of a z800 failover.

balanced (lean run: 32 general, live and follow-up turns plus 12 control phrases once, chosen to include the hard ones; 77 requests; the control phrases overlap with fast's):

Group Turns Pass % (without review) TTFS p50 / p95 (s) Total p50 / p95 (s) control (12 chosen phrases) 12 92 6.64 / 35.85 6.93 / 36.39 follow-ups 12 83 5.92 / 12.79 6.24 / 12.91 general 15 100 (2 review) 3.37 / 9.13 4.02 / 9.27 live 11 100 8.36 / 39.01 9.34 / 39.30 all 50 94 6.37 / 17.63 6.59 / 17.85

balanced is about twice as slow as fast (TTFT p50 3.0 s, p95 15.7 s; one control answer took 36 s and one live answer 39 s) and not more accurate on the same phrases: on the 12 shared control phrases fast passed 11 and balanced 11. Its follow-up misses were clarifying questions where fast just acted ("which light?" for the two lights of the bedroom). The tier is shared with the coding workload, so its serving backend cannot be attributed to this run. advanced was not run: the 30-day gateway TTFT p50 of 4.6 s and p95 of 16 s already rule it out for voice.

Method notes on the grading, for honesty: after the first pass the resolver was corrected so that a whole-area "turn off" no longer includes sensors, case differences in answer checks were ignored ("Veintinueve" against "veintinueve"), and acting device by device inside an allowed set is no longer an "extra action"; the stored calls were re-graded offline (regrade). Two of those corrections turned fast failures (state question with "22 grados y 4 décimas", "apágalo todo en la cocina") into passes; the model's outputs were not touched. The first attempt on the gateway also exposed that it repeats the whole tool name in every stream chunk (some backends do); the client was fixed to accept that and covered by a test.

docs.title: Privacy note
docs.text:
• This run: about 300 requests with synthetic Spanish phrases, the fake home and the system prompt were sent to the gateway; for fast the metrics show they were all served by alibaba-coding-plan (Alibaba, kimi-k2.5); the balanced requests could have gone to any of its backends. No real user data was involved. The harness sends only the synthetic phrases in phrases_es.yaml, a fake home, and the system prompt; results (which contain the model's answers and fake tool results) go to a git-ignored directory outside this repository (~/webos-voice-satellite/devices/private/kivi/). Never commit them.
  • Which backends would see the text when a tier is used (documented from the custom resources; the data-handling terms of each provider were not verified): fast can go to Alibaba (two plans: kimi-k2.5 and qwen3.8-flash), opencode (a free tier, where free usually means the text may be retained or used for training; unverified), millaguie (a third-party host), and z800 (the owner's PC); balanced adds the same; advanced can go to millaguie-advanced, Alibaba and OpenAI via ChatGPT OAuth. The routing is dynamic, so the owner cannot choose which one answers a given request.
  • For real use every utterance, and the static home context in the prompt (room, device and alias names, plus live state when a tool is called), would leave the house to those providers. That is the main cost of option C in the backlog and the reason a local agent or prefer_local_intents for most control phrases is attractive.

docs.title: Conclusion and confidence
docs.text:
• fast is good enough in accuracy and the right tier, but its latency is at the limit. On 126 graded turns: 93 % pass on control (94 % on action phrases, 100 % on state questions, follow-ups and live information), 100 % spoken-format compliance, no invented data. Misses are underspecified or colloquial phrases ("Para el toldo", "Cancela el temporizador", "Quita la tele"), and they repeat deterministically. Confidence: medium-high for this fake home and phrase set (88 control turns, 2 repetitions identical); lower for the owner's real names and speech, which the synthetic text does not cover.
  • Latency: time to first speech p50 3.06 s and p95 3.7 s for a control phrase through an LLM (two round trips, about 1.5 s TTFT each), measured over the public URL from the workstation, with all requests served by one backend (kimi-k2.5 on alibaba-coding-plan) and no failover. Gateway metrics over 30 days (other workloads) agree: TTFT p50 1.9 s, p95 4.5 s. This is acceptable for conversation, slow for "turn on the light".
  • balanced: not worth it. About twice as slow (TTFS p50 6.4 s, p95 17.6 s, outliers of 36 and 39 s) with no accuracy gain on the shared phrases. advanced (not run) is out on the gateway's own latency (TTFT p50 4.6 s, p95 16 s).
  • Failover: none occurred; z800 is skipped through its open circuit at no cost. Its cost when tried stays unmeasured (hypothesis: up to about 5.5 s once per circuit cycle).
  • Recommendation (confidence medium): use Kiais fast as the Kivi fallback agent, together with prefer_local_intents = true, so that about two thirds of the control phrases (30 of 44 on the fake home, inferred) are answered locally in well under a second and only the colloquial, state, numeric "pon ..." and general requests pay the roughly 3 s of the LLM. Keep balanced and advanced out of the voice path. The privacy position still has to be accepted by the owner: every utterance and the home's device names go to Alibaba and possibly other providers behind the tier, whose terms were not checked. The local models study should be compared against these numbers (same harness, same prompt and tools): pass 93 %, TTFS p50 3.06 s.

docs.title: Rollback and cleanup
docs.text: Nothing outside this repository was changed: no Home Assistant, cluster, TV or audio action. To remove the work: delete scripts/voice-assistant/agent_eval/ and this section of the docs. Delete the private results directory (~/webos-voice-satellite/devices/private/kivi/) when no longer needed. The Kiais key was used from the owner's existing client configuration; nothing to revoke.

docs.title: Follow-ups / unresolved questions
docs.text:
1. Owner: accept or reject sending utterances and the home's device names to the providers behind fast (Alibaba and others); read their data terms if option C is chosen.
  2. Whether Home Assistant can reach Kiais at all: the core openai_conversation integration has no base-URL option (backlog #12 of the satellite repository), so a custom or HACS integration may be needed; verify tool calling and streaming through it, since this harness talks to the gateway directly.
  3. Re-run with the owner's real entity names, aliases and areas (read-only export, not committed) for both the LLM pass rate and the built-in-intents hit rate (section C).
  4. Cost of one z800 try (measure with a controlled request while z800 is up and while it is down; needs the owner's agreement because it targets his PC).
  5. Compare with the local models by running the same harness against Ollama's /v1.
  6. Whether the gateway's TTFT includes reasoning tokens, and whether a thinking model needs enable_thinking: false for voice (the fast Model resource has a compatibility variant for Alibaba that does this for none).
  7. Confirm the tool names, argument shapes and result shapes against a live Home Assistant (the harness is modelled on the 2026.10.4 source only), and the end-to-end latency through the satellite, which adds STT, TTS and the network on the HA side.
  8. Re-measure fast at a different time of day; this run is one afternoon with all requests on one backend.

docs.title: Decision models for Kivi: can a small classifier rescue the commands the built-in intents miss?
docs.text:
Status: DONE for the synthetic corpus, the fake homes of kivi-fake-v1 (text) and the owner's real names (text, counts only); offline, measured on the workstation Date: 2026-11-05 Systems: workstation z800 (Ryzen 9 5950X 16 cores, RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB, shared with another GPU job during the runs); inferred for prusik (Zen 4 CPU, GTX 1060 3 GB Pascal sm_61) Related: small local models (corpus, transcripts, embedding router, GPU budget), conversation agent design, conversation agent evaluation (phrases, fake home, grader) Risk: offline. Home Assistant was read once, read-only (registry lists, exposure list and states over the websocket API; no service call, no conversation request). No cluster change, no TV, no Kiais request. Scripts: scripts/voice-assistant/decision_models/ on top of agent_eval/ and small_models/

Evidence labels: documented (model card, package source, version named), measured (run on z800 in this study), inferred (computed from the above, not run on the target), hypothesis. All audio is synthetic (Piper voices, TV-content mixes); no real voice was used.

docs.title: Question
docs.text:
Kivi's pipeline today: Whisper large-v3-turbo on the GTX 1060, then Home Assistant's built-in intents (prefer_local_intents, about 1 s end to end), and everything they do not answer goes to the Kiais LLM (about 4.1 s for a command, about 2.3 s for a general question; design note). Can a small non-generative decision model (picks one option per typed question with a probability, generates no text) sit between the two and execute the home commands the built-in intents miss, fast and without wrong actions, handing everything it is unsure about, and every general question, to Kiais?

built-in intents miss -> decision stage: request type, action, area, device kind (one pass),
                         then which device if several match; our code parses the number
   |- every used answer at or above the threshold, and the combination is valid -> execute locally
   |- otherwise (unsure, general question, invalid combination)                    -> Kiais

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
1. Not worth wiring in as they are (measured). Used zero-shot (typed questions over the home's options, no training), no candidate rescues a useful share of the missed commands at a near-zero wrong-action rate. With the gate set so that wrong actions stay at about 1 % of what reaches the stage, the decision models execute correctly 0 to 8 % of the commands the built-in intents miss on the corpus transcripts, 4 to 6 % on the kivi-fake-v1 text, 3 to 6 % on its audio subset, and at most 1 of 27 on commands built from the owner's real names. Everything else still goes to Kiais.
  2. The embedding and fuzzy-matching baseline is as good or better on everything except the corpus: 11 % against 4 to 6 % on kivi-fake-v1 text (paired McNemar p < 1e-6), about the same rescues on audio. Its confidence is coarse, though: on audio it cannot be gated below 1.6 % wrong actions, because Whisper drops the question marks and state questions ("¿Está abierta la luz?") look like orders.
  3. Best decision model: Quyet-1.0-Tiny (183 M, Apache-2.0) with English instructions: 20 of 265 missed corpus commands (8 %, against 3 for the baseline, p < 0.001), 6 % on fake-v1 text and audio. Laya multilingual (322 M) is close to chance zero-shot on the action and area questions in Spanish, as its card warns ("not a zero-shot decision engine"); the English Laya root does not understand Spanish. Quyet-Small (328 M) is no better than Tiny.
  4. The confidence gate does not transfer: a threshold fitted on half of the phrases gives up to 17 wrong actions on the other half. Negatives are not the problem at those thresholds (TV dialogue with command verbs, general, live and chit-chat questions: none acted on in the text sets, 1 of 54 TV-dialogue transcripts on audio by Quyet-Tiny en); the problem is that a safe threshold hands off almost every command too.
  5. Speed and memory are not the obstacle: one decision of the Spanish-capable candidates takes 15 to 360 ms on 16 CPU threads and 17 to 80 ms on the workstation GPU (fp32). In fp32, only the baseline (0.75 GiB) and Quyet-Tiny (0.90 GiB, just) fit the 1.0 GiB left on the GTX 1060; Laya multilingual and Quyet-Small (1.5 GiB) do not. A CPU on prusik would do.

Recommendation: do not add a zero-shot decision stage to Home Assistant. If the owner wants a local decider, it has to be trained on Spanish home commands (the decider PoC has the data, and custom sentences cover much of the same room more cheaply), then re-measured with this harness. The candidate to fine-tune is Quyet-Tiny, or a small classifier on the embedding model, run on the prusik CPU (no risk to Whisper's VRAM, about 0.15 s per decision) rather than on the 1060.

docs.text:
Candidate Checkpoint (pinned revision) Encoder, parameters (measured) Licence Languages (card) Input and limits Runtime used Laya multilingual convaiinnovations/laya, subfolder multilingual (7b928d8) mmBERT-base + decision head, 321.9 M Apache-2.0 "100+ languages"; MASSIVE intent in 13 non-English languages 0.451 (card) state text plus typed questions (choice, score, noul); option text shares a 256-token head budget; up to 1024 tokens laya 0.4.9 (PyPI, 2026-10-17) Laya (English root) same repository, root (7b928d8) ModernBERT-large + head, 421 M (card) Apache-2.0 English ("English only on root", card) as above, 512 tokens laya 0.4.9 Quyet-1.0-Tiny chinhnc/Quyet-1.0-Tiny (fba8ca9) first 16 layers of mmBERT-small + wide option-query head, 182.9 M Apache-2.0 (keep NOTICE) "English; also tuned for Vietnamese. Other languages work, with lower accuracy" same question format; at most 10 options per question; 8192 tokens; temperature-calibrated per type and option count quyet 1.0.2 Quyet-1.0-Small chinhnc/Quyet-1.0-Small (f007dfe) SEA-LION-ModernBERT-300M + 2-layer head, 327.6 M Apache-2.0 as Tiny as Tiny quyet 1.0.2 Baseline (no new model) ibm-granite/granite-embedding-278m-multilingual (a9cb533) XLM-R type encoder, CLS pooling, 278.0 M Apache-2.0 12 languages including Spanish (card) 3 nearest neighbours over synthetic training phrases for request type and action; fuzzy string matching (rapidfuzz) of area, device kind and device against names and aliases; numbers by our parser transformers 5.22

The owner's description of Laya ("ModernBERT-large, about 421 M, multilingual") mixes two checkpoints: the 421 M root checkpoint is English-only by its card, the multilingual one is mmBERT-base with 322 M parameters. Both were run; the multilingual one is the relevant candidate.

Card caveats that matter here (documented): Laya's base checkpoints are "near chance on typed-decisions zero-shot ... a fast base to specialise, not a zero-shot decision engine", they ship over-confident and laya-multilingual has no fitted temperatures (all 1.0 in its config); action.act_probability "carries no usable signal yet", so the gate uses the answer probability. Quyet ships fitted temperatures but names only English and Vietnamese as tuned languages.

Code review before running (documented): both packages load only safetensors weights, JSON configs and a local tokenizer (snapshot_download restricted to those files; no repository .py, no trust_remote_code, no pickle). Quyet's manifest SHA-256 sums matched. The newest laya (0.4.24, uploaded the same morning) adds a dependency on the same author's new vegaml package, so the 19-day-old 0.4.9 without it was used; the card says the checkpoints did not change. On CUDA both packages autocast (Laya fp16 on pre-Ampere GPUs, Quyet bf16); for the GTX 1060 (Pascal sm_61: no bf16, very slow fp16) the evaluation turns autocast off and runs fp32 everywhere.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
• The decision stage (decide.py, identical for every candidate): one forward pass with five choice questions: request type (home command, timer, state question, anything else), action (ten options: on, off, set a value, volume up and down, mute, unmute, pause or stop, resume, next), timer action, area (every area of the home plus "no area named" and "the whole home") and device kind (lights, blinds, awnings, gates, climate, TV, speakers, fans, plugs, everything; only kinds the home has, each with up to six device names in its description). When the area and kind leave several devices, a second question asks which one (or all of them). Questions with more than ten options are split into knockout rounds. Our code parses the value (digits, Spanish number words, "y medio", "a la mitad", "al máximo") and the timer length, resolves the entities and maps the decision to a Home Assistant intent call. Invalid combinations (a volume action on a light, a set command without a number, a kind with no device in the area) hand off.
  • Gate: the minimum, over the questions the decision used, of the probability of the chosen option. Swept from 0 to 0.999. The chosen threshold is the lowest one whose wrong actions are at most 1 % of the items that reach the stage; it is fitted in-sample, so a phrase-split check (fit on half of the phrases, apply to the other half) is reported as well.
  • Instruction variants for the decision models: Spanish (es) or English (en) question and option texts (the state is always the Spanish transcript), and neutral option keys A, B, ... with the meaning only in the description (esN, enN; Laya's card suggests this when label keys dominate).
  • Outcome of an item that reaches the stage: rescued (the call matches the phrase's expectation from agent_eval: intent, exact target entities, value), wrong action (any executed call that does not, and any call on a general, live or state question, an unknown target or a two-action request), handed off to Kiais.
  • Test sets:
  • Corpus: Whisper large-v3-turbo transcripts of the 69 graded single-turn phrases of agent_eval spoken by the 5 intelligible Piper voices, with the verbs-only Whisper prompt (the shipped one), clean and mixed with TV content at +5 and 0 dB (run turbo_b5_vonly of the small local models study; 1035 transcripts). Each transcript first goes through the built-in matcher (agent_eval/builtin_intents.py, hassil 3.12.1 and home-assistant-intents 2026.10.6 as in Home Assistant 2026.10.4); only what it does not answer reaches the stage. Main subset: the graded home commands it misses (265); negatives: every general, live and state question (420). Sanity: the commands it answers correctly (319), run through the stage as if it came first.
  • kivi-fake-v1 (built by the decider proof-of-concept, read-only here): four fake homes, 17 phrasing styles (direct, polite, short, word order, disfluent, relative, Latin American, Spanish colloquial, implicit, multi-action, state, missing target, out of domain, general, live, chit-chat, TV dialogue with command verbs), template and validated LLM paraphrases, gold intent, entities and value; the text of all 2273 items and Whisper transcripts of a 500-item audio subset at three noise levels.
  • The owner's real names (private): the exposed entities, areas and aliases read once from Home Assistant (read-only), templated commands with gold targets generated from them (real_phrases.py, text only), plus the general and live questions of agent_eval. Only counts are published.
  • Paired tests: exact McNemar on the same items against the baseline (rescued, and wrong actions). Items of the same phrase in different voices or noise levels are not independent, so p-values are indicative.
  • Latency: GPU fp32 on the RTX 4060 Ti with decision_eval.py bench (warm, one process per candidate, 40 distinct clean transcripts twice; the card was shared with another job at 100 % utilisation, so an upper bound). CPU fp32 on 16 threads: the per-decision times of the corpus accuracy run (Ryzen 9 5950X, load average about 8 to 25 from other jobs). Peak VRAM: torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated and the process's own nvidia-smi figure (includes the CUDA context).

docs.title: 1. Corpus transcripts (verbs-only Whisper prompt), measured
docs.text:
What reaches the stage, per noise level (the built-in matcher on the same transcripts): clean 67 missed commands and 138 general, live and state questions; +5 dB 87 and 142; 0 dB 111 and 140. The built-in matcher answered 128, 108 and 83 commands correctly (the sanity set) and acted wrongly on 1 (at 0 dB).

Without a gate (threshold 0, pooled over the three noise levels; 265 missed commands, 420 negatives), what each candidate would do on its own:

Candidate (variant) Missed commands: rescued / wrong Negatives acted on Baseline 129 / 92 87 Laya multilingual (es) 33 / 60 48 Laya English root (en) 20 / 133 137 Quyet-Tiny (es) 55 / 38 42 Quyet-Tiny (enN) 25 / 52 41 Quyet-Small (es) 11 / 44 53

At the chosen threshold (wrong actions at most 1 % of stage inputs; per noise level: rescued / wrong among the missed commands, negatives acted on; "sanity" = of the commands the built-in intents already answer, how many the stage would get right / wrong):

Candidate (variant) Threshold Clean (67 / 138) +5 dB (87 / 142) 0 dB (111 / 140) All: rescued, wrong, handed off Sanity (319): right / wrong Baseline 0.70 0 / 0; 0 2 / 0; 0 1 / 0; 0 3 (1 %), 0, 99 % 41 / 0 Laya multilingual (es) 0.85 1 / 0; 0 0 / 0; 0 2 / 0; 1 3 (1 %), 0, 99 % 60 / 32 Quyet-Tiny (es) 0.65 0 / 0; 0 1 / 1; 0 5 / 0; 0 6 (2 %), 1, 97 % 84 / 8 Quyet-Tiny (enN) 0.70 5 / 0; 0 6 / 1; 0 9 / 0; 0 20 (8 %), 1, 92 % 47 / 11 Quyet-Small (es) 0.60 0 / 0; 0 4 / 0; 0 6 / 1; 0 10 (4 %), 1, 96 % 60 / 30 Laya English root (en) 0.45 0 / 0; 0 2 / 0; 1 3 / 0; 1 5 (2 %), 0, 98 % 38 / 0

Paired against the baseline at each one's threshold (exact McNemar on the 685 stage items): only Quyet-Tiny enN rescues more (20 against 3, p < 0.001; wrong actions 1 against 0, p 1.0); Quyet-Tiny en 10 against 3 (p 0.09), Quyet-Small es 10 against 3 (p 0.09), every other variant p ≥ 0.25. The other variants (en, esN, enN for Laya, esN for Quyet-Tiny, en for Quyet-Small, es for Laya's English root) rescued 0 to 10 at their thresholds; the full tables are reproducible with decision_eval.py report.

The threshold does not transfer (phrase-split check, measured): for Quyet-Tiny enN, a threshold fitted on the odd-numbered phrases (0.6) gives 21 rescued and 17 wrong on the even ones; fitted on the even ones (0.7) it gives 0 and 0 on the odd ones. Laya multilingual: 0 rescued and 7 wrong in one direction. The confidence does not separate right from wrong reliably enough to set a threshold that holds on new phrases.

Why (per-question accuracy against hand-labelled correct answers for 23 control phrases and every general question, all voices and noise levels, measured):

Question Baseline Laya multilingual es Quyet-Tiny es Quyet-Tiny en Quyet-Small es Request type (735) 84 % 41 % 70 % 83 % 64 % Action (315) 71 % 44 % 50 % 40 % 13 % Area (315) 96 % 51 % 47 % 48 % 39 % Device kind (315) 92 % 84 % 84 % 89 % 80 % Timer action (30) 47 % 97 % 93 % 93 % 97 %

Zero-shot, the decision models are close to chance on the action and the area in Spanish (ten and seven options), and Laya's median confidence is about the same for its right and wrong answers to the request type (0.78 and 0.76). They do recognise the device kind and the timer action. English instructions helped Quyet-Tiny with the request type (70 to 83 %) but not with the action or the area; neutral option keys did not help either model.

docs.title: 2. kivi-fake-v1, text (2273 items, four fake homes), measured
docs.text:
The built-in matcher answers 395 of the 1776 single-action commands correctly, acts wrongly on 3 and misses 1378 (78 %: the set is built from phrasings the built-in sentences do not cover); it also acts on 7 of the "short" negatives (fragments such as a bare device name). Reaching the stage: 1378 missed commands and 457 negatives (general, live, chit-chat, out of domain, state, missing target, two-action requests, TV dialogue that contains command verbs).

Candidate (variant) Ungated: rescued / wrong; negatives acted on Threshold Rescued Wrong (missed) Negatives acted on Sanity (395): right / wrong Baseline 765 / 537; 303 0.75 148 (11 %) 9 (0.7 %) 8 of 457 63 / 1 Quyet-Tiny (es) 412 / 471; 141 0.85 67 (5 %) 6 0 47 / 1 Quyet-Tiny (en) 342 / 400; 142 0.75 78 (6 %) 16 2 59 / 2 Quyet-Tiny (enN) 284 / 369; 119 0.80 57 (4 %) 13 1 33 / 0 Laya multilingual (es) 196 / 440; 93 0.95 53 (4 %) 9 0 41 / 2

Quyet-Small and the other Laya variants were not run on this set (the corpus already ranked them lower, and the workstation was saturated by other jobs). Paired against the baseline: the baseline rescues significantly more than every decision model (Quyet-Tiny es 59 only-candidate against 140 only-baseline, p < 1e-8; en 67 against 137, p < 1e-6; enN 49 against 140, p < 1e-10), with as many or fewer wrong actions (Quyet-Tiny es 6 against 17, p 0.03; en 18 against 17 and enN 14 against 17, p ≥ 0.7). Phrase-split check for the baseline: 61 rescued and 5 wrong on one half, 76 and 13 on the other.

Per style at the chosen threshold, rescued share of the missed commands (wrong actions in brackets), measured:

Style (missed commands) Baseline Quyet-Tiny en Laya multilingual es direct (187) 14 % (5) 4 % (1) 4 % (0) polite (156) 14 % (0) 4 % (5) 2 % (2) short (161) 14 % (0) 4 % (1) 3 % (0) word order (191) 14 % (1) 3 % (4) 5 % (1) disfluent (181) 9 % (0) 6 % (2) 4 % (0) Latin American (227) 11 % (0) 11 % (3) 4 % (5) Spanish colloquial (163) 4 % (2) 8 % (0) 7 % (0) relative ("un poco más ...", 112) 1 % (1) 4 % (0) 0 % (1)

Negatives acted on at the chosen threshold (baseline / Quyet-Tiny en / Laya): TV dialogue 0 of 48 for all three; general 0 of 40, live 0 of 24, chit-chat 0 of 32, out of domain 0 of 27 for all three; state questions 2 / 0 / 0 of 45; missing target 3 / 0 / 0 of 60; two-action requests 3 / 2 / 0 of 63. At the thresholds that keep wrong actions near 1 %, all of them hand off almost every negative; the cost is that they also hand off 89 to 96 % of the missed commands.

docs.title: kivi-fake-v1, audio subset (500 items × clean, +5 dB, 0 dB; Whisper with the verbs prompt), measured
docs.text:
The built-in matcher answers 56 / 43 / 34 of the 302 commands per noise level (clean / +5 / 0 dB) and misses 245 / 258 / 267; with the negatives, 1326 transcripts reach the stage.

Candidate (variant) Threshold Clean: rescued / wrong; negatives +5 dB 0 dB All (770 missed, 556 negatives): rescued, wrong, negatives acted on Baseline none reaches 1 % (strictest shown) 20 / 3; 6 20 / 2; 6 20 / 1; 3 60 (8 %), 6, 15 (2.7 %) Quyet-Tiny es 0.85 10 / 1; 0 9 / 1; 0 6 / 2; 0 25 (3 %), 4, 0 Quyet-Tiny en 0.75 17 / 2; 0 18 / 2; 1 12 / 3; 0 47 (6 %), 7, 1 Quyet-Tiny enN 0.80 7 / 3; 0 11 / 3; 0 6 / 3; 0 24 (3 %), 9, 0 Laya multilingual es 0.95 11 / 3; 0 11 / 1; 0 5 / 2; 0 27 (4 %), 6, 0

Paired against the baseline: Quyet-Tiny en rescues about as many (44 only-candidate against 57 only-baseline, p 0.23) with fewer wrong actions (8 against 21, p 0.02); Quyet-Tiny es and enN and Laya rescue fewer (p < 0.001) with fewer wrong actions (Laya 6 against 21, p 0.006). The baseline cannot be gated below 1.6 % wrong actions on audio: Whisper drops the question marks, so "¿Está abierta la luz de la terraza?" arrives as "Está abierta la luz de la terraza." and the 3-NN votes "turn on" unanimously (10 of its 15 negatives acted on are such state questions; 3 are two-action requests of which it executes the first, 2 name a device the area does not have). Phrase-split check: Quyet-Tiny en 36 rescued / 1 wrong on one half, 11 / 7 on the other; the baseline 35 / 16 and 28 / 7.

docs.title: 3. The owner's real names (text, counts only), measured
docs.text:
Home Assistant exposes 100 entities to Assist in 5 areas (50 switches, 25 of them without an area; 25 sensors; 5 climate, 4 media players, 6 buttons, 3 lights, 3 covers, 2 fans, 1 vacuum, 1 binary sensor; no entity aliases, Spanish aliases on the areas). The first-pass questions then have 7 areas and 7 device kinds, and "which plug" has up to 50 options (knockout rounds of at most 10). Templated commands with gold targets (95 items: 65 graded commands, 3 state questions, 1 unknown area and the 26 general and live questions; text only, no audio): the built-in matcher answers 38 commands correctly and misses 27; 28 negatives reach the stage.

Candidate (variant) Ungated: rescued / wrong; negatives acted on At 0.5 At the chosen threshold Baseline 20 / 7; 4 13 / 2; 4 0.90: 0 rescued, 0 wrong Quyet-Tiny (es / en / enN) 2 to 4 / 4 to 9; 0 to 1 1 to 2 / 0 to 1; 0 0 or 1 rescued, 0 wrong Laya multilingual (es / en / enN) 0 / 6 to 17; 3 to 5 0 / 2 to 11; 3 0 rescued, 0 wrong Quyet-Small (es / en) 1 to 4 / 6 to 10; 1 to 3 0 / 0 to 1; 0 0 rescued, 0 wrong

With the real home the decision models rescue almost nothing even ungated. The area names are English labels with Spanish aliases, the 67 actionable entity names are all distinct but long (median five words), and the "which device" question over dozens of plugs goes through knockout rounds whose confidences multiply. Of Quyet-Tiny en's ungated failures, most are a wrong device kind or area (8 "no target", 4 media actions on a non-media kind) or a wrong cover action (5 wrong calls on "para ..." and "... a la mitad"). Fuzzy matching of the names does better ungated, but its confidence is too coarse for a safe gate. (Quyet-Small enN was not run here: stopped for time.)

docs.title: 4. Latency and memory
docs.text:
One decision on the fake home is 1.0 to 1.4 forward calls on average (the "which device" question adds a second call when area and kind leave several devices). Warm, fp32, p50 / p95 per decision (measured on the workstation; CPU while other jobs ran, load average about 8 to 25 from other jobs; the CPU figures are the per-item times of the corpus accuracy run, as a dedicated CPU benchmark later ran at load 110 and was discarded; 4 threads was not measured for the same reason):

Candidate CPU 16 threads CPU 4 threads GPU RTX 4060 Ti (shared) GTX 1060 (inferred, ×4.5) Process VRAM fp32 (peak tensors) Fits 1.0 GiB next to Whisper Baseline (granite 278 M + fuzzy) 15 / 22 not measured 17 / 20 about 75 748 MiB (567) yes Quyet-Tiny 151 / 222 not measured 26 / 45 about 120 904 MiB (733) just (926 MiB with the real home's options) Laya multilingual 358 / 476 not measured 76 / 115 about 340 1466 MiB (1288) no Quyet-Small 357 / 494 not measured 80 / 97 about 360 1504 MiB (1314) no Laya English root 1391 / 1775 not measured not measured not measured (421 M parameters) no (inferred)

On the real home the option lists are longer (up to 50 plugs, names of about five words). That was not measured cleanly (the workstation was saturated by other jobs from about 17:50 on). In one contended GPU run, Quyet-Tiny took 206 ms p50 per decision on the real home's lists and the baseline 119 ms in the same conditions, against 26 and 17 ms on the fake home at low load. The longer lists therefore cost at most a modest factor on top of the contention (inferred). Quyet-Tiny's peak process VRAM with the real lists was 926 MiB (measured).

GPU figures on the 4060 Ti are upper bounds (another job kept it at 100 % utilisation). The GTX 1060 column scales them by 4.5, the ratio measured for Whisper's encoder between the two cards (small local models, section 2); it is an inference, not a measurement. VRAM is the process's own nvidia-smi figure on the 4060 Ti (weights, activations and the CUDA context; the tensors alone in brackets); on the 1060 the weights and activations are the same size in fp32, the context size may differ. Only the baseline and Quyet-Tiny fit the 1.0 GiB budget, and Quyet-Tiny only just. Laya multilingual and Quyet-Small would need fp16 storage (very slow on Pascal) or the CPU. On prusik's Zen 4 CPU the CPU columns should be similar or faster (inferred, as in the earlier study).

Against the alternative, every candidate is fast enough: even 0.5 s on a CPU is far below the 3 s the Kiais round trip costs for a command. Latency is not what rules them out; accuracy is.

docs.title: Conclusion and recommendation
docs.text:
• Zero-shot decision models do not earn a place between the built-in intents and Kiais (confidence high for zero-shot use on this kind of data: three test sets, two model families, four instruction variants, and the per-question accuracy shows why: the action and area questions are near chance in Spanish). What they would save is small: with the PoC's bound of about 3 s saved per rescued command, rescuing 6 % of the missed commands saves about 0.2 s per missed command on average, at a wrong-action rate of about 1 % of what reaches the stage.
  • The baseline (no new model) is a fair comparison and often better, but its confidence is too coarse to gate safely, and it acts on state questions once Whisper has dropped the question marks. Not recommended either, as it stands.
  • Where it would run, if a trained version is ever built: the prusik CPU (Quyet-Tiny about 0.15 s per decision on 16 workstation threads, more knockout rounds with many plugs), not the 1060: only Quyet-Tiny and the baseline fit its 1.0 GiB in fp32, and fp16 is slow on Pascal.
  • Wiring (unchanged from the design note): Home Assistant has one agent per pipeline, so a stage like this would be a small custom conversation agent that calls the intents itself and forwards the rest to Kiais with conversation.async_converse. Not proposed now.

docs.title: Reproduce
docs.text:
# workstation, throw-away venv (torch, transformers>=5.17, rapidfuzz, hassil==3.12.1,
# home-assistant-intents==2026.10.6, pyyaml, websockets; laya==0.4.9 and quyet==1.0.2 with --no-deps)
export KIVI_PRIVATE=~/webos-voice-satellite/devices/private/kivi DECISION_MODELS=<hf cache>/hub
cd scripts/voice-assistant/decision_models
python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test_decision_models.py'          # 15 tests, no model
python decision_eval.py run --candidates baseline laya-ml quyet-tiny quyet-small laya-en --langs es en esN enN --device cpu
python decision_eval.py report --langs es en esN enN                     # corpus tables
python decision_eval.py run --fake-v1 <kivi-fake-v1 dir> --tag fakev1-text --candidates baseline quyet-tiny laya-ml --langs es en enN
python decision_eval.py run --fake-v1 <dir> --fake-v1-stt <dir>/stt_fake.csv --tag fakev1-audio ...
python decision_eval.py report --tag fakev1-text --by style
# real names (private output only; admin token in a 0600 file, shredded afterwards)
python fetch_inventory.py --token-file <0600 file> --out $KIVI_PRIVATE/decision-models/inventory_real.yaml
python real_phrases.py --inventory .../inventory_real.yaml --out .../phrases_real.jsonl
python decision_eval.py run --phrases .../phrases_real.jsonl --inventory .../inventory_real.yaml --tag real-text ...
python decision_eval.py bench --candidate quyet-tiny --device cuda       # latency and VRAM

Per-item results (transcripts, decisions, calls) are written as JSONL to $KIVI_PRIVATE/decision-models/ and never committed. The model downloads are pinned to the revisions in the candidates table.

docs.title: Rollback and cleanup
docs.text: Nothing changed in the cluster or Home Assistant. Home Assistant was read once over the websocket API with the Whisper name-fetch token (from its Kubernetes Secret into a 0600 file in memory, shredded afterwards); only list and get_states commands were sent. The real inventory and the phrases generated from it stay in the private directory. Locally, the uv package cache was deleted; to rerun, the pinned model snapshots (3.9 GB, Hugging Face cache layout) and the Python environment stay in the workstation's scratch work directory on the NVMe disk (about 9 GB), not under /home.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• Fine-tuning: both model cards say the capability comes from fine-tuning on the domain (Laya's fine-tuned checkpoint goes from 0.36 to 0.77 on its own benchmark). The decider PoC has the data (kivi-fake-v1 train split) to test whether a fine-tuned Quyet-Tiny or Laya (or a small classifier on the embedding model) closes the gap; that is a separate, larger experiment.
  • Confidence: a gate on raw answer probabilities did not transfer between phrase sets. A fine-tuned model would need temperatures fitted on held-out data of the household's own phrasing.
  • Question marks: Whisper's transcripts lose "¿...?", so a stage behind STT cannot tell "¿Está encendida la luz?" from an order by punctuation; any stage needs state questions in its training or negatives.
  • Real voices and the real phrasing of the household (workstream c of the plan) decide how much room is left after custom sentences; all audio here is synthetic.

docs.title: Kivi decider PoC: is there headroom behind the built-in intents?
docs.text:
Status: P0 headroom analysis DONE (offline, synthetic); P1 to P3 (data at scale, fine-tuning, gates) NOT STARTED by owner decision, pending this analysis and the zero-shot baselines Date: 2026-11-05 Systems: workstation z800 (Ryzen 9 5950X, RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB, shared with the wake-word training); nothing ran on the cluster, Home Assistant or a TV Related: Kivi plan, workstream d, decision models (P0 zero-shot), small local models (corpus, Whisper prompt, GPU budget), conversation agent evaluation (phrases, fake home, grader) Risk: offline. No cloud request (a key was looked up by name, never used, and the file holding it was shredded), no Home Assistant access, no real names. All audio is synthetic (Piper voices, TV content mixes). Scripts: scripts/voice-assistant/decider_poc/ on top of agent_eval/ and small_models/

Evidence labels: documented (model card, package source), measured (run on z800 here), inferred (computed from the above), hypothesis. Every built-in intent figure is an inference of Home Assistant's behaviour: hassil 3.12.1 with home-assistant-intents 2026.10.6 (the pins of HA 2026.10.4), the slot lists of a fake home and prefer_local_intents semantics, as in agent_eval/builtin_intents.py. It is not a run of Home Assistant.

docs.title: Question
docs.text: The planned "Kivi decider" is a small local model behind Home Assistant's built-in intents. When the built-in sentences miss, it decides "home command, which intent, which target" and executes; anything uncertain goes to Kiais. Before data, training or a teacher: how many commands do the built-in intents miss in a way such a decider could rescue, and how many of those a cheap fix (aliases, custom sentences) already covers?

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
1. Teacher (P0b): not feasible locally (documented). pplx-decider-v1.1-27b needs about 49 GiB of bf16 weights on one CUDA GPU and its inference code has no quantised path. Cloud access is ruled out by the owner. The teacher was dropped without downloading the weights. If P2 ever runs, it trains on gold labels only (or Laya as a teacher).
  2. The hand-written corpus (39 commands, 5 voices, verbs prompt): the built-in intents miss 34 % of commands on clean audio, 45 % at +5 dB and 57 % at 0 dB of TV content. Of all commands, a decider could rescue at most 20 % (b1 phrasing) + 3 % (b2 near-miss). Another 12 % are misheard beyond recovery and 8 % lost only their verb. Upper bound of time saved: 0.7 s per command (b × 3 s / all commands). Custom sentences cover 8 of the 10 phrasing misses and cut that bound to 0.25 s.
  3. kivi-fake-v1 (new, shared with the zero-shot study): 2273 synthetic items over four fake homes (39 to 116 entities) and 17 phrasing or negative styles. 673 items are paraphrases by a local qwen3:14b, validated to keep their label; hand-checked label noise is about 2 % (5 % counting marginal cases). 500 items also have audio (clean, +5, 0 dB; Whisper large-v3-turbo with the verbs prompt).
  4. On kivi-fake-v1 text, the built-in intents get 22 % of commands right (44 % for the direct and polite templates, 4 to 7 % for colloquial, LatAm, word-order and disfluent phrasing, 0 % for "un poco más"). They take no wrong action on commands. On route-Kiais items they act only on bare device names ("Aire": HA's own sentences turn a bare name on).
  5. Cheap fix versus model: 92 custom sentences, written in about an hour from the template families, lift built-in success on the templates from 21 % to 70 % (0 wrong actions) but on the LLM paraphrases of the same commands only from 25 % to 33 %. They cover 62 % of the misses whose phrasing they were written for and 11 % of misses in unseen phrasing. Unseen phrasing is the room left for a model. How large that room is depends on how varied the household's real phrasing is, which only the real-usage replay (workstream c) can tell.
  6. Audio (500 items, 302 commands): with the built-in sentences, misheard commands (a) are 8 / 16 / 29 % at clean / +5 / 0 dB and rescuable phrasing (b1 + b2) is 64 / 58 / 50 %. That bounds the saving at 1.9 / 1.8 / 1.5 s per command, or 1.2 / 1.2 / 1.0 s with the custom sentences. On this deliberately varied mix, phrasing outweighs Whisper errors except at 0 dB.

Verdict for the owner: there is real headroom on synthetic data, largest for phrasing nobody anticipated. Custom sentences remove most of it for phrasing someone did anticipate, at no runtime cost. Recommendation: ship the custom sentences first (after a review against the real names), then decide P1 to P3 on the real-usage replay and the zero-shot baselines. Build the decider only if real misses look like the "unseen phrasing" rows here, not like the misheard rows.

docs.title: 1. Teacher (P0b): pplx-decider-v1.1-27b
docs.text:
Item Finding Label Weights Apache-2.0, Qwen3_5Model backbone (Qwen3.8-27B) plus a BF16 [255, 5120] readout; the card asks for "a CUDA GPU with room for roughly 49 GiB of weights plus working memory" documented (model card) Inference code source/src/autojev/model.py loads bf16 on CUDA and float32 on CPU (about 108 GB); no quantised loading; non-causal full-attention layers that a generic runtime does not reproduce documented (source, read without running) API Perplexity /v1/decisions needs a Perplexity key (none exists), the model is not listed on OpenRouter, and the owner ruled out cloud calls documented, observed This PC 16 GB VRAM, of which about 8 GB in use by the wake-word training at the time; 62 GB RAM, about 27 GB available observed

A 4-bit load would need a patched loader (bitsandbytes) and CPU offload of about half the layers. bitsandbytes cannot offload 4-bit weights (they would stay fp32 on the CPU, about 28 GB). It also risks breaking the non-causal attention setup. That is over the budget of about 1 h of setup and 1 example/s, so the teacher was dropped (inferred). No weights were downloaded. If P2 runs, it uses gold labels from the generator, optionally with Laya soft labels.

docs.title: 2. Headroom on the existing transcript corpus
docs.text:
Corpus of the small-models study: the 39 control phrases of agent_eval/phrases_es.yaml with a tool expectation (state questions c35 to c37, c43 and the missing-target c44 are not commands), 5 intelligible Piper voices, clean and +10 / +5 / 0 dB of TV content. Transcripts: large-v3-turbo int8 with the static verbs-only initial_prompt (run turbo_b5_vonly).

Rules (decider_poc/headroom.py), for each command the built-in intents miss (no match, a match HA ignores for an LLM agent, or an unresolved target):

  • Key words: the words of the reference text after the Phase 2 normalisation (numbers spelled out), minus articles, prepositions and fillers. A key word survives if it occurs in the transcript exactly, or fuzzily (rapidfuzz ratio ≥ 80 against a word or a two-word join). The spoken number must be parsed back unchanged.
  • a (misheard): a key word or the number is lost; intent or target cannot be recovered from the text. a-verb: only the leading verb is lost ("Con un temporizador de 10 minutos"); target and value survive, so the intent is sometimes inferable (counted apart, not in the bound).
  • b1 (phrasing): all key words survive and the reference text itself is not handled by the built-in sentences: a decider or a custom sentence can rescue it.
  • b2 (near-miss): all key words survive but some only fuzzily ("pesiana", "Apara"), and the reference is handled: strict matching breaks on a small mishearing that a robust decider could absorb.
  • c (other): all key words survive exactly and the reference is handled, yet the transcript misses (extra words, number format).

Built-in sentences only (measured; % of all commands of the condition):

Condition Commands Built-in correct Built-in wrong Miss a misheard a-verb b1 phrasing b2 near-miss c other Upper bound (b1+b2) × 3 s per command clean 195 128 (66 %) 0 67 (34 %) 6 (3 %) 10 (5 %) 47 (24 %) 4 (2 %) 0 0.78 s +10 dB 195 113 (58 %) 1 81 (42 %) 9 (5 %) 19 (10 %) 42 (22 %) 9 (5 %) 2 (1 %) 0.78 s +5 dB 195 108 (55 %) 0 87 (45 %) 22 (11 %) 17 (9 %) 41 (21 %) 7 (4 %) 0 0.74 s 0 dB 195 83 (43 %) 1 111 (57 %) 58 (30 %) 16 (8 %) 27 (14 %) 5 (3 %) 5 (3 %) 0.49 s all 780 432 (55 %) 2 346 (44 %) 95 (12 %) 62 (8 %) 157 (20 %) 25 (3 %) 7 (1 %) 0.70 s

Spot check (by hand, 6 to 8 per category): every sampled a-item had lost the device or verb ("Pon al volumen del Atelier 30", "Mirá."); every b1 item was a correct transcript of a phrase the built-in sentences do not cover; b2 items were one-letter slips ("Abre el tolo de la terraza", "Renuda la tele"); c items had trailing TV words ("Silencia la tele. Jerk, Tom.").

The b1 misses come from 10 phrases: c15 "Pon el aire del salón a 22 grados", c40 "Ponme la tele más bajita", c41 "Apágalo todo en la cocina", c38 "Está muy oscuro aquí", c26 "Pon la siguiente canción en el altavoz de la cocina", c05 "Pon la luz del salón al cuarenta por ciento", c13 "Pon la persiana del salón a la mitad", c14 "Para el toldo", c39 "Quita la tele", c16 "Pon la temperatura del dormitorio a veintiuno y medio". Several of them fall through because "pon ..." matches HassMediaSearchAndPlay, which prefer_local_intents ignores when the agent is an LLM.

Cheap fix (measured): with decider_poc/custom_sentences_es.yaml matched before the built-in sentences, as Home Assistant's default agent does, 37 of the 39 reference texts resolve (all but c16 "veintiuno y medio" and the implicit c38). Built-in success rises to 83 / 74 / 71 / 52 % (clean, +10, +5, 0 dB), b1 falls to 4 % of commands and the bound to 0.25 s per command, with no new wrong action. Caveat: the sentences were written after reading these phrases, so on this corpus they are not a blind test (the paraphrase result in section 4 is).

docs.title: 3. Dataset kivi-fake-v1
docs.text:
Location: /work/workspaces/kivi-decider-poc/data/kivi-fake-v1/ on the workstation (not in git). Schema: SCHEMA.md next to the data. Generators: decider_poc/fake_v1.py (homes, templates, negatives) and decider_poc/paraphrase.py (local LLM paraphrases and validation). All names are invented; nothing comes from the owner's Home Assistant.

Home Naming style Entities exposed Target options Items generica generic, the room repeated in the name ("Luz del salón", "Persiana de invitados") 39 46 570 coloquial colloquial and brand-like invented names with aliases ("Lámpara Arco", "Split", "Altavoz Lumo") 56 46 577 personas rooms named after invented people ("Cuarto de Candela"), the same device names in many rooms, two floors 77 67 558 latam Mexican Spanish ("recámara", "foco", "pantalla", "bocina", "clima"), many duplicates, two floors 116 92 568

Sensors fill the homes to a realistic count; only controllable domains are targets. Target options are the entities plus per-area groups (lights, covers, "everything") and "all lights", built from the inventory at request time (schema.target_options).

Kind (route) Styles Items command (execute) direct 301, polite 268, LatAm 259, word order 228, disfluent (fillers, repeats, self-corrections) 216, short ("Lámpara off") 203, Spain colloquial 189, relative volume ("Sube un poco el volumen") 112 1776 (673 paraphrased) question (Kiais) general 40, live 32, chit-chat 35, TV dialogue with command verbs ("¡Apaga eso y vámonos!") 48, state of the home 65 220 other (Kiais) out of domain 29, devices or rooms the home does not have 60 89 unclear (Kiais) implicit ("No veo nada aquí", "Hace frío") 39, verb-less ("Luz salón") 26 65 multi (Kiais) two actions in one request 63 unsupported (Kiais) relative brightness, temperature or cover moves ("Sube dos grados el aire") 60

Gold labels come from structured actions (intent, target option, value), never from text. Implicit requests are labelled unclear, as the owner asked. Relative volume is a command (HA has HassSetVolumeRelative), while relative brightness, temperature and position are "unsupported" (no HA intent; Kiais).

Paraphrases. A private Ollama 0.35.1 on the loopback interface (store on /datasets) ran qwen3:14b with thinking off on the 4060 Ti. It rewrote 400 stratified template commands, two versions each, in a requested register (colloquial Spain, polite, word order, Mexican, telegraphic, filler, indirect). The validator (paraphrase.validate) keeps a paraphrase only if:

  • the target name or alias is still there (and the area, if the source named it);
  • it adds no other area of the home;
  • numbers_es parses the same value;
  • an intent cue word is present and no cue of the opposite intent;
  • it is a single request.

Result: 673 of 800 kept. Rejected: 101 for a lost intent cue, 12 identical, 4 two requests, 3 opposite intent, 3 another area added, 2 lost target, 2 wrong value. Hand check:

  • 60 kept paraphrases: 1 clear label error (an invented "de la habitación") and 2 marginal ones ("Sigue activando la bocina" for resume), so label noise is about 2 %, 5 % counting the marginal ones. Two more errors of the same kind (an area added when the source had none) turned up among the built-in "wrong" actions and led to the "other area" rule.
  • 15 rejected paraphrases: 7 real label changes ("apaga" became "enciende", "para el toldo" became "abre el toldo") and 8 false rejections ("aumenta", "disminuye", "reduce", "eleva" are not cue words). The kept paraphrases are therefore biased towards common verbs, which makes them slightly easier for the built-in sentences than free speech.

Audio subset. 500 items stratified over kind, style and source: 302 commands and 198 route-Kiais items. Each was spoken by one of the 5 intelligible Piper voices at -22 dBFS active speech, clean and mixed with the TV content set at +5 and 0 dB (1500 clips, 141 MB). Transcripts come from large-v3-turbo int8 on CUDA, beam 5, language es and the verbs-only prompt (audio.py).

docs.title: 4. Built-in coverage on kivi-fake-v1 (text)
docs.text:
Commands, built-in sentences only, then with the custom sentences (measured):

Style Template n Built-in + custom Paraphrase n Built-in + custom direct 213 44 % 93 % 88 23 % 26 % polite 190 43 % 73 % 78 40 % 49 % short 113 19 % 39 % 90 20 % 32 % word order 132 7 % 75 % 96 28 % 35 % disfluent 124 6 % 15 % 92 30 % 39 % LatAm 164 6 % 71 % 95 23 % 33 % Spain colloquial 106 4 % 92 % 83 27 % 35 % relative volume 61 0 % 100 % 51 0 % 10 % all 1103 21 % 70 % 673 25 % 33 %

By home (all commands, built-in / + custom): generica 26 / 56 %, coloquial 27 / 59 %, personas 19 / 56 %, latam 16 / 54 %. Duplicate names and LatAm vocabulary cost the most.

  • Wrong actions on commands: 0 of 1103 templates. 3 of 673 paraphrases, all label problems: "Enciende todas las luces" is the whole house in the gold label but the satellite's area for HA, and "la persiana de la habitación" names a room that does not exist.
  • Route-Kiais items (497): the built-in sentences (with or without the custom ones) act on 7, all bare device names ("Aire", "Tele del salón"). HA's Spanish sentences turn a bare name on, which is HA's design rather than a mistake. 33 more get a local answer (time, timer status), and none of the 48 TV-dialogue lines, 60 missing-target commands or 63 multi requests triggers an action.
  • Cheap fix versus model: of the 1381 built-in misses (78 % of commands), the custom sentences rescue 603 (44 %). That is 62 % of template misses but only 11 % of paraphrase misses. A phrasing someone wrote down is cheap to cover, and the rest is what a decider would have to learn.

Upper bound of time saved on text (every miss of a command rescued, × 3 s, divided by all commands): 2.3 s per command with the built-in sentences and 1.3 s with the custom sentences. These are bounds on a deliberately varied synthetic mix, not on real usage frequencies.

docs.title: 5. Audio subset of kivi-fake-v1
docs.text:
302 commands and 198 route-Kiais items, each spoken once and heard in three conditions (measured, synthetic voices). The subset is balanced over styles, so its built-in rate on clean audio (19 %) is below the text figure of the natural mix (22 %). Same categories as section 2, with the item text as the reference; % of all commands of the condition.

Condition Sentences Correct Wrong Miss a misheard a-verb b1 phrasing b2 near-miss c other Upper bound (b1+b2) × 3 s per command clean built-in 56 (19 %) 1 245 (81 %) 24 (8 %) 27 (9 %) 192 (64 %) 1 (0 %) 1 (0 %) 1.92 s +5 dB built-in 43 (14 %) 1 258 (85 %) 49 (16 %) 32 (11 %) 173 (57 %) 3 (1 %) 1 (0 %) 1.75 s 0 dB built-in 34 (11 %) 1 267 (88 %) 89 (29 %) 24 (8 %) 143 (47 %) 8 (3 %) 3 (1 %) 1.50 s clean + custom 126 (42 %) 2 174 (58 %) 24 (8 %) 24 (8 %) 112 (37 %) 9 (3 %) 5 (2 %) 1.20 s +5 dB + custom 99 (33 %) 1 202 (67 %) 49 (16 %) 31 (10 %) 104 (34 %) 13 (4 %) 5 (2 %) 1.16 s 0 dB + custom 82 (27 %) 2 218 (72 %) 88 (29 %) 23 (8 %) 79 (26 %) 19 (6 %) 9 (3 %) 0.97 s
  • Misheard grows with noise: 8 % of commands at clean, 16 % at +5 dB and 29 % at 0 dB. The 0 dB transcripts of a are often TV lines ("Que no soportó el esfuerzo y cayó muerto." for "Por favor, para el toldo"). No text model can rescue them.
  • Phrasing dominates the rescuable part on this varied mix: b1 is 47 to 64 % of commands with the built-in sentences and 26 to 37 % with the custom ones. b2 (one-letter slips such as "Apara la luz de la cochera", "pepsiana", "tolo") is 1 to 6 %. A decider would need fuzzy name matching to rescue b2.
  • Wrong actions (measured):
  • Route-Kiais items: 5, 2 and 4 of 198 per condition, all bare device names ("Altavoz Lumo", "Tele del salón") that HA's own sentences turn on.
  • Commands: the one label-noise paraphrase ("la persiana de la habitación"). With the custom sentences, "Detener persianas sala" was also heard as "Detener persiana sala" and stopped one blind instead of the group (clean and 0 dB). Strict sentences are safe only as long as the transcript is: a singular/plural slip already picks another target.

docs.title: 6. Limitations
docs.text:
• Synthetic only: Piper voices, a mixed-in TV bed with no room acoustics or AEC residue, invented homes. The style mix is chosen to be varied, so miss rates are not usage frequencies. The real-usage replay (workstream c) decides how often each style really occurs.
  • The built-in figures infer HA's behaviour with hassil and a fake resolver, not with a live Home Assistant. The custom sentences were matched as HA's default agent orders them, but they were not loaded into a real HA.
  • The paraphrase validator is conservative (false rejections of "aumenta" or "reduce"), so the kept paraphrases under-represent unusual verbs. Label noise is about 2 to 5 %.
  • "a-verb" and "unclear" items might be partly rescuable with context; they are excluded from the upper bound on purpose.

docs.title: 7. Reproduce, data and cleanup
docs.text:
POC=/work/workspaces/kivi-decider-poc; D=$POC/data/kivi-fake-v1
cd scripts/voice-assistant/decider_poc
python headroom.py [--custom custom_sentences_es.yaml]        # corpus, needs $KIVI_PRIVATE/stt-runs
python fake_v1.py --out $D --per-home 400                      # template items and homes
OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1:11510 python paraphrase.py --data $D --n 400 && python paraphrase.py --data $D --merge
python audio.py synth --items $D/items.jsonl --data $D --split fake --audio $D/audio --conds clean snr+5 snr+0
python audio.py transcribe --data $D --split fake --audio $D/audio
python headroom_v1.py --data $D [--custom custom_sentences_es.yaml] [--audio]
python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test_decider_poc.py'

Dependencies: hassil 3.12.1, home-assistant-intents 2026.10.6, pyyaml, rapidfuzz, numpy, soundfile, piper-tts, and faster-whisper 1.2.1 with the CUDA 12 cuBLAS and cuDNN wheels (nvidia-cublas-cu12, nvidia-cudnn-cu12) on LD_LIBRARY_PATH. Kept on the workstation: the dataset and its audio under /work/workspaces/kivi-decider-poc/data/, the venv, and env.sh. Removed at the end: the Ollama model store on /datasets/kivi-decider, the Whisper model cache, uv cache, and an unused first generator output (data/items_*.jsonl of the training-split draft, see gen_data.py).

gen_data.py is the train/dev/test generator drafted for P1 before the scope change (held-out template families and name pools). It is kept for P1 but no audio or training was run with it.

docs.title: 8. Open questions for the owner
docs.text:
1. Ship the custom sentences (after checking them against the real names and aliases), and re-run this analysis on the real-usage replay before any decider work?
  2. Go on to P1 to P3 only if the real misses are mostly "unseen phrasing" rather than "misheard"?
  3. Treat "todas las luces" as the whole house or the satellite's area (HA uses the area)?

docs.title: Custom wake word "kivi": training an openWakeWord model and measuring recall and false accepts offline
docs.text:
Status: DONE offline (model trained and measured on synthetic voices and public recordings). Deployed on 2026-11-05 as the wake word of the "Kiwi" pipeline (see Deployment). Real-voice recall is unknown until the owner test below is run. A v2 candidate (server-exact features, front-end emulation; v2) exists, not deployed. A v3 candidate (v2 plus real takes of one speaker and real room negatives; v3) passes the owner gate on point estimates for that speaker on c3-a, not deployed. A v4 candidate for the new wake phrase "oye Kivi" (v4) exists, not deployed; its real recall is untested. Date: 2026-11-05 Device alias / model / firmware / webOS / architecture: none. PC only (x86_64, RTX 4060 Ti 16 GB, 32 threads). No TV, no microphone, no speaker, no change in Home Assistant, the cluster or the GitOps tree. Power and playback state: not applicable Related research / requirements / issue: satellite-side ADR 0003, server-side wake word for the MVP; the Phase 2 corpus and TV content set of that repository (P2 corpus); conversation agent evaluation for the same pipeline Risk: the offline run had none. The deployment changes which word wakes both TV satellites; alexa stays loaded as the rollback. Approval needed / obtained: none for the offline run. The owner approved the deployment on 2026-11-05 and accepted the weaker noisy-TV recall, with AEC and noise suppression coming. The real-voice test still needs the owner.

Evidence labels: documented (read in a source or a model card), observed-offline (measured on the PC with synthetic or public recordings, not in the room), inferred, hypothesis. Nothing here is a measurement with a real voice or the TV microphone.

docs.title: Question and falsifiable hypotheses
docs.text:
Can a custom openWakeWord model for the lone Spanish word "kivi" (/ˈki.βi/; the owner chose the single word despite the higher false-wake risk of a two-syllable name) replace alexa in the "Kiwi" pipeline (Home Assistant wake_word.openwakeword, the cluster's wyoming-openwakeword 2.1.0), with recall and false accepts the owner can accept?

  • H1: on held-out synthetic Spanish voices (never used in training), recall at the chosen threshold is at least as high as the stock alexa model's recall on "alexa" said by the same voices.
  • H2: on long Spanish speech and TV-like audio, false accepts per hour at that threshold are at most about 1 per 10 hours (0.1/h), and not worse than alexa on the same audio by more than the confidence intervals allow.
  • H3: the Spanish near-words ("kiwi", "Vivi", "tivi", "aquí vi", ...) wake the model rarely; the risky ones are named.

docs.title: Training data (synthetic, Spanish phonetics)
docs.text:
• Positives: "kivi" rendered by Piper ONNX voices from Spanish phonemes, 60 000 training and 3 000 validation clips. Variants: kˈiβi 45 %, kˈibi 20 %, kˈivi 20 %, kˈiːβi 10 %, kˈiːbi 5 % ("kivi", "quivi" and "kibi" all phonemize to kˈiβi in Spanish espeak, so the phonemes are varied directly), with trailing punctuation for prosody ("", ".", "!", ",", "?"), length scale 0.75 to 1.35, noise scales 0.4 to 1.0, peak -12 to -1 dBFS.
  • Speakers: training voices are 4 native Spanish speakers (es_ES sharvard M and F, davefx, es_MX ald) plus English multi-speaker models fed with the Spanish phonemes (LibriTTS-R speakers 0-799 of 904, VCTK 0-89 of 109) and Italian, Portuguese and Catalan voices, for speaker variety (about 45 % native Spanish by weight). Held out for evaluation only: es_MX claude, es_AR daniela, es_ES carlfm (native Spanish), LibriTTS-R speakers 800-903 and VCTK 90-108. The MLS "low" Spanish voices and ca_ES pau were dropped: they babble or repeat on a single word (median 1.5 to 2.6 s and 2 to 8 energy bursts for "kˈiβi"; observed-offline).
  • Adversarial negatives: 60 000 + 3 000 clips of 121 Spanish words and phrases close to "kivi" (the /w/ form "kiwi"/"kiui"; one consonant away: "Vivi", "Bibi", "tivi", "Fivi", "chivi", "Kiki", "Kiko", "bici", "civil"; "qui-" words: "quizá", "quieres", "quién", "esquivo", "equívoco"; across word boundaries: "aquí vi", "y vi", "qué vi", "ki") and 30 sentences with them in context. The full list is in scripts/voice-assistant/wakeword/kivi_data.yaml.
  • General negatives: ACAV100M openWakeWord features (the first 8 GiB of the 17.3 GB file, about 990 h of multilingual real-world audio) and 20 h of Spanish read speech from MLS (train shard 0), as feature windows; the 11.3 h openWakeWord false-positive validation set during training.
  • Background and reverberation: MIT room impulse responses (270), AudioSet balanced-train shard 00 (500 clips of noise and music, weighted 3x) and Spanish speech from MLS train shard 2 (1 500 x 10 s). The official run used openWakeWord's augment_clips with these (-10 to +15 dB SNR, EQ, distortion, pitch shift, band-stop, coloured noise, gain); the final model uses the word-level augmentation below.

docs.title: Training
docs.text:
1.
