Official recipe first (failed). openWakeWord train.py (commit 368c037, 2025-12-30) with --augment_clips --train_model: model dnn, layer 32, 50 000 steps, batch per step ACAV 1024 + MLS 256 + adversarial 100 + positive 100, max_negative_weight 1500, target 0.2 false positives per hour. The model collapsed: 3.5 % recall on its own validation positives and 8 % on held-out voices. Removing the "aquí vi" phrases (they contain the target sound a-kˈi-βi) and lowering the weight to 300 did not help (1-6 % validation recall). See Pitfalls, item 2, for the cause.
  2. What worked (augment_set.py --mode simple, train_simple.py, fast_eval.py mine):
  3. Own augmentation with the SNR measured on the word itself: clip end-aligned in a 2 s window (0-200 ms jitter), room impulse response with p 0.5, background with p 0.7 at 5 to 30 dB against the clip's RMS, peak -20 to -1 dBFS. The "aquí vi" family (5 % of the adversarial clips) is excluded from training and kept in the evaluation.
  4. The same openWakeWord DNN head (Flatten, Linear, LayerNorm, ReLU, one FCN block, Linear, Sigmoid; exported by openWakeWord's export_model), layer 64, trained with a plain balanced loop: 6 000 steps, Adam with one-cycle LR 3e-4, batch per step 256 positives, 512 ACAV, 128 MLS Spanish, 64 adversarial and 128 mined hard negatives, a fixed negative weight of 3, and no auto_train weight ramp.
  5. Hard-negative mining: a first model scored 31 h of other Spanish speech (MLS train shard 1), and its 40 718 highest-scoring windows (above 0.05, at most one per 0.4 s) became an extra negative class.
  6. Variants trained (11, 2-6 min each on the GPU): with and without adversarials, two augmentation strengths, layer 32/64/128/256, one or two mining rounds. They were ranked by held-out recall at a fixed false-accept count on MLS dev only (not the test sets), with server-exact features. The chosen model is variant s5.
  7. Export: export_tflite.py (the onnx_tf path of train.py does not install with current TensorFlow) rebuilds the head as a TensorFlow function and converts it; max |ONNX - TFLite| 1.5e-6. --calibrate-threshold 0.98 shifts the last bias by -logit(0.98), so the file deployed with the server's default global threshold 0.5 decides exactly like the raw model at 0.98 (checked in the server runtime).

Time on the PC (RTX 4060 Ti, 32 threads, shared with other heavy jobs all evening): clip generation 37 min (131 000 clips, CPU), official augmentation and features 23 min, official training 26 min, own augmentation 3 min, each variant 2-6 min, mining 3 min of GPU embedding. Wall clock including the failed recipe and the evaluation fix: about 6 h.

docs.title: Evaluation (offline, server-exact features)
docs.text:
The cluster runs pyopen-wakeword 1.1.0 inside wyoming-openwakeword 2.1.0 (TFLite C API, 80 ms chunks, detection when the probability is above the threshold, trigger level 1, 2 s refractory). Every reported number uses that server's exact features: either pyopen-wakeword itself (eval_stream.py, used for alexa and to verify) or fast_eval.py embed --stream-onnx, which reproduces the server's chunking with a melspectrogram model whose 80 dB clamp is per chunk (see Pitfalls, item 1). It matches pyopen-wakeword streaming to 0.002 in the final score (12 clips checked one by one) and to 0.032 in the embeddings (unit test). fast_report.py refuses features that are not tagged server-exact. Cross-check of the alexa emulation: 55/97 on the Phase 2 positive session at 0.5, against 58/97 in Home Assistant's own digital run of P2 session 2.

  • Recall: each held-out clip as its own stream (fresh state after the 8 s autofill, 1 s before and after), clean and mixed with the Phase 2 TV content clips (not used in training) at 10 dB and 0 dB SNR. alexa is measured on "alexa" said by the same held-out voices with Spanish phonetics (alˈeksa / alˈeɣsa).
  • False accepts per hour: every detection on audio without the wake word, exact Poisson 95 % intervals. MLS Spanish dev (10.3 h) was used only to pick the model and threshold. The test sets are MLS Spanish test (10.3 h, LibriVox readers disjoint from training), VoxPopuli Spanish test (5.2 h, parliament speeches), the Phase 2 TV content set (1.15 h of Spanish and English speech, film, music with and without vocals, and an action scene), the Phase 2 negative and near-miss sessions (0.09 h), and the Phase 2 positive session (0.23 h of Spanish commands after "alexa"; no "kivi" in it). None of the MLS or VoxPopuli transcripts contains "kivi", "kiwi", "quivi" or "kibi".
  • Near-words: 1 799 held-out-voice clips of the 121 adversarial words and 30 sentences.

docs.title: Results (observed-offline, server-exact)
docs.text:
Chosen model: variant s5 (layer 64, 416 KB TFLite), recommended threshold 0.98 (picked on MLS dev). In the deployable, calibrated file, 0.98 sits at 0.5. "alexa" is the stock model at the server's default 0.5, as the household uses it today.

Recall on held-out synthetic voices (n = 1 800 clips each; 95 % Wilson interval):

Condition kivi @ 0.98 alexa @ 0.5 (same voices) Clean 60.2 % [57.9, 62.4] 63.2 % [60.9, 65.4] TV content at 10 dB SNR 25.1 % [23.1, 27.1] 38.2 % [36.0, 40.4] TV content at 0 dB SNR 9.7 % [8.4, 11.1] 21.3 % [19.5, 23.3]

Per held-out voice, clean (kivi @ 0.98 / alexa @ 0.5): es_MX claude 58 % / 86 %, es_AR daniela 78 % / 64 %, es_ES carlfm 46 % / 23 %, LibriTTS-R 800-903 68 % / 75 %, VCTK 90-108 43 % / 73 %. Both models depend strongly on the voice; with TV in the background "kivi" loses recall faster than "alexa" (daniela drops to 3.5 % at 10 dB).

False accepts per hour (exact Poisson 95 % interval):

Audio (hours) kivi @ 0.98 alexa @ 0.5 MLS Spanish test (10.3) 3 = 0.29/h [0.06, 0.85] 2 = 0.20/h [0.02, 0.71] VoxPopuli Spanish test (5.2) 1 = 0.19/h [0.005, 1.08] 2 = 0.39/h [0.05, 1.41] Phase 2 TV content (1.15) 0 (< 3.2/h) 0 (< 3.2/h) Phase 2 negatives + near-misses (0.09) 0 2 ("Alexandria"-type near-misses) Phase 2 commands after "alexa" (0.23) 0 not applicable (contains "alexa") Test total, 16.9 h (16.5 h for alexa) 4 = 0.24/h [0.06, 0.61] 6 = 0.36/h [0.13, 0.79] MLS dev, 10.3 h (selection only) 4 = 0.39/h 3 = 0.29/h

Trade-off of the threshold (same model; test total 16.9 h; clean / 10 dB recall):

Threshold Clean recall 10 dB recall False accepts on the test sets Near-word acceptance 0.97 71.7 % 31.7 % 12 = 0.71/h 5.3 % 0.98 60.2 % 25.1 % 4 = 0.24/h 3.7 % 0.985 48.1 % 19.2 % 3 = 0.18/h 2.7 % 0.99 28.7 % 12.7 % 0 (< 0.18/h) 1.4 %

Near-words at 0.98 (held-out voices, about 12 clips per word; 66/1 799 = 3.7 % [2.9, 4.6] overall): "Kili" 5/12, "kiri" 5/12, "Pipi" 4/11, "tivi" 4/12, "kiwi" 3/12, "quiwi" 3/12, "chivi" 3/12, "pipí" 3/12, "Kiki" 3/12, "aquí viví" 3/12, "ti vi" 3/12, "qué vi" 3/12, "que vi" 3/12; 1/12 for "la tivi", "Fivi", "Titi", "Gigi", "Didi" and "Fifi"; 0 for most others ("Vivi", "bici", "civil", "quizá", "quieres" ...). "kiwi" said as /kiui/ wakes it about a quarter of the time: a member of the household who says the pipeline's name "Kiwi" will sometimes wake it and sometimes not.

docs.title: Hypotheses
docs.text:
• H1 (recall at least alexa's): not met with noise, about equal when clean (60 % vs 63 %, intervals overlap; 25 % vs 38 % at 10 dB SNR).
  • H2 (about 0.1/h or less, not worse than alexa): 0.24/h at 0.98, the same as alexa within the intervals; 0.1/h is not shown (zero false accepts at 0.99, but with 29 % recall).
  • H3 (near-words): partly. The model rejects most of them, but "Kili", "kiri", "Pipi", "tivi" and "kiwi" pass 25-42 % of the time at 0.98.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• The lone word "kivi" is usable only at about the same recall as "alexa" in quiet. Both are measured on synthetic voices, so the absolute numbers say little about real people. With TV sound in the room it is clearly worse than "alexa", which matters on a TV satellite (the echo canceller is parked).
  • The best lever left is to retrain on server-exact features (inferred; the model is now trained on batch features that differ from what the server computes, see Pitfalls), followed by real-voice positives from the owner's test. A two-word phrase such as "oye Kivi" should separate much better from running Spanish speech (hypothesis, not measured).

docs.title: Pitfalls
docs.text:
Both are recorded with symptom, cause, detection, fix and guard in lessons learned.

  1. Melspectrogram clamp: the server's features are not the training features. openWakeWord's melspectrogram model (ONNX and TFLite) ends with ReduceMax over its whole input and a clamp at max - 80 dB. The server (pyopen-wakeword) calls it on one 1760-sample chunk at a time, so the floor is per 80 ms chunk. Batch extraction (AudioFeatures.embed_clips, used for training and by most offline evaluation code) puts the floor at the loudest point of the whole batch. For the same clip the scores differed by up to 0.99 (for example 0.96 in the server and 0.004 in batch). This made the first offline estimates wrong in both directions. Fix: stream_mel.py rewrites the model so that the max is per batch row, and fast_eval.py embed --stream-onnx feeds it the server's 1760-sample chunks with pyopen-wakeword's frame and window bookkeeping. Verified tolerance: embeddings within 0.032 of pyopen-wakeword streaming (values reach ±63) and final scores within 0.002 on 12 clips. Guard: test_server_exact_features.py (streaming vs batched within 0.05; batch features must differ; fast_report.py refuses features not tagged server-exact).
  2. Augmentation SNR over the whole window buries a short word. openWakeWord's augment_clips mixes background at -10 to +15 dB SNR computed over the whole 2 s padded window. For a 0.45 s word, many positives end up at or below 0 dB on the word itself (the measured word-to-background amplitude ratio was 1.0 to 2.4). With auto_train's negative weight rising to 1500x (doubled when the false-positive target is missed), every run collapsed to 2-9 % recall. Fix: augment with the SNR measured against the word (5 to 30 dB), and train with a fixed small negative weight plus mined hard negatives. Guard: augment_set.py --mode simple documents the choice, and the training history shows validation recall at fixed false accepts (train_simple.py).

docs.title: Deployment notes (written before the deployment)
docs.text:
The deployment that was made is in Deployment; it uses neither option below but a private image (see lessons learned).

How the cluster's server loads models (documented, read-only check of apps/home-assistant/values.yaml and the wyoming-openwakeword 2.1.0 source): the openwakeword controller runs rhasspy/wyoming-openwakeword:2.1.0 with --preload-model alexa, an option that 2.x still accepts but ignores (deprecated). Custom models are read from --custom-model-dir <DIR> (repeatable): every *.tflite in it becomes a model whose id is the file stem, with a _vX.Y suffix removed (kivi.tflite and kivi_v0.1.tflite both give kivi). The model must be TFLite (pyopen-wakeword runs it through the TFLite C API); the ONNX file is not used. --threshold (default 0.5), --trigger-level (1) and --refractory-seconds (2) are global, for all models of the server.

Threshold without touching alexa: the recommended operating point is far above 0.5, so the deployable file is exported with export_tflite.py --calibrate-threshold T, which shifts the last layer's bias by -logit(T). The output then crosses 0.5 exactly where the raw model crosses T, so the server keeps its default --threshold 0.5 and alexa (and any other pipeline) is unaffected.

GitOps change that would be needed (in apps/home-assistant/, not made):

  1. Get the file into the pod. The calibrated model is 416 KB (555 KB in base64), which fits a ConfigMap (1 MiB limit). Options, for the owner to choose:
  2. (a) an init container that downloads kivi.tflite from an owner-chosen URL (for example a bucket on the in-cluster MinIO) into an emptyDir and checks its SHA-256 before the server starts. No binary in git.
  3. (b) commit the binary (for example apps/home-assistant/files/wakeword/kivi.tflite) and mount it through a ConfigMap rendered with binaryData: {kivi.tflite: {{ .Files.Get "files/wakeword/kivi.tflite" | b64enc }}}. This is the simplest GitOps path, but it needs the owner's licensing decision first: the model inherits CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 terms from the ACAV100M features (the stock openWakeWord models carry the same terms), and some training voices are CC BY-SA.
  4. Mount it read-only at /custom in the openwakeword container (an advancedMounts entry under persistence, as the whisper and piper volumes do), and add the argument:
args:
  - --preload-model   # deprecated in 2.x, harmless; can be dropped in the same change
  - alexa
  - --custom-model-dir
  - /custom
  1. After Argo CD rolls the pod, reload the Wyoming openWakeWord integration in Home Assistant so that it reads the new model list (kivi next to alexa, hey_jarvis, ...).
  2. Pipeline: in the "Kiwi" Assist pipeline set the wake word to kivi (stored as wake_word_id: kivi in .storage/assist_pipeline.pipelines; today alexa). This is a Home Assistant change made outside git, so it needs the owner's explicit yes per AGENTS.md. Rollback: set wake_word_id back to alexa (the stock model stays loaded either way), then revert the GitOps commit if wanted. The satellite needs no change: the wake word runs on the server (satellite ADR 0003).

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
Deployed on 2026-11-05: model v1-2026-11-05, kivi.tflite, sha256 5e20c8ee46428a4b6692efe19309d8ca4d02c2cf73679704d891c316297778cb, served at the server default threshold 0.5 (= raw 0.98).

Delivery (no binary in git, no ConfigMap, no extra credential):

  • The private repository agil/kivi-models builds an image on a version tag (.forgejo/workflows/image.yml): busybox pinned by digest with the served file at /models/kivi.tflite, checked against the version's SHA256SUMS inside the build, and the label cloud.grigri.kivi.model.sha256. It is pushed as a package of the user agil, linked to the repository: git.grigri.cloud/agil/kivi-models:v1-2026-11-05@sha256:9e51e0c9dba009480f0706da8f90f178380fd72fceeb05e9e148555bb178b40c. An anonymous pull is refused (checked). Packages take the visibility of their owner, not of the repository, so this holds only while agil stays "limited" (set on 2026-11-05); the image was first published under the private organisation grigri for that reason, and moved once agil became limited.
  • The init container 01-copy-kivi of the openwakeword controller runs that image and copies the file into an emptyDir (16Mi), mounted read-only at /custom in the server, which runs with --custom-model-dir /custom (model id = file stem, kivi). Its log is the sha256sum of the copy. The nodes pull the image with their existing containerd credential for git.grigri.cloud, like the Whisper image, so there is no imagePullSecret, token or Vault entry.
  • Version swap: push the version tag in agil/kivi-models, then change the image tag and digest in apps/home-assistant/values.yaml and update the registry row. The deployment uses the Recreate strategy, so the wake word is down for a few seconds while the pod restarts; open satellite runs reconnect by themselves.
  • History: the first rollout (commit 63045e4aa) downloaded the file with curl, a bot token from Vault and a PVC cache. It worked but was replaced the same evening; see lessons learned.

Home Assistant change (outside git): pipeline "Kiwi" (the preferred one), wake_word_id from alexa to kivi through the websocket command assist_pipeline/pipeline/update, every other field unchanged (checked by a diff of assist_pipeline/pipeline/list before and after). The two TV satellites follow it without a per-satellite change: their pipeline selects are preferred, and their wake word selects are unavailable (no_wake_word) because the wake word runs on the server. Updating the pipeline aborts the open wake word runs (wake_word_detection_aborted) and the satellites start new ones with the new wake word within about 15 s (observed-on-cluster). No Wyoming config entry reload was needed: wake_word/info listed kivi right after the pod restart.

Verification (observed-on-cluster, 2026-11-05, no sound on the TVs):

  • First rollout (63045e4aa): Argo CD Synced and Healthy; init log downloaded, sha256 OK; the server Ready; Wyoming describe lists kivi next to the stock models. The same file (same sha256) is served by the image-based rollout. Before that rollout, a temporary pod on the openwakeword node pulled the image without any pull secret and copied the file as uid 568 with the expected sha256.
  • Synthetic check from a temporary in-cluster pod with a Wyoming client (no TV involved), on held-out Piper clips (never used in training): "kivi" by three native Spanish held-out voices, 3 of 3 detected as kivi; a held-out "alexa" clip sent to kivi not detected, and sent to alexa detected; a "kivi" clip sent to alexa not detected.
  • Both satellites idle, each with an open Wyoming connection to the server; the server's CPU use shows the streams being processed. The Home Assistant log has only ConnectionRefusedError from the 8 s pod restart window and nothing after it.

Rollback:

  1. Pipeline: assist_pipeline/pipeline/update on "Kiwi" with wake_word_id: alexa and the other fields unchanged (or Settings > Voice assistants > Kiwi > wake word "alexa"). The open satellite runs restart on the update. alexa stays loaded, so this alone is a full functional rollback.
  2. Optionally remove the init container, the kivi-model volume and --custom-model-dir in GitOps. The image can stay in the registry (private) or be deleted from the agil packages.

docs.title: Real-voice test for the owner (written, not run)
docs.text:
Synthetic recall says nothing reliable about real voices. Before switching the "Kiwi" pipeline:

  1. Deploy as above, but set kivi only on a test pipeline (for example "Kiwi Test", today alexa_v0.1), assigned to one TV.
  2. Recall: each adult says "Kivi" 20 times at 1 to 3 m, in three blocks: TV off, TV at normal volume with speech, TV with music. Count detections in the Assist debug view (Settings > Voice assistants > ... > Debug). No audio is stored. Optional: 10 times "kiwi" said as /kiui/, to see whether the household's natural pronunciation of the pipeline's name wakes it.
  3. False wakes: leave the test pipeline active for 3 to 7 evenings of normal TV, and count pipeline runs that nobody started (Home Assistant logbook or the satellite's wake events). Only counts, no recordings.
  4. Suggested acceptance: recall of at least 80 % with the TV off and at least 60 % with the TV on, and at most 1 false wake per evening. If it fails, go to the alternatives below rather than lower the threshold.

docs.title: Real-voice measurement and dataset tools (built 2026-11-07, not yet run on a person)
docs.text:
Tools in scripts/voice-assistant/wakeword/ measure kivi on real voices and keep every recording as a permanent, private dataset at /work/workspaces/kivi-wakeword/datasets/real/ (outside git, mode 700, never deleted by the tools; see data register rows 8-11). They were tested with synthetic signals only: no microphone was opened while writing them.

Tool Who runs it What it does kivi_session.py the speaker text-only cues ("say KIVI now", about every 5 s) while recording the desk mic and the webcam mic; writes session.json kivi_extract.py the owner copies the satellite's wake files for the session out of the HA pod (kubectl exec ... cat), aligns them to the desk mic by GCC-PHAT, cuts clips of the three sources, appends to manifest.jsonl. --button-takes cuts takes marked by input_button.kivi_take presses instead kivi_score.py the owner kivi (uncalibrated head, raw thresholds) and alexa through the server-exact path over the aligned satellite audio: recall per block and threshold, near-word false accepts, false accepts per hour on the non-cue time; aggregates only kivi_import_phone.py the owner imports a phone voice memo (takes found by energy, source phone) kivi_negatives.py the owner, on request copies about 30 h of closed wake files of both TVs as real negatives, minus the cues, presses, detection boundaries, every session window and --exclude-after / --exclude-between windows kivi_dataset_marks.py the owner records a later split for a session (splits.jsonl) or marks an extraction revision superseded (superseded.jsonl); append-only, manifest and audio untouched

Satellites are a parameter (--device c3-a, --device c3-b, mapped to the HA device-id prefix in kivi_devices.json; the source label is tv-c3a, tv-c3b, ...). Speakers are pseudonymous ids only (spk01, spk02): the mapping to people is kept by the owner, outside the tools and the repository.

docs.title: Owner procedure: one session (about 12 min, c3-a, first speaker)
docs.text:
cd ~/homelab/scripts/voice-assistant/wakeword
PY=/work/workspaces/kivi-wakeword/.venv/bin/python
# 1. Unmute c3-a in Home Assistant (its mute switch), so the wake stage audio flows.
python3 kivi_session.py --list-devices            # pick the hardware inputs (alsa_input.*), not monitors or Easy Effects
# 2. The session. Cues are text only. Sit at 1.5 m, then 3 m; the TV is off, then on (normal volume, your content).
python3 kivi_session.py --device c3-a --speaker spk01 --desk-mic Samson --webcam-mic C920 --tag volume=normal
# 3. Soon after (Home Assistant deletes files after 90 days). Check first with --dry-run.
$PY kivi_extract.py --session-dir ~/kivi-sessions/<session id> --dry-run
$PY kivi_extract.py --session-dir ~/kivi-sessions/<session id>
# 4. Scores (aggregates only; also saved in the dataset's scores/ directory).
$PY kivi_score.py --session /work/workspaces/kivi-wakeword/datasets/real/<session id> --also-pc
# 5. Mute c3-a again.

The protocol: positions 1.5 m and 3 m, each with the TV off and with the TV on, 10 "kivi" per block; then the near-words kiwi, tivi, kili, kiri, Pipi and "aquí vi", 2 each; then 60 s of silence with the speaker present and quiet. Enter separates the blocks. For the 4-6 training sessions vary the conditions: --repeat 2, --only kivi-3m-tvon, --tag volume=loud, --tag speed=fast, or --blocks my_blocks.json (print the default with --print-protocol). Check the align lines the extractor prints: a source marked LOW CONFIDENCE was not aligned reliably (its clips use the file-time estimate and may be shifted by up to a second). alexa is not said in the protocol: its recall on "kivi" is a cross-talk check, and its false accepts per hour are the baseline to compare with.

docs.title: Second speaker (consent first)
docs.text:
Nobody's voice is imported before that person has agreed, knowing what is stored (local, never in git, kept until the owner deletes it, used to measure and train Kivi) and that they can ask for it to be deleted. The importers refuse without --consent-confirmed.

  1. Phone memo (3 minutes, any quiet room). Hold the phone at about 1 m. Say "kivi" 30 times, about 3 s apart: ten at normal volume, ten louder and slower, ten quicker and softer. Then say each of kiwi, tivi, kili, kiri, Pipi and "aquí vi" twice, in that order. Say nothing else (no counting, no comments) and leave a clear pause between takes. Send the memo to the owner. Import with $PY kivi_import_phone.py MEMO --speaker spk02 --split train --consent-confirmed --expect 42 --near-labels kiwi,kiwi,tivi,tivi,kili,kili,kiri,kiri,Pipi,Pipi,"aquí vi","aquí vi" (--split has no default and must be given; --dry-run first: it only counts the takes; a mismatch with --expect writes nothing).
  2. Button takes on c3-b (about 5 min). Unmute c3-b. Say "kivi" once, then press the Kivi take button in Home Assistant (input_button.kivi_take), then wait about 5 s; repeat 30 times (10 with the TV off, 20 with it on, from where she normally sits). Then mute c3-b. The owner runs $PY kivi_extract.py --button-takes --device c3-b --speaker spk02 --since 2026-11-.. --until 2026-11-.. --split test (times are local unless they end in Z). The extraction looks for the word in the window from max(press - 4 s, the previous take's press + 0.3 s) to press + 1 s (--button-order say-then-press, the default; the old press-then-say looks 0 to 6 s after the press), and treats presses less than 1.5 s apart as one take (a double press, counted). The report counts presses, takes, double presses, clips cut and takes without a clear speech onset. A take whose speech does not start before the press, or whose speech span exceeds 2.5 s is flagged needs_review and, to keep it out of test, its split is set to unassigned until the owner has listened to it (--keep-review-in-split overrides). The press times are the distinct state values of the button, so a state restored after an HA restart is not a press.
  3. The button exists only after the Home Assistant configuration change (apps/home-assistant/config/integrations/kivi_take.yaml) is deployed and the helper is loaded (restart, or reload input buttons). One button serves every satellite: the extraction names the device, so run one speaker and one satellite per time window.

docs.title: Split policy (decided 2026-11-07)
docs.text:
• Every record has a split: train, dev, test or train-only (unassigned until the owner decides). The split belongs to the session: all takes of a session and all channels of one utterance (satellite, desk mic, webcam) are in the same split. kivi_import_phone.py requires --split (there is no default).
  • Production model: the phone memo of spk02 is train. Her c3-b button takes are test and are never trained on. Sessions of the first speaker on c3-a are train sessions (and the c3-a evaluation sessions are dev or test, decided by the owner per session).
  • Unseen-speaker check (an ablation, not the production model): train again with ALL spk02 data excluded (training_rows(..., exclude_speakers=["spk02"]) in kivi_real_common.py does it, and also drops needs_review takes) and evaluate on her test takes: that run says how the model treats a voice it has never heard. It is the only run in which she is held out; a held-out device (c3-b) contributes no training audio there either.
  • PC and webcam audio is train-only material (eval_channel false): it is not what the wake word hears. In a train or unassigned session these channels are tagged train-only; in a dev or test session they carry that split, so they cannot leak into training. Evaluation uses the satellite channel only (eval_channel true).
  • Negatives (negatives/) are split by device and by time; none from a session window or a held-out device may train in the ablation.

docs.title: If the model under test is the live wake word
docs.text: Pre-flight: kivi_session.py and kivi_extract.py read .storage/assist_pipeline.pipelines from the HA pod (read only) and print the preferred pipeline's wake word id; they warn loudly when it is kivi. As of 2026-11-07 the "Kiwi" pipeline uses alexa, so saying "kivi" does not close the wake file. If it did, the tools cope: a closed file that ends inside a cue window is a server detection (run_end_in_window, the clip ends at the file end), the audio after it is missing until the next run starts, and cues that no aligned audio covers are lost, shown as their own count and counted as misses in the denominators. Copies are cut by byte range to the session window plus or minus 60 s, through .part files with a checked byte count, and listed 01_stt-*.wav files of those runs are fetched too. Files whose alignment is not trusted are left out of the clips and the scores (flagged in the report; --include-unaligned overrides). The scorer streams each raw file from its sample 0 through pyopen-wakeword, the library inside the server (which includes its 8 s startup autofill), and maps the times through the alignment; the 2.1.0 handler (source in the work directory, src/wyoming-openwakeword) does not re-chunk: it resets the features and models on AudioStart and passes each converted AudioChunk straight to process_streaming, which is what the scorer does. Only the chunk size Home Assistant sends is unconfirmed (the scorer uses 1280 samples).

docs.title: Trade-offs and doubts
docs.text: The alignment confidence is a peak-to-sidelobe ratio of GCC-PHAT in 15 s windows; unrelated audio can look sharp in one window, so a source is trusted only when several windows agree on one offset line (small residual, plausible drift). The Postgres read (--button-takes without --presses-file) is a single SELECT DISTINCT of the button's state values through kubectl exec ... psql with default_transaction_read_only. Checked on 2026-11-07 against the cluster with read-only SELECTs: the defaults (home-assistant-postgres-0, container postgres, user postgres, database home_assistant) work, input_button.kivi_take exists in states_meta with state unknown (never pressed), and the query returns 0 presses. A real press has not been read yet.

docs.title: First real sessions and room audio (2026-11-07, observed on c3-a and c3-b)
docs.text:
Numbers only. Two sessions of one speaker (spk01) on c3-a, scored with the server's own runtime (kivi_score.py) on the uncalibrated v1 (final/, sha256 81e0827f...0511) and v2 (v2/final/, sha256 aeab0360...a627). Each model is read at its server-0.5 point (v1 raw 0.98, v2 raw 0.95, given as --calibration, not assumed) and at raw 0.9. Session 1 is split train, session 2 test (marks in splits.jsonl). One take is excluded per session because nothing was said: session 1 block 4 cue 5 (B4c5), session 2 block 4 cue 7 (B4c7; the desk mic and the webcam show no speech burst there). Scores used extraction revision (default) for session 1 (fixed time offset) and r2 for session 2 (desk-mic sample count, see below). "TV off" in the block names means the TV on and silent.

Session 1: what was lost and recovered. The live wake word (alexa) fired at 11:36:53Z and Home Assistant then ran 8 request-only runs (01_stt-*.wav, no wake file) until 11:38:57Z. kivi_extract.py now also takes request-only runs inside the session window, aligns each file on its own (PSR at least 15, and at least two files agreeing on the listing latency within 0.5 s), and marks the stage (stt). Of the 8 runs, 6 aligned (PSR 50 to 83; offsets within 0.64 s of the listed start); 2 did not (PSR 5.4 and 8.7) and stay out. Cue coverage of tv-c3a for 52 cues, counting the cue window of 4 s: before 40 full and 12 none; now 43 full, 8 partial (0.1 to 0.7 of the window), 1 none. Partial cues have audio but not the whole window (a run ends at the end of speech, gaps of 2 to 5 s between runs); clips are cut only for full windows (3 new cue clips, 2 new segments; 5 new manifest rows).

Session 2. 1 wake file spans the whole window, no request-only run and no live detection inside it (the live detection and the follow-up runs are at 12:26Z, after the session). Cue coverage: tv-c3a, pc-mic and webcam-mic 52 of 52 full. Takes present per source: 40 of 40 "kivi" and 12 of 12 near-words on each. Flagged takes (energy heuristics on the clips): 1 empty on pc-mic and webcam-mic (B4c7); 7 "multi-burst" on pc-mic, 12 on tv-c3a and 6 on webcam-mic (with the TV on, its content makes bursts); 12 clipped on webcam-mic (3 or more full-scale samples), 1 on tv-c3a, none on pc-mic; 1 digital-silence clip on pc-mic (the same B4c7 window, the desk mic gates to zero when quiet). The desk mic fell about 0.5 s behind the clock between about 600 s and 720 s, 0.7 s over the whole session (its recorded sample count; probably a dropout while the PC was busy, not verified), so a single offset line no longer fits tv-c3a or webcam-mic (residual 108 and 96 ms, all windows confident, PSR 30 and 12). kivi_extract.py now accepts a smooth offset curve when at least 80 % of the windows have a sharp peak, the offsets are continuous and the line fails (flagged piecewise; the unrelated-audio test still fails), and it maps session times to the desk-mic file by its sample count when the desk mic lost more than 0.3 s. The first extraction (revision "") used the old mapping: its 80 desk-mic rows are superseded (superseded.jsonl; audio kept) and skipped by read_manifest, training_rows and the scorers; the data is in revision r2.

tv-c3a recall on "kivi" (k/n), counting every cue as a trial (a cue without a full window of audio is a miss), and over full-audio cues only. Session 1 has 39 cues (B4c5 excluded), session 2 has 39 (B4c7 excluded).

docs.title: Decided training recipe (2026-11-07)
docs.text:
Evidence review: kivi-models repo, docs/research/kivi-training-evidence.md. Retraining follows this recipe:

  1. Server-exact features for training and evaluation (stream_mel.py, fast_eval.py embed --stream-onnx); no batch features.
  2. Real positives from household speakers on the TVs, post-front-end (the wake files are exactly what the wake word sees), plus the PC, webcam and phone takes as train-only extras.
  3. Interference augmentation: TV speech, music and household voices mixed in at 0-30 dB measured on the word, then passed through the front-end emulation. No stationary noise.
  4. Front-end emulation (120 Hz high-pass, AEC3 and noise suppression, +24 dB) applied to the training audio, so it matches what the satellites send.
  5. Real TV-room negatives (kivi_negatives.py) plus hard-negative mining on them.
  6. Keep room impulse response and level augmentation.
  7. Evaluation as the false-reject rate at 0.5 and at 0.1 false accepts per hour, with a DET curve, reported per speaker and per device. The test set is spk02's c3-b button takes (never trained on); the unseen-speaker ablation excludes all spk02 data from training.

docs.title: v2 (2026-11-07, candidate, not deployed)
docs.text: Status: candidate model files and an offline comparison with v1. Not deployed, no change in Home Assistant, the cluster or kivi-models. PC only; no TV, no microphone. All numbers are observed-offline on synthetic voices (Piper); real voices are still unmeasured. Recipe items 1, 3, 4 and 6 were applied; items 2 and 5 (real positives and real TV-room negatives) wait for the owner's sessions.

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
1. Server-exact features. Positives, adversarial negatives, mined hard negatives and the MLS Spanish speech negatives were recomputed with the server's chunking and per-chunk clamp (v2_augment.py, built on fast_eval.StreamFeatures). Two traps were found on the way, both in lessons learned: the old stream training window cut up to 100 ms of the word in about half of the positives, and v1's evaluation clips are padded with digital silence, which decides the comparison by itself.
  2. ACAV100M kept as batch features. Its audio is not available, so the gap was measured on proxy audio computed both ways (400 AudioSet and 400 MLS clips of 10 s at -30 to -1 dBFS peak, v2_acav_check.py). The median |embedding difference| was 0.27 (values reach ±43; the 99th percentile was 10.5, in quiet windows). v1's score changed by 0.005 on average, and its rates above 0.5 / 0.9 / 0.98 were 0.46 / 0.03 / 0 % in batch and 0.43 / 0.03 / 0 % in stream. A linear probe separated batch from stream windows of the same audio only at AUC 0.61. Removing ACAV made validation recall worse (10.8 % against 12.0 to 15.6 % at 4 dev false accepts), and so did 128 ACAV + 512 MLS per step (5.3 %).
  3. Interference, TV-like only: 964 AudioSet balanced-train clips (shards 00-03) with a music, singing, speech, conversation, TV, radio, laughter, applause or crowd label and none of 40 stationary-noise labels (v2_prep_bg.py), plus 1 500 x 10 s of MLS Spanish speech, about half and half. The SNR is measured on the word, and the interference runs through a 2 s lead before the window so the noise suppression has adapted. No white, pink or fan noise.
  4. Front-end emulation after mixing: the satellite's own chain, the aec_offline example of webos-voice-satellite (daemon file mode; v2_frontend.py). It applies the 120 Hz high-pass, sonora AEC3 with noise suppression (the shipped [aec] enabled = true, ns = true), +24 dB and saturating S16, at 166x real time per core, and the 224-sample latency is removed. The echo reference is silent, because synthetic mixes have none. AEC3 therefore passes the mix through, and the interference stands for sound that the canceller leaves, such as household voices or residual echo; NS still acts on it.
  5. Level and floor, calibrated on real satellite audio. Aggregates only, from the last 2.5 s of 24 closed wake-stage files that ended in a detection, plus 4 x 20 s from other files, both TVs (data register, row 12):
  6. loudest 0.5 s before the detection: median -21.5 dBFS RMS (IQR -26.5 to -20.6), peak median -7.4 dBFS, no clipping;
  7. quietest 80 ms frames: -74.6 to -49.9 dBFS (5th to 95th percentile).

Clips get a word level of N(-23, 5) dBFS (loudest 0.5 s) and a white mic floor of -62 to -48 dBFS before the front-end, which NS lowers by 13 dB into the measured range. Long evaluation audio is scaled to a 90th-percentile 80 ms RMS of -24 dBFS. 6. Kept from v1: RIR at p 0.5; the same 60 000 positives, the 57 103 adversarial clips without "aquí vi", and the same held-out voices; train_simple.py settings (layer 64, one-cycle, per step 256 positives, 512 ACAV, 128 MLS, 64 adversarial and 128 mined, weight 3). One mining round ran on 31 h of MLS train shard 1 through the front-end (27 618 windows). 7. Evaluation: fast_report.py on server-exact features of the held-out voices (clean, P2 TV content at 10 and 0 dB), the near-words and v1's false-accept test sets (16.9 h), all through the same level, floor and front-end. The threshold was picked on MLS dev through the front-end. v1's original zero-padded set is also reported, labelled as such.

docs.text:
18 heads on these features (plus 6 diagnostic heads on the earlier stream features), 1-6 min each on the GPU. They were ranked only on the training-voice validation positives (0-30 dB, p 0.8, through the front-end) at 4 / 8 / 16 false accepts on MLS dev through the front-end (v2_rank.py). The held-out voices were not used for the choice.

Variant Validation recall at 4 / 8 / 16 dev false accepts v1 (reference) 17.5 / 34.6 / 46.2 % From scratch, 0-30 dB, p 0.8 (3 seeds; layer 128 similar) 12.0-15.6 / 16.9-24.2 / 26.5-30.6 % From scratch, 5-30 dB, p 0.7 17.2 / 26.3 / 35.2 % From scratch, 10-30 dB, p 0.5 (3 seeds) 18.0-27.4 / 31.3-34.3 / 37.6-40.6 % v1 + v2 training data together 27.7 / 36.5 / 44.1 % v1 warm start, 0-30 dB data, 2 000 steps at 1e-4 21.8 / 33.2 / 46.4 % v1 warm start, 10-30 dB p 0.5 data, 2 000 steps at 1e-4 (3 seeds; 4 000 steps worse) 34.2-39.8 / 42.3-46.3 / 47.9-50.4 %

Chosen: the v1 warm start on 10-30 dB data, seed 1. Its threshold is 0.95, the highest threshold with at most 4 false accepts on MLS dev through the front-end (v1 had 4 at its 0.98 on the raw dev). It differs from the recipe in two ways:

  • SNR 10-30 dB at p 0.5 instead of 0-30 dB at p 0.8. With 0-30 dB, every from-scratch run was worse than v1 on validation. Harder interference made the model fire on plain speech.
  • Fine-tuned from v1 (2 000 steps, lr 1e-4) instead of trained from scratch. The best from-scratch run reached 27.4 % at 4 dev false accepts, and the warm start 39.8 %.

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text:
• At equal false accepts per hour, v2 has a much higher clean recall than v1 through the emulated front-end: +14 points at about 0.45/h and +26 points at about 1/h. With TV interference it is level with v1, within about ±3 points and inside the intervals. The interference augmentation did not buy noisy-TV recall here.
  • v2 accepts near-words more often at the same false-accept rate (5.7 % against 3.2 % at about 0.45/h, 11.4 % against 6.1 % at about 1/h).
  • v1 loses 15 points of clean recall when its input goes through the front-end and floor (60.2 % to 45.7 % at 0.98). The deployed model's real recall is probably closer to the front-end number (inferred, not measured on real voices).
  • The candidate is worth a real-voice A/B against v1 (the owner procedure above, kivi_score.py with v2/final/kivi_uncalibrated.onnx) before any deployment decision. If deployed at 0.95 (the calibrated file at 0.5), the offline false-accept estimate is 0.8/h [0.45, 1.4]. That is above v1's 0.47/h and far above the 0.1/h goal; 0.97 gives about v1's false-accept rate.
  • The cheapest next levers remain the recipe's items 2 and 5 (real positives, real TV-room negatives). A two-word phrase is the fallback if near-words and false accepts stay high.

docs.title: v3 (2026-11-07, candidate, not deployed)
docs.text: Status: candidate model files and a one-shot comparison with v1 and v2 on real audio. Not deployed, no change in Home Assistant, the cluster, the TVs or kivi-models. PC only. v3 adds the real data of the recipe (items 2 and 5): spk01's session-1 takes and the room negatives. Real numbers below are observed on c3-a, synthetic ones observed-offline. One speaker only.

docs.title: What changed against v2
docs.text:
1. Real positives (v3_real.py takes): every session-1 cue take of all three sources (training_rows(read_manifest(...)), split train / train-only; superseded rows, needs_review and B4c5 left out).
  2. Each take is re-cut from its raw file with 5 s before and 1 s after the word end. The cut uses the manifest row's window (start_s) and offset (align_offset_s), and is checked sample for sample against the stored clip (144 of 144 identical).
  3. The word end comes from the desk-mic energy burst (kivi_score.word_span_from_ref; median word 0.54 s). v2's score peaks a median 0.11 s after it (p10 -0.05, p90 0.43 s) on the 27 tv-c3a takes, inside the training jitter.
  4. 141 take-sources kept. 3 tv-c3a takes were dropped: their STT-stage files hold less than 5 s before the word. Only full-coverage cues have clips, so no partial cue is used.
  5. Validation hold-out: 10 of 51 takes (20 %, 2 per block, all sources of a take together, seed 2026). They stay out of the final model too; it was not retrained on them.
  6. Augmentation, 200 copies per take-source, word end -50 to +250 ms before the end of the window:
    • tv-c3a (already through the real front end): gain -6 to +6 dB, and TV-like interference at 10-30 dB on the word with p 0.4. The interference alone goes through the front-end emulation and is then added; the take gets no second front-end pass.
    • pc-mic and webcam-mic: RIR with p 0.5; level N(-23, 5) dBFS on the word; interference at 10-30 dB with p 0.5; the calibrated mic floor (-62 to -48 dBFS; the desk mic gates to digital zero); then the front-end emulation.
  7. Windows: "kivi" 4 200 tv (21 take-sources) and 12 400 desk (62); near-words 2 000 tv (10) and 4 000 desk (20).
  8. Ratio: per step 256 synthetic positives plus 48 tv and 48 desk real windows, so 27 % of the positives are real. Per take-source, a real take is drawn about 535 times (tv) and 180 times (desk) as often as one synthetic clip.
  9. Near-words (kivi_v3_near.yaml, gen_clips.py, Piper training voices):
  10. 40 000 training and 3 000 validation clips of 31 words and 10 short sentences, weighted toward the measured confusers (kili, kiri, Pipi, tivi and kiwi at 3; "aquí vi" at 2; quizá, Kiki, tipi, chivi, Vivi, Fifi, tevé, la tele, and other C-iβi / kˈi-C-i words at 0.5-2).
  11. 1 220 clips by the held-out voices for evaluation.
  12. The same interference (10-30 dB, p 0.5) and front end as the positives, so the noise level cannot predict the label.
  13. Real near-words: the session-1 near-word takes of all sources, augmented as above.
  14. Room negatives (v3_room.py split): per TV, ordered by start time and cut by duration into three parts:
Part c3-a c3-b Use train (first 50 %) 8.22 h 8.40 h training and mining sel (next 25 %) 4.11 h 4.20 h threshold selection test (latest 25 %) 4.11 h, from 2026-11-06 09:52Z 4.20 h, from 11:42Z final evaluation only

Server-exact features of the audio as recorded: no front end, level or floor. The train part gives 92 723 windows (every 8th frame, 128 per step) and 8 816 hard negatives (v2 score above 0.02, at most one per 0.4 s; 128 per step). No session window is in the negatives (kivi_negatives.py already removed them). 4. Warm start from v2: 2 000 steps, lr 1e-4, layer 64, the v2 batch (256 synthetic positives, 512 ACAV, 128 MLS, 64 v1 adversarial, 128 MLS hard; weight 3) plus the above. From scratch (6 000 steps) did worse on synthetic voices at the same room false accepts (24.9 % against 35.1 % clean) and the same on real takes (21/22 against 20/22). 5. Selection: the threshold is the lowest raw threshold with at most 2 false accepts on the selection room part (8.38 h scored, 0.24/h). It was never chosen on session 2 or on the test part. At that threshold, candidates were compared on: - the held-out synthetic voices (clean, 10 dB, 0 dB; both near-word sets); - the 10 held-out real takes.

Rule, fixed before round 3: keep candidates with at least 20/22 real held-out "kivi" and held-out-voice near-word acceptance no higher than v2's at the same false-accept rate (13.7 %); then take the highest mean synthetic recall.

Findings (observed-offline, selection data only):

  • Real positives are what moves the real takes: 2-5/22 without them, 20-22/22 with them.
  • The room negatives do not cost synthetic recall. With the rest fixed, clean recall was 24.7 % without room data, 24.9 % with the room windows, 29.7 % with the room hard negatives and 35.1 % with both.
  • The synthetic near-words cost the synthetic voices' recall: 75 % clean without them, 44 % at weight 3, 35 % at weight 6, 27 % at weight 10. Real near-word discrimination barely changed (3/6 held out at every weight).
  • Seeds of one configuration differ by up to 7.5 points of clean recall, mostly through the threshold, which rests on the 3rd-highest room peak.
  • Choice: by the rule, weight 1 / real 15 fails the near-word bound (14.4 %). Synthetic near weight 2 (44.1 / 21.6 / 9.1 %), weight 3 (43.6 / 21.5 / 9.3 %) and weight 3 with real near-words at 15 (44.0 / 21.1 / 8.7 %) are equal within the seed spread. The tie went to the last: 22/22 real held-out and the lowest near-word acceptance.

docs.title: Deviations from the brief, with the evidence
docs.text:
• "kibi" is not a near-word. Spanish espeak gives kˈiβi for "kivi", "quivi" and "kibi" (checked 2026-11-07; also noted in kivi_data.yaml), and the positives use kˈibi on purpose. "TV" is read as letters by espeak (tˌeˈuβe), so "tevé" and "la tele" stand for it.
  • The synthetic near-word weight is 3, not "high". At weight 6 or 10 the held-out synthetic voices lost 9 to 17 more points of clean recall for no gain on the real near-words. The real near-words carry the high weight instead (15, 64 + 64 per step).
  • tv-c3a interference is added after the front end (the interference alone goes through the emulation) rather than passing the take through a second front end.
  • The final model is the validated one. It was not retrained with the 20 % hold-out.
  • Synthetic held-out voices were used for selection, as instructed, so the synthetic numbers below are not independent of the choice.

docs.title: Gate verdict
docs.text:
Gate v3 Verdict Recall with the TV silent, at least 80 % 17/20 = 85 % [64, 95] met on the point estimate Recall with the TV on, at least 60 % 16/19 = 84 % [62, 94] met on the point estimate At most 1 false wake per evening (about 0.25/h) 2 in 8.31 h = 0.24/h [0.03, 0.87] met on the point estimate

v3 passes the gate on point estimates. The intervals do not prove it: the TV-silent lower bound is 64 %, and the false-accept upper bound is 0.87/h, about 3.5 per 4 h evening. The weakest block is still 3 m with the TV silent (7/10). Near-words on the TV channel did not improve (7/12; "tivi" 2/2).

What this test is and is not:

  • It covers one speaker, spk01, who is also the training speaker.
  • Session 2 is one other recording of the same person, the same TV (c3-a) and the same day.
  • On held-out synthetic voices, v3 is level with v1 and well below v2 (44 % against 78 % clean). It has become a better detector of spk01 on this TV, not of voices in general. Other household voices are likely to do worse than spk01 (inferred).
  • spk02's c3-b button takes (test split, never trained on) are the next decisive measurement, with the unseen-speaker ablation of the split policy.

Data caveat: the room negatives (2026-11-05 17:18Z to 2026-11-06 20:37Z) were mostly recorded while kivi v1 was the live wake word (deployed about 2026-11-05 20:16Z).

  • A real "kivi" that v1 missed would sit unlabelled in the negatives. Without listening this cannot be checked.
  • A test-part "false accept" could then be a correct detection, so the reported rate is conservative, not optimistic.
  • The ablation above showed no recall cost from training on the room data.

docs.title: spk02 c3-b button takes (2026-11-07, observed-offline, test split only)
docs.text:
Consent: relayed by the owner on 2026-11-07 (recorded in dataset 9 of the data register). These takes are test and are never trained on. Nothing was listened to or transcribed; the numbers below are counts, levels and scores.

Presses. input_button.kivi_take has 23 presses since it was created (the helper was loaded at 10:39Z; the recorder holds no earlier press): all between 14:11:54Z and 14:13:54Z on 2026-11-07, none before, none during the c3-a sessions (the two unknown states at 10:39Z and 12:27Z are the entity being loaded and restored, not presses). Two pairs are 0.8 s apart (double presses of one take), so there are 21 takes. Gaps between consecutive takes: 2.2 to 18 s (median 3.5 s). Three clusters, split at gaps over 12 s: A 3 takes, B 3 takes, C 15 takes.

Coverage. All 23 presses lie inside one closed c3-b wake file (14:11:21Z to 14:15:11Z, 7.36 MB, 230 s, first press 33 s in): 21 of 21 takes have full audio, none partial, none missing. Speech energy in the 5 s before the press (window start at the previous take's press when that is closer): 20 of 21 takes have RMS 28 to 43 dB and peak 40 to 55 dB above the floor (the floor is -71.6 dBFS, the 20th percentile of 20 ms frames over the press span; peaks -31 to -16 dBFS). One take (the second of cluster A) has RMS 3.5 dB and peak 15 dB above the floor: no speech. The wake file closed at 14:15:11.7Z, 78 s after the last press, with a 1.1 s request-audio file (a server-side wake detection of the live word alexa, not related to a take). Offline alexa on the same file: peak score 0.43, no detection above 0.5 in the take span. A second wake file started at 14:15:25Z and holds no press.

The extraction tool and this protocol do not match. kivi_extract.py --button-takes looks for the word 0 to 6 s after a press. These takes were spoken before the press (the model scores peak a median 1.4 s before it). With presses 3.5 s apart the tool therefore cut the next take's word: 20 clips from 23 presses, 3 presses with no clear onset, 16 clips flagged needs_review (set to unassigned), 4 clips in test, and 6 pairs of clips that cut the same burst twice (median onset 2.1 s after the press). Do not use those clips; they are in datasets/real/button-20261107T141100Z-spk02-tv-c3b/ and have since been marked superseded (revision ""; audio kept). The extractor was fixed the same day (say-then-press window, default), see the re-extraction below. The scores below do not use them: the stored raw wake file was streamed once through pyopen-wakeword (the server's runtime) and each take's score is the maximum of the model's output between max(press - 4 s, previous press) and press + 1 s (the 1 s is the file-time uncertainty, +-1 s).

Re-extraction (say-then-press, revision stp3, 2026-11-07, observed-offline). kivi_extract.py --button-takes now defaults to the owner's order (say, then press): 23 presses are 21 takes (2 double presses merged). The word is the energy-burst span before the press in max(press - 4 s, previous take's last press + 0.3 s) to press + 1 s. Result: 19 clips cut (median speech onset 2.7 s before the press), 2 takes without a usable burst (no burst shorter than 2.5 s above the file floor inside the window), 11 clean clips and 8 flagged needs_review (a span over 2.5 s, or speech that only starts after the press). Earlier tries with a context floor cut 17 and 10 clips (revisions r2, stp1, stp2); all of them and the press-then-say rows are marked superseded, audio kept. Owner decision the same day: these takes are train (session mark in splits.jsonl), not test; needs_review takes stay out of training. The one take known to hold no speech (the second of cluster A) still produced a 0.2 s noise burst, so its clip is marked excluded (excluded.jsonl, kivi_dataset_marks.py exclude); training_rows skips excluded rows, leaving 10 clean clips usable for training. Energy only: nothing was listened to.

Check of the scores with the new extraction record (kivi_score.py --button-takes, 21 takes, the extractor's window, the no-speech take counted as a miss): server-0.5 point v1 5/21 (earlier 6/21), v2 10/21 (earlier 9/21), v3 5/21 (earlier 4/21); raw 0.9 v1 14/21, v2 11/21, v3 2/21 (identical to the earlier figures). Each model differs by one take at its server-0.5 point only. Hypothesis, not tested: the windows differ slightly (the new one starts 0.3 s after the previous take's last press, the earlier one at the previous press), and these takes sit close to the threshold. Without the excluded take (n 20): 5, 10 and 5 hits.

Recall, uncalibrated models, window before the press (Wilson 95 % interval; raw threshold in brackets):

Model Server-0.5 point Pooled (n 21) Cluster A (3) Cluster B (3) Cluster C (15) Raw 0.9, pooled Median of max scores v1 raw 0.98 6/21 = 0.29 [0.14, 0.50] 1/3 [0.06, 0.79] 1/3 [0.06, 0.79] 4/15 [0.11, 0.52] 14/21 = 0.67 [0.45, 0.83] 0.94 v2 raw 0.95 9/21 = 0.43 [0.25, 0.64] 1/3 [0.06, 0.79] 1/3 [0.06, 0.79] 7/15 [0.25, 0.70] 11/21 = 0.52 [0.32, 0.72] 0.94 v3 raw 0.8653 4/21 = 0.19 [0.08, 0.40] 1/3 [0.06, 0.79] 1/3 [0.06, 0.79] 2/15 [0.04, 0.38] 2/21 = 0.10 [0.03, 0.29] 0.71

Per cluster at raw 0.9: v1 1/3, 3/3, 10/15; v2 1/3, 2/3, 8/15; v3 0/3, 1/3, 1/15. Sensitivity to the window (pooled, server-0.5 point): from press - 4 s to press + 1 s without the previous-press limit: v1 7/21, v2 10/21, v3 6/21; the tool's after-press window (press - 1 s to press + 7 s, which reaches the next take): v1 8/21, v2 11/21, v3 7/21. The no-speech take counts as a miss in every figure (without it, n is 20). The clusters are not independent samples of the voice (one speaker, one session, 2 minutes), and the intervals are wide. These are the same models that scored higher on the spk01 and synthetic sets; on this speaker the v3 server-0.5 point (chosen for a false-accept budget) recovers fewer takes than v1 and v2 at theirs.

docs.title: v5 (2026-11-07, candidate, not deployed)
docs.text:
Status: candidate model files, a one-shot comparison with v1, v2 and v3, and a leave-spk02-out ablation. Not deployed; no change in Home Assistant, the cluster, the TVs or kivi-models. PC only. Real numbers are observed on c3-a and c3-b, synthetic ones observed-offline. Nothing was listened to, transcribed or printed. Verdict: v5 does not meet its goal. At its false-accept point it is level with v3 on synthetic voices (+5 points on quiet speech) and below v3 on spk01. On spk02 it is 2/4, which is too few takes to rank anything.

Why. v3 fitted spk01: 33/39 on spk01's session 2, but 44 % on held-out synthetic voices (v2: 78 %) and 5/21 on spk02's c3-b button takes. v5 adds spk02's real takes and aims at household voices in general: synthetic held-out recall close to v2's while gaining on both real speakers.

docs.title: What changed against v3
docs.text:
1. spk02's real takes (v5_buttons.py, revision stp3, tv-c3b only):
  2. 10 clean takes: training_rows, take 2 excluded (no speech). The word end is the row's clip minus the 1 s pad; a fresh energy-burst span agrees on all 10.
  3. 3 extra takes cut from the raw wake file, labelled separately (s2x). They were picked from the 8 needs_review takes and the 2 without a clip. The window is max(press - 4 s, previous take's last press + 0.3 s) to the last press + 1 s; bursts are measured against the file's 10th-percentile 20 ms floor. A burst had to start before the press. Rule 1 (first to last such burst, at most 2.5 s) kept none. Rule 2 (the last burst before the press alone, at most 1.2 s) kept takes 5, 11 and 14. Dropped: takes 1, 4 and 16 (speech only after the press), 6 and 21 (span too long), 9 and 19 (no burst).
  4. Hold-out: 4 of the 10 clean takes (seed 2026, by take: 3, 7, 13, 15). That leaves 6 clean and 3 extra takes for training. spk01's split is as in v3 (10 of 51 takes held out).
  5. Augmentation as v3's tv takes, 600 copies per take.
  6. Speakers balanced: per step, spk01 gets 32 real positives (16 tv-c3a, 16 desk sources) and spk02 gets 32 (22 clean, 10 extra).
  7. Real share lowered from 27 % (v3) to 17 %: 64 real positives against 256 synthetic and 64 quiet synthetic. Tuned on validation in round 1 (below).
  8. Level widened down to quiet speech.
  9. Measured on the TV channel (v5/levels.py, numbers only), as the loudest 0.5 s RMS, which is the unit of v2_augment.py --level-db (post-gain, the level after the front end): spk02's 20 speech takes are -35.1 to -17.1 dBFS (median -30.3; sample peaks -20.8 to -3.1). spk01's tv-c3a takes are -28.5 to -19.3 (median -23.7).
  10. The old level, N(-23, 5) dBFS, reaches spk02's 25th percentile in about 3 % of draws.
  11. Added: 20 000 quiet synthetic positives and 12 000 quiet synthetic near-words, at uniform -45 to -28 dBFS (--level-db u:-45,-28, new). -45 dBFS RMS is about -31 dBFS sample peak, close to the brief's "about -35 dBFS peak".
  12. Real tv takes of both speakers get -12 to +6 dB of gain (v3: ±6). spk01's desk takes get N(-27, 7).
  13. Warm start from v2 (2 000 steps, lr 1e-4, layer 64, the v3 batch otherwise). Validation said v2: the v3 warm start lost 8 points of synthetic clean recall at equal room false accepts (35.9 against 43.6 %).
  14. Validation (selection only):
  15. Each model's threshold for at most 2 false accepts on the room selection part (8.38 h, 0.24/h).
  16. Held-out synthetic voices: clean, TV at 10 and 0 dB, and a new quiet set (the same 1 800 clips at -35 dBFS, spk02's quietest take).
  17. Synthetic near-words: the v1 set, the v3 set and a quiet copy of the v3 set.
  18. Real held-out takes: spk01's 10 (6 "kivi" on tv-c3a) and spk02's 4.
  19. The room test part and spk01's session 2 were not used for any choice.

At each model's own threshold for at most 2 false accepts in 8.38 h of the room selection part. "spk01 tv" is spk01's held-out "kivi" takes on tv-c3a (6); "spk02" is the 4 held-out takes (features path, v3_select.py).

Findings (validation only):

  • The real share moves the real takes: with none, 0/6 and 0/4; at 9 %, 4/6 and 1/4; at 17 %, 5/6 and 2/4. At 23 %, synthetic recall drops. The evidence review's 5-10 % was too low for spk02 here.
  • Seeds dominate. One configuration ranges over 20 points of synthetic clean recall across 3 seeds. The threshold rests on the third-highest room peak in 8.4 h. Synthetic recall and near-word acceptance rise together, so seeds mostly change the operating point, not how well the model separates.
  • Synthetic near-words are the main cost to synthetic recall, as in v3. At near-word weight 1, or with none, synthetic recall reaches or passes v2 at the same room budget (59-66 % clean against 54 %), but near-word acceptance rises to 19-23 % (v2 13.7 %).
  • spk02's extra takes made no difference on held-out takes: 2/4 with and without them at every seed.
  • Rule, fixed before round 2: keep candidates with spk01 tv at least 5/6, spk02 at least 2/4 and v3-set near-words no higher than v2's 13.7 %; then take the highest mean synthetic recall (clean, 10 dB, 0 dB, quiet). Passing: extras + near weight 3, seed 3 (mean 29.5); without extras, near weight 1, seed 1 (29.3); the averaged model with extras (28.8). These are equal within the seed spread. Chosen by the rule: x_sn3_s3, raw 0.89283. It does not reach v2's synthetic recall at equal false accepts (45.6 against 54.2 % clean).
  • Not tested on the test data: soup_nox_sn1 (weight average, near weight 1). On validation it meets the brief's criterion on synthetic and real voices (63.9 % clean, 54.8 % quiet, 6/6 and 2/4), but it accepts more near-words (21.3 % against v2's 13.7 % at the same budget). It is kept in v5/alt/ to score on spk02's fresh test takes. That set is new data, so it can decide between the two without reusing a test.

docs.title: Final evaluation (one shot)
docs.text:
v5/final.sh, run once after the choice:

  • spk01's session 2 through kivi_score.py (B4c7 excluded).

docs.text:
The chosen recipe without any spk02 draws, seeds 1-3, each at its own room-selection threshold (0.872, 0.866, 0.866). Scored with the server runtime (kivi_score.py --button-takes). These models never saw spk02, so all 20 of her speech takes are unseen (take 2 has no speech).

Model spk02, 4 held-out takes spk02, all 20 speech takes Median max score (21 takes) Synthetic clean (validation) without spk02, seeds 1 / 2 / 3 0/4, 0/4, 0/4 2/20, 2/20, 2/20 0.66 / 0.64 / 0.66 46.9 / 49.3 / 51.0 % v5 (with spk02) 2/4 not a test (trained on 9 of them) 0.96 45.6 % v1 / v2 / v3 (never saw spk02) 3/4, 3/4, 1/4 5/20, 10/20, 5/20 0.95 / 0.94 / 0.71 46.6 / 54.2 / 44.0 %
  • spk02's takes are what move spk02, at a small cost in synthetic recall.
  • The recipe does not generalise to an unseen speaker at this false-accept budget. Without her takes it gets 2/20, below v1 and v2. Training on spk01, the room negatives and the near-words makes the model stricter on unknown voices than v1 or v2 were. Inferred: a third household voice will do about as badly unless its takes are added.
  • spk02's 3 extra takes: no effect on her held-out takes (2/4 with and without at 3 seeds, validation path).

docs.title: Deviations from the brief, with the evidence
docs.text:
• Real share 17 %, not lower. 9 % lost spk01 (4/6) and spk02 (1/4) on validation, with the same synthetic recall.
  • The success criterion is not met under the near-word rule fixed before round 2. Dropping that rule meets it on validation (soup_nox_sn1), at about twice v2's near-word rate at equal false accepts. This is the owner's call.
  • "-35 dBFS peak" was read in the augmentation's own unit (loudest 0.5 s RMS): -45 to -28 dBFS RMS covers spk02's quietest take (-35.1) with 10 dB of margin.
  • Selection was by validation, not retrained: the final model is the validated one; the hold-out takes were not added back.

docs.title: Scoring the fresh spk02 test takes
docs.text:
After kivi_extract.py --button-takes --device c3-b --speaker spk02 --split test --since ... --until ... (say, then press), one command from /work/workspaces/kivi-wakeword gives recall per model at its server-0.5 point and at the default thresholds. Add --exclude-take N for a take with no speech; the reports go into the session's scores/ directory:

systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=12G -p CPUQuota=800% nice -n 10 .venv/bin/python -I \
  ~/homelab/scripts/voice-assistant/wakeword/kivi_score.py --button-takes datasets/real/<new button session> \
  --model v1=final/kivi_uncalibrated.tflite --model v2=v2/final/kivi_uncalibrated.tflite \
  --model v3=v3/final/kivi_uncalibrated.tflite --model v5=v5/final/kivi_uncalibrated.tflite \
  --model v5alt=v5/alt/soup_nox_sn1/kivi_uncalibrated.tflite \

docs.title: v4: "oye Kivi" (2026-11-07, candidate, not deployed)
docs.text:
Status: candidate model files for the new wake phrase "oye Kivi" and a one-shot evaluation. Not deployed; no change in Home Assistant, the cluster, the TVs or the kivi-models tags. PC only. Nothing was listened to, transcribed or printed. Real "oye Kivi" recall is untested: no real "oye Kivi" takes exist yet. The real audio below only tests what must not wake the model ("Kivi" alone, near-words, room audio).

Why. On 2026-11-07 the owner switched the household wake phrase from "Kivi" to "oye Kivi" (kivi-models docs/plan/2026-11-fallback-wake-phrase.md, in progress in parallel with Kivi v5): - v2 got 21/39 on spk01 and 9/21 on spk02. - v3 got 33/39 on spk01, but only 4/21 on spk02 and 44 % on held-out synthetic voices. - "kili", "kiri", "pipi" and "tivi" score as high as "kivi".

docs.title: Method
docs.text:
1. Synthetic positives (v4_gen.py, v4_oye_kivi.yaml): 59 969 training and 3 000 validation clips from 32 voice groups (31 Piper models).
  2. Voices: the four native Spanish voices first (weight 2 each), plus LibriTTS-R, VCTK, L2-ARCTIC (non-native English accents), ARCTIC, ARU, SEMAINE, Basque, Catalan, Italian, Portuguese (PT, BR), Romanian, German (Thorsten emotional) and single English and French voices, all fed Spanish phonemes.
  3. Each clip is "oye" + joiner + "kivi" + ending:
    • "oye" variants: ˈoʝe 55 %, ˈoje 18 %, ˈoʒe 8 %, ˈoʃe 4 %, ˈoʎe 5 %, and "oiga" (ˈoɪɣa) 10 %;
    • "kivi" variants: as v1-v3;
    • joiner: space 50 %, comma 20 %, run together 10 %, or two renderings with a gap of 80-450 ms 20 %.
  4. Speed (length scale 0.75-1.35), Piper noise scales, and with p 0.5 a resampling warp of ±10 % (pitch, formants and tempo together).
  5. Durations: median 0.84 s, p95 1.8 s.
  6. Held-out voices (evaluation only): the v1-v3 set (es_MX claude, es_AR daniela, es_ES carlfm, LibriTTS-R 800-903, VCTK 90-108) plus eu_ES maider and L2-ARCTIC speakers 18-23. 2 216 "oye Kivi" clips and 2 862 near-phrase clips (46 phrases and 16 sentences, about 46 clips each).
  7. Near-phrases (59 982 training and 2 999 validation clips by the training voices):
  8. "Kivi" alone (with the positives' "kivi" variants, weight 8), "oye kili / kiri / tivi / pipi / chivi / Fifi / Vivi / Kiki / ...", "oye", "oye tú", "oye mira", "hoy vi", "o sea", "y Kivi", "ve Kivi", "que / mi / el / ojo / fue Kivi", "oiga", and 16 short sentences such as "Kivi, enciende la luz" and "oye, ¿qué hora es?" (full list and weights in the YAML).
  9. Same interference, level and front-end as the positives, so the level cannot predict the label.
  10. Augmentation, as v2/v3 (v4_augment.py = v2_augment.py plus a quiet branch):
  11. TV-like interference (AudioSet TV/music/speech and MLS speech, no stationary noise) at 10-30 dB on the word with p 0.5; RIR p 0.5; calibrated mic floor; the satellite front end (HPF, AEC3 + NS, +24 dB, S16); server-exact features.
  12. Level: the word's loudest 0.5 s RMS is N(-23, 5) dBFS, or with p 0.3 uniform in -46 to -30 dBFS. Post-front-end word peaks of the validation positives: p1 -34.5, p5 -31.1, median -13.4, p95 -2.5 dBFS. So the training covers spk02's measured -31 to -16 dBFS and reaches about -35 dBFS.
  13. Real negatives (v4_realneg.py): negative_rows_for_phrase(read_manifest(...), "oye kivi") at 1cf33e371. Superseded rows are skipped and the test session never enters.
  14. spk01 session 1: all three sources; 111 "kivi", 36 near-word and 87 background-segment clips.
  15. spk02's c3-b button takes, revision stp3: 10 clean takes plus the 8 needs_review takes. For another phrase a loose cut is still a valid negative.
  16. 30 augmented copies per take (6 per segment). tv sources get a gain of -12 to +6 dB and interference through the front-end emulation; desk sources get RIR, level, floor and the front end.
  17. Every window ending inside the clip, stride 2: 88 800 "kivi", 24 840 near-word and 3 576 background windows.
  18. spk01's session 2 is not in training: it is the false-trigger test below. spk02's takes are now training data (owner, 2026-11-07); fresh spk02 takes come later. So the spk02 figure below is a fit check, not a held-out result.
  19. Room audio, v3's time split per TV:
  20. train part: v3's windows and v3's v2-mined hard negatives;
  21. plus hard negatives mined with an early v4 head (ws_v2_6k, score above 0.02, at most one per 0.4 s): 1 254 room windows and 5 033 MLS shard-1 windows through the front end;
  22. sel part: the threshold;
  23. test part: the final evaluation only.
  24. General negatives as v2/v3: ACAV100M 512 per step, MLS train 0 windows 128, v2's MLS hard negatives 128.

docs.title: Candidates and selection
docs.text:
20 heads in 3 rounds (train_simple.py, layer 64 unless noted, about 1 min each on the GPU). The rule was written down before round 2 (v4/results/selection_rule.txt): 1. Threshold: the lowest raw threshold with at most 2 false accepts in the 8.38 h room selection part (0.24/h). 2. Eligible: a validation "Kivi"-alone acceptance of at most 2 % and a validation near-phrase acceptance of at most 1 %. 3. Choice: the highest validation recall.

Validation means the training voices' held-back windows, so the held-out voices did not enter the choice (unlike v3).

Findings (selection data only): - The warm start from the "kivi" v2 head beats training from scratch. At the same room budget, validation recall was 37-39 % against 22-29 %. - Short warm starts stay a "kivi" detector. At 2 000 steps "Kivi" alone passed 3.8 % of validation; at 3 000-4 000 steps with v4's real and synthetic "kivi" negatives it fell to 0.5-1.9 %. - Without the real "kivi" takes, "Kivi" alone stays higher (0.95 % of validation, 1/46 held out) at equal room false accepts. - The threshold is the noisy part, as in v3: it rests on the third-highest room peak, and the seeds of one recipe span up to 8 points of validation recall.

Chosen: m_ws4k_s2, raw threshold 0.9437. It is the v2 warm start, 4 000 steps, one-cycle lr 2e-4, seed 2. Per step: 256 synthetic positives, 128 synthetic near-phrases, 512 ACAV, 128 MLS, 128 v2 MLS hard, 128 room train, 64 v3 room hard, 128 v4 room hard, 128 v4 MLS hard, and real negatives (64 "kivi" at weight 6, 32 near-word at 6, 32 background); the other negatives at weight 3. m_ws4k_k12_a192 (38.7 %) was within a point but tied on validation near-phrases (0.73 %), so the higher recall stayed.

docs.title: Verdict and interpretation
docs.text:
• "Kivi" alone does not wake v4 in real audio: 0/39 on every source of spk01's held-out session 2, at every threshold from raw 0.5 up, and 0/21 on spk02's (trained-on) takes. The real near-words of session 2 pass 0-1 of 12. On synthetic held-out voices "Kivi" alone still passes 3/46, and "fue / ojo / el / que / mi Kivi" pass 22-45 %. A word ending in a vowel before "Kivi" is the main synthetic confuser.
  • Room false accepts miss the ≤ 0.25/h target on the test part:
  • 0.96/h [0.42, 1.90] pooled, against 0.24/h on the selection part at the same threshold.
  • c3-b carries 6 of the 8.
  • v2 showed the same shift from selection to test (the test part is daytime 2026-11-06).
  • The DET table puts the target near raw 0.98 (1 false accept, 0.12/h [0.00, 0.67]). There the synthetic recall is 57.5 % clean, 30.8 % at 10 dB and 42.3 % quiet.
  • The threshold was not moved after seeing the test part. Choosing 0.98 would need a new selection rule (for example, more room selection hours) or the owner's decision.
  • Synthetic recall is higher than v3's "kivi" at the same selection budget (at most 2 false accepts on the room selection part): 72.8 % against 44.0 % clean, 47.2 % against 21.1 % at 10 dB. The phrases and held-out sets differ, so this is indicative only, and v4's test-part false accepts are 4 times v3's. Quiet speech holds 61.8 %. The weakest held-out voice is es_AR daniela (42 % clean, 28 % quiet). Synthetic numbers say little about real voices (microWakeWord's warning, in the evidence review).
  • Next: record real "oye Kivi" sessions (one train and one test session for spk01, and fresh c3-b button takes for spk02, kivi_session.py --phrase "oye kivi"). Then re-select on more room hours, then apply the gate. Do not deploy before that.

docs.title: Deviations from the brief, with the evidence
docs.text:
• Phrases left out of the near-phrases:
  • "oye kibi" and "oye quivi" phonemize to the target ˈoʝe kˈiβi.
  • v4_gen.py check measures DTW on log-mel of deterministic renderings (62 per phrase), as a ratio to two renderings of the target. On that scale the target's own variants score 6.0-7.8. "oye quiví" (5.7, stress shift only) and "hoy Kivi" (6.8) fall inside that range.
  • "oye kiri" scored 5.4 with 14 % of renderings below 1.5. It is in the brief, so it stays, at weight 1.5 instead of 3. It is also the top synthetic confuser (25/46).
  • "oye kiwi" (the pipeline is called "Kiwi") and "ey / hey Kivi" (the alternative phrase) are neither positive nor negative.
  • Voices left out:
  • fr_FR-mls, de_DE-mls, nl_NL-mls and en_US-norman babble on this phrase: 38 / 5 / 0 / 27 % of clips dropped by the length check, and 20 / 24 / 10 / 3 % of the kept clips with 4 or more energy bursts, against 0 % for the kept voices.
  • Their already-generated held-out rows (fr_mls 100-124) were removed from the manifests, so the held-out set has 7 voice groups, not 8.
  • en_US-lessac, fr_FR-tom, en_US-amy and en_GB-jenny_dioco were not used because of unclear licence terms.
  • No held-out spk02 subset: her takes became training data for Kivi v5 (owner, 2026-11-07), and fresh takes come later. spk02's needs_review rows of stp3 were added to the negatives (see Method, item 5).
  • Warm start from v2, because it validated better (37-39 % against 22-29 % from scratch). Not from v3.
  • The quiet held-out set uses a loudest-0.5 s RMS of N(-42, 2) dBFS. That gives post-front-end peaks of -33 to -25 dBFS, the lower half of spk02's measured range.
  • The first feature job failed on --level-db -42,2: argparse read the value as an option. It was rerun with --level-db=-42,2 (feats2.sh). The three sets already written were kept.

docs.title: Alternatives if the owner test fails
docs.text:
• Retrain on server-exact features (see Pitfalls, item 1). This is the cheapest next step: the scripts exist, about 1 h on the PC.
  • Add real positives: 50 to 100 "Kivi" takes per household member, recorded by the owner. They would stay local and never be committed; recording needs the owner's opt-in and consent.
  • A two-word phrase ("oye Kivi", "hola Kivi"): longer, so likely far fewer false wakes from running Spanish (hypothesis).
  • Keep alexa, which is the rollback anyway.
